doan gay ton kem va nguon thu hai co the tang quy mo. logic tuong tu ap dung cho hang y te, chip, thuc pham hay thiet bi nang luong. sang loc rui ro can phan biet kiem soat xuat khau co chu dich voi cu soc thuong mai thong thuong roi danh gia tung kich ban. moving production can require new plants, training, infrastructure and supplier certification. if the new location has higher costs or less productivity, buyers and consumers may pay more. smaller economies that are not treated as strategic partners can lose investment, even if they offer competitive capacity. friend-shoring criteria can also change after elections, so businesses face policy uncertainty. world bank analysis has cautioned that fragmentation and reshoring can reduce global income; the precise effect depends on the degree of separation and available alternatives. chuyen san xuat doi hoi nha may moi, dao tao, ha tang va chung nhan nha cung cap. neu dia diem moi ton kem hon hoac nang suat thap hon, nguoi mua va tieu dung co the tra them. nen kinh te nho khong duoc xem la doi tac chien luoc co the mat dau tu du co nang luc canh tranh. tieu chi friend-shoring cung co the doi sau bau cu, khien doanh nghiep bat dinh chinh sach. phan tich world bank canh bao phan manh va dua san xuat ve nuoc co the giam thu nhap toan cau; tac dong chinh xac tuy muc tach roi va phuong an thay the. geographic diversification spreads exposure across places without necessarily choosing suppliers based on political alignment. near-shoring prioritizes proximity; reshoring moves activity home. friend-shoring prioritizes trust or geopolitical ties. a robust strategy can use several approaches, but each has different costs. for example, a manufacturer might keep a primary source in one country, qualify two alternatives in separate regions and hold a modest emergency stock. that portfolio may improve resilience more reliably than transferring all production to one “friendly” location. da dang hoa dia ly phan tan phoi nhiem qua nhieu noi ma khong nhat thiet chon nha cung cap dua tren lien ket chinh tri. near-shoring uu tien gan; reshoring dua hoat dong ve trong nuoc; friend-shoring uu tien niem tin hay quan he dia chinh tri. chien luoc vung co the phoi hop nhieu cach, moi cach co chi phi rieng. chang han nha san xuat giu nguon chinh o mot nuoc, tham dinh hai nguon thay the o vung khac va duy tri ton kho khan cap vua phai. danh muc do co the tang kha nang chong chiu hon chuyen toan bo san xuat den mot noi “than thien”. a government can use subsidies, procurement preferences, export controls or investment screening to shape where firms locate. those tools may advance security goals, yet they can conflict with trade commitments or provoke retaliation. transparent, narrow criteria make policy easier to review. an emergency restriction should identify the threat, the affected input, the duration and the process for reassessment. otherwise, temporary security measures can become permanent protection for favored firms, raising costs and weakening competition without reducing the original vulnerability. chinh phu co the dung tro cap, uu tien mua sam, kiem soat xuat khau hay ra soat dau tu de dinh huong dia diem doanh nghiep. cong cu co the phuc vu an ninh, nhung cung xung dot cam ket thuong mai hoac gay tra dua. tieu chi minh bach, hep giup chinh sach de ra soat. han che khan cap can xac dinh de doa, dau vao lien quan, thoi han va quy trinh xem xet lai. neu khong, bien phap an ninh tam thoi co the thanh bao ho vinh vien cho doanh nghiep duoc uu ai, lam tang gia va giam canh tranh ma khong xu ly duoc diem de ton thuong ban dau. for a proposed friend-shoring project, ask what exact disruption it addresses, how concentrated the current source is, how quickly alternatives could supply the input and what the relocation costs. include worker skills, transport, energy, environmental standards and local suppliers. compare the plan with diversified sourcing, recycling, inventory or redesigning the product. as of 2024–25, official reports increasingly discussed trade diversification as a resilience tool, while warning that broad fragmentation can be costly. a policy should be measured by continuity and social outcomes, not by the number of factories moved. voi du an friend-shoring duoc de xuat, hay hoi no xu ly gian doan cu the nao, nguon hien tai tap trung ra sao, nguon thay the cung ung nhanh den dau va chi phi chuyen dia diem la gi. tinh ca ky nang lao dong, van tai, nang luong, tieu chuan moi truong va nha cung cap dia phuong. so sanh voi tim nguon da dang, tai che, ton kho hay thiet ke lai san pham. tinh den 2024–2025, bao cao chinh thuc ngay cang ban da dang hoa thuong mai nhu cong cu chong chiu, dong thoi canh bao phan manh rong gay ton kem. hay do chinh sach qua tinh lien tuc va ket qua xa hoi, khong phai so nha may duoc di chuyen.
tariff-pass-through: thue quan truyen vao gia nhu the nao va ai thuc su ganh chi phi? how tariffs pass through to prices thue nhap khau duoc thu tai bien gioi, nhung ganh nang kinh te co the chia giua nha nhap khau, nha cung cap, doanh nghiep ha nguon va nguoi tieu dung. nghien cuu imf ve dot tang thue my 2025 cho thay can tach gia nhap khau truoc thue, gia sau thue va thay doi nguon hang. a tariff is a tax on imported goods, usually paid to customs by the importer of record. that legal payer is not necessarily the party that bears the full economic burden. the importer may raise its selling price, accept a lower margin, negotiate with a foreign supplier or switch to a domestic source. workers, retailers and consumers can also be affected. the split depends on bargaining power, competition, contracts and how easily buyers can substitute another product. thue quan la thue danh vao hang nhap khau, thuong do nha nhap khau dung ten nop cho hai quan. ben nop theo luat chua chac la ben ganh toan bo chi phi kinh te. nha nhap khau co the tang gia ban, chap nhan bien loi nhuan thap hon, thuong luong voi nha cung cap nuoc ngoai hoac chuyen sang nguon noi dia. nguoi lao dong, nha ban le va tieu dung cung co the chiu anh huong. ganh nang phan chia tuy quyen thuong luong, canh tranh, hop dong va kha nang nguoi mua chuyen sang san pham khac. when a tariff rises, the duty-inclusive price at the border can increase even if the foreign supplier’s duty-exclusive price does not change. that does not tell us exactly how much appears in the shop. wholesalers, distributors and retailers may absorb some cost, re-price goods gradually or change margins on related products. exchange rates, shipping and input costs also move at the same time. imf research published in 2026 on us tariff changes in 2025 separated import prices from tariff-inclusive prices and highlighted import reallocation as another channel. khi thue tang, gia o bien gioi da gom thue co the tang du gia truoc thue cua nha cung cap nuoc ngoai khong doi. dieu do chua cho biet chinh xac gia ban le tang bao nhieu. nha ban si, phan phoi va cua hang co the ganh mot phan, dieu chinh dan hoac doi bien loi nhuan mat hang lien quan. ty gia, van tai va dau vao cung bien dong cung luc. nghien cuu imf nam 2026 ve thay doi thue my nam 2025 tach gia nhap khau truoc thue khoi gia gom thue, dong thoi nhan manh chuyen dich nguon nhap la mot kenh khac. if consumers have many close substitutes, they may switch quickly when prices rise, limiting a seller’s ability to pass the tariff through. if the good is essential or alternatives are scarce, buyers may bear more of the cost. exporters may lower their prices to retain market access, especially when they compete with other suppliers. these responses depend on time: firms can absorb a temporary shock, but change sourcing, contracts or product design over months or years. a single tariff rate therefore cannot predict the final consumer-price effect by itself. neu nguoi tieu dung co nhieu san pham thay the gan, ho co the doi nhanh khi gia tang, han che kha nang chuyen thue vao gia cua nguoi ban. neu hang hoa thiet yeu hoac it lua chon, nguoi mua co the ganh nhieu hon. nha xuat khau co the ha gia de giu thi truong, nhat la khi canh tranh voi nha cung cap khac. phan ung tuy thoi gian: doanh nghiep co the hap thu cu soc ngan han nhung doi nguon, hop dong hay thiet ke trong nhieu thang hoac nam. vi vay, chi thue suat khong du bao duoc muc tang gia cuoi cung. a tariff on steel or electronic components can affect domestic firms that use those imports, not just foreign producers. higher input costs may reduce output, investment or wages if businesses cannot pass them on. a protected producer may gain market share while downstream firms become less competitive. the effect depends on the share of imported inputs, domestic capacity and whether firms can substitute without sacrificing quality. analysts should trace both the protected industry and the industries that purchase its output before calling a tariff a net gain. thue danh vao thep hay linh kien dien tu co the anh huong doanh nghiep trong nuoc dung cac mat hang nhap khau, khong chi nha san xuat nuoc ngoai. chi phi dau vao cao hon co the lam giam san luong, dau tu hoac luong neu doanh nghiep khong chuyen duoc chi phi. nganh duoc bao ho co the tang thi phan trong khi doanh nghiep ha nguon kem canh tranh hon. tac dong tuy ty trong dau vao nhap, cong suat noi dia va kha nang thay the ma khong giam chat luong. nha phan tich can lan theo ca nganh duoc bao ho va nganh mua san pham cua no truoc khi goi thue la loi ich rong. to estimate pass-through, compare product-level prices before and after a tariff with suitable untreated products or markets. account for exchange rates, freight rates, product quality, supplier exit and changes in import composition. if buyers switch to a cheaper variety, the average price index can move differently from the price of the original item. imf’s 2026 study cautioned that results at the country-product level do not automatically equal a complete measure of consumer welfare or total inflation. estimates need a defined time window and an explicit counterfactual. de uoc tinh muc chuyen thue, so gia tung san pham truoc va sau thue voi san pham hoac thi truong doi chung phu hop. tinh den ty gia, cuoc van chuyen, chat luong, nha cung cap roi thi truong va thay doi co cau nhap. neu nguoi mua chuyen sang mat hang re hon, chi so gia trung binh co the khac gia mon ban dau. nghien cuu imf nam 2026 luu y ket qua cap quoc gia–san pham khong tu dong do day du phuc loi tieu dung hay lam phat tong the. uoc tinh can khoang thoi gian xac dinh va tinh huong doi chung ro. consumers can compare prices across brands and origins, but should also consider quality, repairability and the cost of switching. policymakers should identify the objective—revenue, bargaining leverage, security or temporary industry support—and estimate who pays, including downstream firms and lower-income households. as of the 2025–26 research snapshot, tariff effects were unfolding through both price changes and reallocation of imports; the scale varies across products and markets. treat a headline claim that “foreign countries pay the tariff” or “consumers pay all of it” as incomplete without incidence evidence. nguoi tieu dung co the so gia theo nhan hieu va xuat xu, dong thoi can nhac chat luong, kha nang sua chua va chi phi chuyen doi. nha hoach dinh can neu muc tieu—thu ngan sach, don bay thuong luong, an ninh hay ho tro nganh tam thoi—va uoc tinh ai tra, gom doanh nghiep ha nguon, ho thu nhap thap. theo nghien cuu 2025–2026, tac dong thue dang dien ra qua ca gia va chuyen dich nhap khau; quy mo khac theo san pham, thi truong. hay coi tuyen bo “nuoc ngoai tra thue” hay “nguoi tieu dung tra het” la chua du neu thieu bang chung phan bo ganh nang.
industrial-policy: chinh sach cong nghiep: khi nao tro cap tao nang luc, khi nao chi bao ho? industrial policy: building capacity or protecting incumbents? chinh sach cong nghiep gom tro cap, uu dai thue, tin dung va mua sam cong de thuc day nang luc o nganh duoc chon. du lieu oecd 2026 cho thay tro cap cong nghiep o cac cong ty lon theo doi len muc cao nhat ke tu khung hoang tai chinh. danh gia can tinh hieu qua, canh tranh, chi phi ngan sach va tac dong xuyen bien gioi. industrial policy is a set of public measures intended to change the structure or capabilities of an economy. tools include grants, tax concessions, below-market loans, public procurement, training, infrastructure and research support. governments may target emerging technology, decarbonization, regional employment or strategic resilience. these policies are not automatically good or bad. the core question is whether the intervention addresses a clearly identified market failure or public objective and whether its benefits exceed fiscal, competition and opportunity costs. chinh sach cong nghiep la nhom bien phap cong nham thay doi cau truc hay nang luc cua nen kinh te. cong cu gom tro cap, uu dai thue, khoan vay duoi lai thi truong, mua sam cong, dao tao, ha tang va ho tro nghien cuu. chinh phu co the huong den cong nghe moi, giam carbon, viec lam vung hoac kha nang chong chiu chien luoc. cac chinh sach nay khong mac nhien tot hay xau. cau hoi cot loi la can thiep co xu ly that bai thi truong hay muc tieu cong ro rang khong, va loi ich co vuot chi phi ngan sach, canh tranh, co hoi khong. a subsidy lowers a firm’s effective cost or provides capital it might not otherwise obtain. that can help a new technology reach scale, encourage learning or create infrastructure with wider benefits. it can also keep inefficient firms operating, shift business from unsubsidized rivals or trigger subsidy competition among governments. oecd’s 2026 magic database tracked grants, tax concessions and below-market finance to 525 large industrial groups; it reported support levels in 2024 at their highest since the global financial crisis. the data show scale, not proof that every subsidy works or fails. tro cap lam giam chi phi thuc te hoac cung cap von ma doanh nghiep kho co duoc. no co the giup cong nghe moi dat quy mo, khuyen khich hoc hoi hay tao ha tang mang loi ich rong. no cung co the giu doanh nghiep kem hieu qua, chuyen hoat dong khoi doi thu khong duoc tro cap hoac kich hoat canh tranh tro cap giua chinh phu. co so du lieu magic oecd 2026 theo doi tro cap, uu dai thue va tai chinh duoi gia thi truong cho 525 tap doan cong nghiep lon; du lieu ghi nhan muc ho tro nam 2024 cao nhat ke tu khung hoang tai chinh toan cau. quy mo khong chung minh moi tro cap thanh cong hay that bai. a program should state what outcome it seeks: research spillovers, lower emissions, supply security, worker skills or regional development. then ask what would happen without the support. if a firm would have built the same factory anyway, the subsidy may transfer public money without changing behavior. additionality is difficult to measure because the counterfactual cannot be observed directly; evaluation may use comparison firms, project milestones or independent review. clear objectives prevent success from being redefined after results disappoint. chuong trinh can neu ket qua muon dat: lan toa nghien cuu, giam phat thai, an ninh cung ung, ky nang lao dong hay phat trien vung. tiep do hoi dieu gi se xay ra neu khong co ho tro. neu doanh nghiep van xay nha may tuong tu, tro cap co the chuyen tien cong ma khong doi hanh vi. tinh bo sung kho do vi khong the truc tiep quan sat kich ban doi chung; danh gia co the so doanh nghiep, cot moc du an hay ra soat doc lap. muc tieu ro ngan viec dinh nghia lai thanh cong sau khi ket qua gay that vong. support to one company can affect prices, entry and investment decisions across an industry. a subsidy may create learning that benefits other firms, or it may entrench an incumbent and discourage new competitors. public procurement can create a first customer for an innovative product but may also lock in a supplier. competition safeguards include open eligibility, transparent award criteria, access to shared infrastructure and review of market concentration. oecd research in 2025–26 cautioned that market-share gains linked to subsidies do not necessarily represent productivity gains. ho tro mot cong ty anh huong gia, gia nhap nganh va quyet dinh dau tu cua doi thu. tro cap co the tao tri thuc lan sang doanh nghiep khac, hoac cung co doanh nghiep duong nhiem, lam doi thu moi nan long. mua sam cong co the tao khach hang dau tien cho san pham doi moi nhung cung khoa chat nha cung cap. bao ve canh tranh gom tieu chi du dieu kien mo, quy trinh trao ho tro minh bach, tiep can ha tang chung va ra soat tap trung thi truong. nghien cuu oecd 2025–2026 canh bao tang thi phan gan voi tro cap khong nhat thiet dong nghia tang nang suat. every grant or tax break has an opportunity cost: funds cannot simultaneously support health, education or other priorities. the public may also bear risk if government guarantees private borrowing. benefits can flow to shareholders while workers, taxpayers or consumers shoulder costs. a complete evaluation reports the amount spent, who receives it, jobs and capabilities created, wages, productivity, environmental effects and the cost per outcome. it should also consider whether support crowds out private investment or makes a favored sector more dependent on continued aid. moi khoan tro cap hay mien thue deu co chi phi co hoi: tien khong the dong thoi dung cho y te, giao duc hay uu tien khac. cong chung con co the ganh rui ro khi chinh phu bao lanh khoan vay tu nhan. co dong co the huong loi trong khi nguoi lao dong, nguoi nop thue hay tieu dung chiu chi phi. danh gia day du can cong bo khoan chi, nguoi nhan, viec lam va nang luc tao ra, luong, nang suat, tac dong moi truong va chi phi tren moi ket qua. cung can xet ho tro co lan at dau tu tu hay khien nganh phu thuoc tro cap keo dai khong. a credible policy has a review date, measurable milestones, disclosure and a route to stop support if conditions are not met. time limits can reduce capture, but industries may need long-term infrastructure and research commitments. the design should separate public-good investment from firm-specific assistance and publish the rationale for exceptions. international spillovers matter: one country’s subsidy may prompt others to respond, shifting costs rather than creating global capacity. good policy compares targeted support with neutral tools such as research funding, skills development or broad infrastructure investment. chinh sach dang tin co ngay ra soat, cot moc do duoc, cong bo du lieu va loi dung ho tro neu khong dat dieu kien. gioi han thoi gian giam nguy co bi nhom loi ich chi phoi, nhung nganh co the can cam ket dai han cho ha tang, nghien cuu. thiet ke can tach dau tu hang hoa cong khoi ho tro rieng doanh nghiep va cong bo ly do ngoai le. tac dong xuyen bien gioi quan trong: tro cap mot nuoc co the khien nuoc khac dap tra, chuyen chi phi chu khong tao nang luc toan cau. chinh sach tot so ho tro co muc tieu voi cong cu trung lap nhu tai tro nghien cuu, ky nang hay ha tang chung.
platform-work: viec lam qua nen tang so: linh hoat ve gio, nhung thu nhap va quyen loi can duoc nhin du platform work: flexibility, income and protections viec lam qua ung dung ket noi khach hang voi nguoi cung cap dich vu, tu giao hang den thiet ke truc tuyen. so lieu kho so sanh vi cong viec co the la nghe chinh, viec phu hoac nhiem vu rat ngan. oecd/ilo huong dan do luong nhan manh can tinh thoi gian cho, chi phi, bao tro xa hoi va quyen thuong luong. platform work uses a digital intermediary to match clients with workers or organize tasks. it includes location-based services such as ride-hailing and delivery, as well as online work such as translation, design or data labeling. a person may rely on a platform as a main job, use it occasionally or perform tasks through several platforms. this makes the category hard to measure with one question. the oecd, ilo and european union handbook on measurement emphasizes distinguishing the platform’s role, the task, payment arrangement and worker relationship. viec lam qua nen tang dung trung gian so de ghep khach hang voi nguoi lao dong hoac to chuc nhiem vu. no gom dich vu tai dia diem nhu goi xe, giao hang va viec truc tuyen nhu dich thuat, thiet ke hay gan nhan du lieu. mot nguoi co the song chu yeu bang nen tang, dung thinh thoang hoac lam qua nhieu nen tang. vi vay kho do bang mot cau hoi duy nhat. cam nang do luong cua oecd, ilo va lien minh chau au nhan manh can phan biet vai tro nen tang, nhiem vu, cach tra cong va quan he lao dong. a worker may choose when to log in, but demand, ratings and platform rules shape whether that time produces paid tasks. waiting for a customer, travelling to a pickup or bidding on work can consume time without direct payment. workers may value autonomy or the ability to combine tasks with study and caregiving, while still facing unstable earnings and limited control over prices. a fair comparison should calculate net hourly income after fuel, equipment, insurance, unpaid time and taxes, not just gross payments shown in an app. nguoi lao dong co the chon luc dang nhap, nhung nhu cau, xep hang va quy tac ung dung quyet dinh khoang thoi gian ay co tao viec tra tien khong. cho khach, di den diem don hay dau thau cong viec tieu ton thoi gian ma khong duoc tra truc tiep. ho co the coi trong tu chu, kha nang ket hop viec voi hoc tap hay cham soc, dong thoi van doi mat thu nhap bat on va it quyen dinh gia. so sanh cong bang can tinh thu nhap rong moi gio sau nhien lieu, thiet bi, bao hiem, thoi gian khong luong va thue, khong chi khoan gop trong ung dung. whether a platform worker is legally an employee, self-employed or in another category depends on the jurisdiction and facts, such as control over work, substitution rights and economic dependence. a platform’s label is not always decisive. employment status can affect minimum wages, leave, social insurance, collective bargaining and access to remedies. some systems create intermediate protections. do not generalize a court ruling or law from one country to another; workers and platforms should check current local rules and the actual contractual arrangement. nguoi lam nen tang duoc xem la nhan vien, tu doanh hay nhom khac tuy tham quyen va tinh tiet nhu muc kiem soat cong viec, quyen thue nguoi thay va phu thuoc kinh te. nhan do ung dung dat chua chac quyet dinh. tinh trang viec lam anh huong luong toi thieu, nghi phep, bao hiem xa hoi, thuong luong tap the va quyen yeu cau khac phuc. mot so he thong tao lop bao ve trung gian. dung ap phan quyet hay luat mot nuoc cho nuoc khac; nguoi lao dong va nen tang can kiem tra quy dinh dia phuong hien hanh va hop dong thuc te. headline counts may miss people who work only a few hours or combine online gigs with a standard job. a robust survey asks how often a platform assigned tasks, how much time was spent searching or waiting, who set prices and whether income was received. the 2023 oecd/ilo/eu handbook recommends improving measurement because definitions and national surveys differ. administrative platform data can help but may exclude inactive accounts, workers who leave and activity on competing apps. use multiple sources and disclose what each misses. so lieu tieu de co the bo nguoi chi lam vai gio hoac ket hop viec nen tang voi cong viec thuong. khao sat tot can hoi tan suat nen tang giao viec, thoi gian tim hay cho, ai dinh gia va co nhan thu nhap khong. cam nang oecd/ilo/eu nam 2023 khuyen nghi cai thien do luong vi dinh nghia va khao sat quoc gia khac nhau. du lieu hanh chinh tu ung dung co ich nhung co the bo tai khoan khong hoat dong, nguoi da nghi hay cong viec qua ung dung canh tranh. hay phoi hop nhieu nguon va cong khai gioi han tung nguon. workers can face difficulties organizing when they are dispersed, classified as independent contractors or dependent on platform access. collective representation may help them discuss rates, safety, deactivation rules and dispute procedures. social protection models can be portable across jobs so that contributions follow a person who works for several platforms. policy choices should account for small firms and genuine independent businesses while preventing a business model from shifting all risks to workers. fairness requires transparent criteria and a meaningful appeal when accounts are suspended. nguoi lao dong co the kho to chuc tieng noi chung khi phan tan, duoc xep la nha thau doc lap hay phu thuoc vao quyen truy cap ung dung. dai dien tap the giup ban muc tra, an toan, quy tac vo hieu hoa tai khoan va quy trinh tranh chap. mo hinh bao tro xa hoi co the chuyen theo nguoi lao dong giua nhieu nen tang. chinh sach can tinh doanh nghiep nho va hoat dong tu doanh thuc su, dong thoi ngan mo hinh kinh doanh day toan bo rui ro sang nguoi lam. cong bang doi tieu chi minh bach va quyen khang nghi thuc chat khi tai khoan bi khoa. before relying on a platform, check how pay is calculated, who bears equipment and accident costs, what happens when demand is low, how ratings affect access to work and whether you can export your records. compare net income across several weeks, not one high-demand day. keep receipts and a record of hours, including unpaid waiting if relevant to local rules. as of 2023–25, official measurement and workplace studies continued to flag income security, social protection and opaque management as issues; actual conditions differ by platform, country and occupation. truoc khi phu thuoc vao nen tang, hay kiem tra cach tinh tien, ai chiu chi phi thiet bi va tai nan, chuyen gi xay ra khi it khach, xep hang anh huong quyen nhan viec the nao va co tai duoc ho so khong. so thu nhap rong qua vai tuan chu khong chi mot ngay cao diem. giu hoa don va ghi gio lam, ke ca thoi gian cho khong tra neu quy dinh dia phuong lien quan. tinh den 2023–2025, nghien cuu chinh thuc ve do luong va noi lam tiep tuc neu an toan thu nhap, bao tro xa hoi va quan ly thieu minh bach; dieu kien thuc te khac theo ung dung, nuoc va nghe.
algorithmic-management: quan ly bang thuat toan: phan viec nhanh hon, nhung quyet dinh can co the giai thich algorithmic management: efficiency with accountability phan mem co the phan ca, giao nhiem vu, theo doi nang suat, cham diem va quyet dinh quyen nhan viec. oecd 2025 ghi nhan viec dung cong cu quan ly thuat toan va cac lo ngai ve quyen tu chu, tai cong viec, niem tin va cang thang. rui ro phu thuoc muc dich, du lieu va co che con nguoi xem xet. algorithmic management refers to software that automates or assists the coordination, assignment, monitoring or evaluation of workers. a warehouse system may set a task sequence; a delivery app can match orders and score completion; an office platform can track activity or recommend shifts. some tools use artificial intelligence, while others rely on fixed rules or dashboards. the key issue is not the label “ai” but what decision the tool makes, which data it uses and how much practical control a worker or supervisor retains. quan ly bang thuat toan la phan mem tu dong hoa hoac ho tro dieu phoi, phan cong, giam sat hay danh gia nguoi lao dong. he thong kho co the dat thu tu nhiem vu; ung dung giao hang ghep don va cham muc hoan thanh; nen tang van phong theo doi hoat dong hoac de xuat ca. mot so cong cu dung tri tue nhan tao, so khac dua quy tac co dinh hay bang dieu khien. van de chinh khong phai nhan “ai” ma la cong cu quyet dinh dieu gi, dung du lieu nao va nguoi lao dong hay quan ly giu duoc bao nhieu quyen kiem soat. automation can coordinate thousands of tasks, match demand with staffing and make some decisions more consistent. it may also increase monitoring, intensify work or penalize employees when data are incomplete. a productivity score based on clicks may reward visible activity rather than quality, collaboration or careful service. the same system may benefit managers by reducing scheduling work while shifting uncertainty onto staff. oecd’s 2025 employer survey and research note both efficiency claims and concerns; results vary by job, tool design and workplace governance. tu dong hoa co the dieu phoi hang nghin nhiem vu, khop nhu cau voi nhan su va lam mot so quyet dinh nhat quan hon. no cung co the tang giam sat, day cuong do cong viec len hoac phat nhan vien khi du lieu khong day du. diem nang suat dua tren so lan nhap co the thuong hoat dong de thay thay vi chat luong, hop tac hay dich vu chu dao. cung he thong giup quan ly giam viec xep lich nhung day bat dinh sang nhan vien. khao sat chu su dung lao dong va nghien cuu oecd nam 2025 ghi nhan ca loi ich hieu qua lan lo ngai; ket qua tuy nghe, thiet ke va quan tri noi lam. a system inherits limitations from its inputs. if past schedules gave some groups fewer desirable shifts, a model trained on past acceptance or performance may reproduce that pattern. location, device type or time online can act as proxies for protected characteristics. monitoring data can also be wrong because of a broken sensor, shared login or missing context. employers should test for disparate effects, verify data accuracy and explain what information is collected. workers need a way to correct records before a score affects pay, discipline or access to work. he thong ke thua gioi han tu du lieu dau vao. neu lich su cho mot nhom it ca tot hon, mo hinh hoc tu muc nhan ca hay hieu suat cu co the lap lai mau do. vi tri, loai thiet bi hay thoi gian truc tuyen co the thay the gian tiep cho dac diem duoc phap luat bao ve. du lieu giam sat cung co the sai do cam bien hong, dung chung tai khoan hay thieu ngu canh. nha tuyen dung can kiem tra tac dong khac biet, xac minh du lieu va giai thich thong tin thu thap. nguoi lao dong can cach sua ho so truoc khi diem so anh huong luong, ky luat hay co hoi viec. a nominal appeal button is weak if the reviewer simply accepts the algorithm’s recommendation. meaningful human oversight means a qualified person can access relevant evidence, understand the system’s limits and change the result. workers should be told when an automated tool materially influences an employment decision and receive a reason they can challenge. the review process must be timely, especially for shift access or pay. some decisions may be prohibited or governed by strict data-protection and employment laws; legal duties differ across jurisdictions. nut khang nghi tren danh nghia it gia tri neu nguoi xem xet chi chap nhan de xuat thuat toan. giam sat cua con nguoi thuc chat nghia la nguoi du nang luc duoc xem chung cu lien quan, hieu gioi han he thong va co the doi ket qua. nguoi lao dong can biet khi cong cu tu dong anh huong dang ke den quyet dinh viec lam va nhan ly do co the phan bien. quy trinh phai kip thoi, nhat la khi lien quan ca lam hay tien cong. mot so quyet dinh co the bi cam hoac chiu luat bao ve du lieu, lao dong nghiem ngat; nghia vu khac nhau theo nuoc. before deploying a tool, employers should identify its purpose, assess risks, consult workers, test under realistic conditions and document who is accountable. data minimization reduces privacy exposure; access controls limit who can inspect sensitive records. policies should set retention periods and restrict use of data collected for one purpose from being repurposed without a lawful basis. worker representatives can identify unintended consequences that developers miss. monitoring should be proportionate to a legitimate need, and alternatives should be considered when less intrusive methods can achieve the same goal. truoc khi trien khai cong cu, nha tuyen dung can xac dinh muc dich, danh gia rui ro, tham van nguoi lao dong, thu trong dieu kien thuc va ghi ro ai chiu trach nhiem. giam thieu du lieu han che lo rieng tu; kiem soat truy cap gioi han nguoi xem ho so nhay cam. chinh sach can dat thoi han luu va han che dung du lieu thu thap cho muc dich nay sang muc dich khac neu thieu can cu phap ly. dai dien lao dong co the nhan ra he qua ngoai y muon ma nha phat trien bo sot. giam sat phai tuong xung voi nhu cau hop phap; can xem xet cach it xam pham hon neu dat cung muc tieu. workers can ask what is monitored, how scores affect decisions, how long records remain, who sees them and how to challenge errors. managers should audit outcomes across teams and compare algorithmic recommendations with actual job quality, safety, turnover and complaints. as of oecd 2025 findings, algorithmic management was associated in worker reports with concerns such as autonomy and stress, though association does not prove a tool caused each outcome. the goal is accountable coordination: save administrative time while preserving dignity, privacy and fair treatment. nguoi lao dong co the hoi he thong theo doi gi, diem so anh huong quyet dinh ra sao, ho so luu bao lau, ai duoc xem va cach khieu nai sai sot. quan ly can kiem tra ket qua giua cac nhom, so khuyen nghi thuat toan voi chat luong viec, an toan, nghi viec va khieu nai. theo phat hien oecd 2025, bao cao cua nguoi lao dong lien he quan ly thuat toan voi lo ngai ve quyen tu chu va cang thang, du moi lien he khong chung minh cong cu gay moi ket qua. muc tieu la dieu phoi co trach nhiem: tiet kiem hanh chinh dong thoi giu pham gia, rieng tu va doi xu cong bang.
ai-productivity-measurement: ai va nang suat: vi sao loi ich o mot nhom viec chua hien ngay trong gdp? ai and productivity: why local gains may not show up in gdp mot cong cu ai giup hoan thanh tac vu nhanh hon chua dong nghia nang suat toan doanh nghiep hay nen kinh te da tang. can tinh thoi gian kiem chung, loi, tai thiet ke quy trinh, dao tao, chi phi von va tac dong len chat luong. cac tong hop ilo nam 2025–2026 nhan manh bang chung con khong dong deu va khoang cach do luong. productivity measures output relative to inputs, such as units per hour or value added per worker. an ai assistant may draft a response faster, but the employee may spend more time checking errors, correcting tone or handling exceptions. if output volume rises while quality falls, the productivity gain may be overstated. a useful evaluation defines the task, quality standard, worker time, software and compute cost, training and downstream rework. faster generation is a mechanism that could raise productivity, not the final evidence that it has. nang suat do san luong so voi dau vao, nhu so don vi moi gio hay gia tri gia tang tren lao dong. tro ly ai co the soan cau tra loi nhanh hon, nhung nhan vien co the mat them thoi gian kiem tra loi, sua giong dieu hay xu ly ngoai le. neu so luong tang ma chat luong giam, loi ich nang suat co the bi phong dai. danh gia huu ich xac dinh nhiem vu, chuan chat luong, thoi gian lao dong, chi phi phan mem va tinh toan, dao tao cung viec sua loi sau do. tao noi dung nhanh la co che co the tang nang suat, khong phai bang chung cuoi cung rang nang suat da tang. at the task level, compare completion time and error rates for similar work. at the team level, check whether queues shrink, service improves or work shifts to another department. at the firm level, examine value added, costs, output and customer retention. at the economy level, official statistics may take time to capture new services or intangible investment. the unit matters: a faster individual task can coexist with unchanged firm productivity if managers add review steps or demand rises to absorb the saved time. o cap tac vu, so thoi gian hoan thanh va ty le loi cua cong viec tuong tu. cap nhom xem hang cho giam, dich vu cai thien hay viec chuyen sang bo phan khac. cap doanh nghiep xem gia tri gia tang, chi phi, san luong, khach hang quay lai. cap nen kinh te, thong ke chinh thuc co the mat thoi gian ghi nhan dich vu moi hay dau tu vo hinh. don vi do rat quan trong: tac vu ca nhan nhanh hon van co the di cung nang suat doanh nghiep khong doi neu quan ly them buoc ra soat hoac nhu cau tang de hap thu thoi gian tiet kiem. a simple before-and-after comparison can be misleading if demand, staffing or the product changed at the same time. a better test compares similar teams or tasks, documents who used the tool and for what, and runs long enough to include learning and maintenance. randomized trials can help when fair and feasible; otherwise, matched comparisons and careful process data can be informative. results from one firm, language or job cannot be generalized automatically. publish uncertainty and include failed or neutral pilots to avoid selecting only success stories. so sanh truoc–sau don gian co the gay hieu lam neu nhu cau, nhan su hay san pham dong thoi thay doi. thu nghiem tot hon so doi hoac tac vu tuong tu, ghi ai dung cong cu, dung cho viec gi va keo dai du de tinh thoi gian hoc, bao tri. thu nghiem ngau nhien huu ich khi cong bang va kha thi; neu khong, nhom doi chieu tuong dong va du lieu quy trinh can than van co gia tri. ket qua o mot cong ty, ngon ngu hay nghe khong tu dong khai quat duoc. hay cong bo bat dinh va ca thu nghiem that bai hay trung tinh, tranh chi chon cau chuyen thanh cong. new technology may initially lower measured productivity because firms spend on software, data cleanup, training and organizational redesign before benefits arrive. official accounts may record much of this as current cost rather than as an asset, while useful knowledge and process changes take time to develop. economists sometimes describe this delay as a productivity j-curve: adoption costs appear first, gains later. it is a possible pattern, not a reason to assume future gains are guaranteed. firms still need evidence that implementation improves output after the adjustment period. cong nghe moi ban dau co the lam nang suat do duoc giam vi doanh nghiep dau tu phan mem, lam sach du lieu, dao tao va thiet ke lai to chuc truoc khi loi ich xuat hien. tai khoan chinh thuc co the ghi nhieu khoan la chi phi hien thoi thay vi tai san; tri thuc va thay doi quy trinh can thoi gian phat trien. kinh te hoc doi khi goi do tre nay la duong cong chu j nang suat: chi phi ap dung xuat hien truoc, loi ich den sau. day la mot mau hinh co the xay ra, khong phai ly do gia dinh loi ich tuong lai chac chan. doanh nghiep van can chung cu trien khai cai thien san luong sau giai doan dieu chinh. productivity gains can be distributed among workers, customers and owners through higher wages, lower prices, shorter hours or profits. if ai intensifies monitoring or eliminates entry-level learning tasks, output per hour may rise while job quality or future skill formation declines. measure errors, autonomy, safety, workload and wages alongside quantity. the ilo’s 2025–26 reviews of empirical evidence describe uneven adoption and measurement gaps; some firms report gains, while broader aggregate effects are not yet clear. local pilot results should not be confused with economy-wide outcomes. loi ich nang suat co the duoc chia giua nguoi lao dong, khach hang va chu so huu qua luong cao hon, gia thap hon, gio lam ngan hon hay loi nhuan. neu ai tang giam sat hoac loai bo nhiem vu dau vao noi nguoi moi hoc nghe, 2025–2026 mo ta muc ap dung khong deu va khoang trong do luong; vai doanh nghiep bao loi ich nhung tac dong tong the con chua ro. ket qua thu nghiem dia phuong khong phai ket qua toan nen kinh te. before adoption, establish a baseline and decide what counts as successful output. track setup time, subscription and computing costs, review time, error severity, customer outcomes and training. reassess after workers have learned the workflow, then ask whether the change is worth scaling or should be redesigned. include workers who perform the task in evaluation; they often know where hidden rework occurs. as of the ilo 2026 evidence review, firm-level gains remain mixed and aggregate productivity effects difficult to isolate. treat each use case as a testable investment rather than assuming that more ai means more productivity. truoc khi trien khai, lap moc nen va dinh nghia san luong thanh cong. theo doi thoi gian thiet lap, phi thue bao va tinh toan, thoi gian kiem chung, muc biet khau sua sai ngam. theo ra soat bang chung ilo 2026, loi ich cap doanh nghiep con trai chieu va anh huong nang suat tong the kho tach rieng. coi tung ung dung nhu khoan dau tu can thu nghiem, dung mac dinh nhieu ai dong nghia nang suat cao.
housing-supply-elasticity: kha nang cung ung nha o: vi sao nhu cau tang co noi lam gia bat manh? housing supply elasticity and affordability gia nha chiu anh huong cua nhu cau lan toc do nguon cung phan ung. oecd 2026 nhan manh khoang cach dai dang giua cung va cau cung thieu nha o xa hoi/gia phu hop. co gian cung giup giai thich vi sao cung cu soc dan so, gia co the khac theo vung; noi quy hoach chi hieu qua neu dat, ha tang, nang luc xay dung va kha nang chi tra cung duoc tinh. housing supply elasticity describes how strongly construction or the housing stock responds when prices or demand change. if supply is elastic, new homes can be added relatively quickly; if inelastic, demand growth shows up more in prices and rents. physical land is only one constraint. zoning, permits, infrastructure capacity, financing, building labor, materials and the time needed to complete a project all matter. oecd research finds substantial differences across regions and countries, so a policy that works in one city may have a smaller effect elsewhere. do co gian cung nha o mo ta muc xay dung hay luong nha phan ung khi gia hoac nhu cau doi. neu cung co gian, nha moi co the bo sung tuong doi nhanh; neu kem co gian, nhu cau tang the hien nhieu hon o gia va tien thue. dat vat ly chi la mot gioi han. quy hoach, giay phep, ha tang, von, lao dong xay dung, vat lieu va thoi gian hoan thanh du an deu quan trong. nghien cuu oecd cho thay khac biet lon giua vung va nuoc, vi vay chinh sach hieu qua o thanh pho nay co the tac dong it hon noi khac. population growth, new jobs, lower borrowing costs or household formation can increase demand for homes in a particular area. where new building is slow, existing owners may receive capital gains while renters and first-time buyers face higher costs. the effect depends on location: a dwelling in a remote area is not a substitute for housing near a job, school or transport. imf’s 2024 housing explainer describes supply and demand as the starting framework, while emphasizing that supply constraints shape the price response. tang dan so, viec lam moi, lai vay giam hay nhieu ho rieng lam tang nhu cau nha o tai mot khu vuc. noi xay moi cham, chu nha hien huu co the huong tang gia tai san trong khi nguoi thue va nguoi mua lan dau chiu chi phi cao hon. tac dong tuy vi tri: nha o vung xa khong thay duoc nha gan viec lam, truong hoc hay giao thong. bai giai thich nha o imf 2024 dung cung cau lam khuon kho xuat phat, dong thoi nhan manh gioi han nguon cung dinh hinh phan ung gia. allowing more homes near transit or jobs can support supply, but changing a zoning code does not produce finished housing overnight. utilities, roads, schools, construction finance and skilled labor must expand too. a large project may take years, and developers respond to expected sale prices and financing conditions. oecd’s 2026 work on affordability points to structural constraints and insufficient public investment in affordable and social housing. reform should be tracked by completions, location, bedroom mix and price bands—not just the number of permits approved. cho phep them nha gan giao thong hay viec lam co the ho tro cung, nhung sua quy hoach khong lap tuc tao nha hoan thien. dien nuoc, duong, truong, tai chinh xay dung va lao dong lanh nghe cung phai tang. du an lon co the keo dai nhieu nam; nha phat trien phan vi tri, co cau phong va phan khuc gia, khong chi so giay phep. even when more homes are built, low-income households may not be able to afford market rents. targeted rental assistance can provide immediate help, but if housing supply is highly constrained, additional purchasing power can push rents up unless more homes follow. social and affordable housing, tenant protections, transport links and land policy can complement new construction. oecd’s 2026 policy brief stresses expanding affordable and social rental supply alongside broader reforms. the right combination depends on local shortages and administrative capacity. ngay ca khi xay them nha, ho thu nhap thap co the van khong du tra tien thue thi truong. tro cap thue nha co muc tieu giup tuc thoi, nhung khi cung bi gioi han manh, suc mua them co the day tien thue len neu nha moi khong theo kip. nha o xa hoi, bao ve nguoi thue, ket noi giao thong va chinh sach dat co the bo sung xay moi. tom luoc chinh sach oecd 2026 nhan can remain in a neighborhood. new investment may improve amenities but also raise rents, displace long-term residents or replace smaller homes with larger units. evaluate both aggregate supply and distribution by income, tenure and location. community input helps identify needs such as accessible units or family-sized apartments. this does not mean every new development should be rejected; it means the public objective should be stated and measured, including affordability and access to opportunity. bung no xay dung co the tang tong cung dong thoi thay doi ai con o lai khu pho. dau tu moi cai thien tien ich nhung cung co the tang thue, day cu dan lau nam di noi khac hoac thay nha nho bang can lon. hay danh gia ca cung tong hop lan phan phoi theo thu nhap, hinh thuc so huu/thue va vi neighborhood conditions. ask which constraint binds: land use, infrastructure, finance, construction capacity or low household income. the oecd 2026 analysis emphasizes that conditions differ and policies should fit national circumstances. a fast-growing city may need both more homes and targeted support; a stagnant region may need transport or job access instead. housing affordability is a climate-risk-insurance: bao hiem rui ro khi hau: khoang trong bao ve va chia se ton that climate-risk insurance and the protection gap bao hiem co the giup ho gia dinh, doanh nghiep va chinh phu phuc hoi sau thien tai, nhung rui ro khi hau tuong quan lon, du lieu khong du va phi tang co the khien bao hiem kho mua hoac kho cung cap. imf 2026 nhan manh moi lien he giua kha nang bao hiem, kha nang chi tra va on dinh tai chinh. an insurance protection gap is the difference between economic losses from an event and the portion covered by insurance. it can be large when households lack policies, exclusions apply, limits are low or claims are delayed. after a flood, for example, insured homes may receive a payout while renters, informal businesses or public infrastructure remain uncovered. the gap is not simply a failure by insurers: affordability, risk awareness, policy design, building quality and public safety nets all affect who bears losses. khoang trong bao ve bao hiem la chenh lech han muc boi thuong nho. nguoi mua nen so hiem hoa duoc bao ve, thoi gian cho, can cu chi phi thay the, muc mien thuong va quy trinh yeu cau boi thuong. nha hoach dinh doi mat danh doi: tro phi bao ve giam; neu khong co ho tro, ho de ton thuong co the khong phuc hoi. bao hiem tham so co the tra khi mot chi so do duoc vuot nguong nhu luong mua, nhung tien nhan co the khong khop thiet hai thuc te. chon cong cu theo hiem hoa, chat luong du lieu va nguoi huong loi. check whether your policy covers flood, storm surge, wildfire or business interruption in your location; standard policies may exclude some hazards. keep an inventory, photos and proof of value, and know how to file a claim. ask whether resilience upgrades qualify for discounts and whether the deductible is affordable. for a city or lender, map exposures and uninsured assets and test how correlated losses could affect public budgets or loan collateral. as of 2026, imf supervisory work emphasized transparency and protection-gap measurement; policy terms and legal duties remain country-specific. hay kiem tra hop dong co bao ve lu, trieu cuong, chay rung hay gian doan kinh doanh tai noi minh khong; hop dong chuan co the loai tru mot so hiem hoa. luu danh muc tai san, anh va bang chung gia tri; biet cach yeu cau boi thuong. hoi nang cap chong chiu co giam phi khong va muc mien thuong co vua kha nang khong. voi thanh pho hay ben cho vay, lap ban do phoi nhiem, tai san khong bao hiem va kiem tra ton that tuong quan anh huong ngan sach hay tai san the chap ra sao. tinh den 2026, cong tac giam sat imf nhan manh minh bach va do khoang trong bao ve; dieu khoan, nghia vu phap ly tuy quoc gia.
pension-longevity-risk: rui ro song tho va luong huu: song lau hon can ke hoach chi tra dai hon pension longevity risk: funding retirement for longer lives khi tuoi tho tang, khoan tiet kiem huu tri phai chi tra lau hon. rui ro nay nam o ca nhan, quy huu tri va ngan sach cong, tuy thiet ke he thong. world bank 2025 nhan manh gia hoa, viec lam phi chinh thuc va thay doi nghe nghiep gay ap luc len muc bao phu lan ben vung. longevity risk is the possibility that people or pension providers must fund retirement for longer than expected. for an individual, savings can run down while living costs continue. for an annuity provider or defined-benefit plan, more years of payments can raise liabilities. for a public pay-as-you-go system, longer retirement can increase the period benefits are paid relative to contribution years. the risk is not that people live longer; it is that financing and benefit arrangements were not designed or adjusted for the realized lifespan. rui ro song tho la kha nang ca nhan hay nha cung cap huu tri phai tai tro thoi gian nghi huu dai hon du kien. voi ca nhan, tien tiet kiem co the can trong khi chi phi song tiep tuc. voi nha cung cap nien kim hay quy phuc loi xac dinh, tra them nhieu nam lam tang nghia vu. he thong cong tra theo muc dong hien tai co the phai chi tro cap lau hon so voi so nam dong. rui ro khong nam o viec con nguoi song lau hon, ma o cho tai tro va quyen loi chua duoc thiet ke hay dieu chinh theo tuoi tho thuc te. in a defined-benefit plan, the sponsor promises a formula-based pension and generally bears investment and longevity risks, subject to plan rules. in a defined-contribution account, the worker bears more investment and drawdown risk because retirement income depends on contributions and returns. an annuity can pool longevity risk across people, though it introduces insurer, pricing and inflation risks. many countries combine public, employer and personal plans. compare systems by who carries which risk rather than judging from the label “public” or “private.” trong quy phuc loi xac dinh, don vi tai tro hua tra luong huu theo cong thuc va thuong ganh rui ro dau tu, song tho tuy quy tac. trong tai khoan dong gop xac dinh, nguoi lao dong ganh nhieu rui ro dau tu va rut tien hon vi thu nhap huu tri tuy dong gop, loi nhuan. nien kim co the gop rui ro song tho giua nhieu nguoi, nhung phat sinh rui ro cong ty bao hiem, dinh gia va lam phat. nhieu nuoc ket hop he thong cong, chu lao dong, ca nhan. hay so ai ganh rui ro nao, dung chi nhin nhan “cong” hay “tu”. an aging population can reduce the number of workers relative to retirees, but demography alone does not determine fiscal outcomes. employment rates, wages, migration, retirement age, productivity and informality affect contributions and tax receipts. people also have unequal life expectancy across income, occupation and health status, so a uniform age rule may affect groups differently. world bank discussions in 2024–25 emphasized adapting pension systems to aging and changing work patterns while addressing coverage gaps. policy analysis should model both demographic projections and the distribution of healthy working years. dan so gia co the giam so nguoi lao dong tuong doi voi nguoi nghi huu, nhung nhan khau hoc khong tu quyet dinh tai khoa. ty le co viec, luong, di cu, tuoi nghi huu, nang suat va phi chinh thuc anh huong dong gop, thu thue. tuoi tho cung khac theo thu nhap, nghe va suc khoe, nen mot tuoi nghi huu chung tac dong khac nhau giua nhom. thao luan world bank 2024–2025 nhan manh dieu chinh he thong huu tri theo gia hoa, thay doi viec lam va xu ly khoang trong bao phu. phan tich chinh sach can mo hinh ca du bao dan so lan phan bo so nam khoe manh co the lam viec. workers in informal jobs may not contribute regularly to a pension scheme, even if they work throughout their lives. caregiving breaks, part-time work and migration can also create gaps in contribution records, disproportionately affecting women in many settings. raising the statutory retirement age cannot by itself provide income security to people with insufficient contributions or poor health. policy options include portable benefits, minimum pensions, subsidized contributions and broader social assistance, each requiring funding and careful targeting. access should be assessed by actual entitlement, not only legal eligibility on paper. nguoi lam phi chinh thuc co the khong dong huu tri deu dan du lam viec suot doi. nghi cham soc, lam ban thoi gian va di cu cung tao khoang trong ho so dong gop, thuong anh huong phu nu nhieu hon. tang tuoi nghi huu theo luat tu no khong tao an toan thu nhap cho nguoi dong chua du hay suc khoe kem. lua chon gom quyen loi co the chuyen theo nguoi, luong huu toi thieu, tro cap dong gop va an sinh rong hon; moi cach can ngan sach, nham muc tieu can than. can danh gia quyen loi thuc te, khong chi dieu kien phap ly tren giay. a pension system can be financially sustainable but provide benefits too low to prevent poverty, or generous today while creating an unfunded liability for future taxpayers. actuarial projections use assumptions about fertility, migration, wages, returns, inflation and life expectancy. small assumption changes can materially change long-term balances. publish ranges and sensitivity tests rather than a single point estimate. reforms may adjust contributions, benefits, retirement age, indexation or funding; each option distributes costs differently across generations and income groups. he thong huu tri co the ben vung tai chinh nhung tro cap qua thap de ngan ngheo doi, hoac hao phong hom nay nhung tao nghia vu chua co nguon cho nguoi nop thue tuong lai. du bao tinh toan bao hiem dua gia dinh sinh suat, di cu, luong, loi nhuan, lam phat, tuoi tho. thay doi nho trong gia dinh co the doi manh so du dai han. hay cong bo khoang va kiem tra do nhay thay vi mot con so don. cai cach co the doi muc dong, quyen loi, tuoi nghi, cach dieu chinh lam phat hay nguon von; moi lua chon chia chi phi khac giua the he, nhom thu nhap. individuals can review expected public benefits, employer plans, contribution records, debt, housing costs and emergency savings. check whether projections are expressed in today’s money and include inflation assumptions. a diversified plan may combine savings with income that lasts for life, but products differ in fees, guarantees and access to funds. do not rely on a generic online calculator for a high-stakes personal decision. as of world bank 2025 work, pension policy increasingly addressed longevity, informality and new work patterns; exact eligibility and benefit rules remain country-specific. ca nhan co the xem tro cap cong du kien, quy chu lao dong, ho so dong gop, no, chi phi nha o va tiet kiem khan cap. kiem tra du bao tinh theo tien hom nay khong va gia dinh lam phat nao. ke hoach da dang co the ket hop tiet kiem voi thu nhap tron doi, nhung san pham khac phi, bao dam va kha nang rut tien. dung chi dua may tinh chung tren mang cho quyet dinh he trong. theo cong viec world bank 2025, chinh sach huu tri ngay cang xu ly song tho, phi chinh thuc va cach lam viec moi; dieu kien quyen loi chinh xac tuy quoc gia.
sovereign-debt-restructuring: tai co cau no quoc gia: khoi phuc kha nang tra no bang thuong luong nhieu ben sovereign debt restructuring: restoring a sustainable path khi quoc gia khong the tra no theo lich ma van duy tri cac chuc nang thiet yeu, tai co cau co the doi ky han, lai, gia tri goc hoac dieu kien. qua trinh phuc tap vi chu no gom song phuong, da phuong, trai chu tu nhan va ngan hang. imf/world bank 2025 nhan manh minh bach du lieu, phoi hop va thoi gian xu ly. a sovereign government may face debt service that exceeds the resources it can mobilize without destabilizing the economy or cutting essential services. if temporary liquidity support cannot restore a credible payment path, restructuring may change interest rates, maturities, principal or other terms. a government can also restructure pre-emptively to reduce risk before missing payments. the choice depends on debt sustainability, market access, policy capacity and social conditions. restructuring is negotiated with creditors; the imf cannot simply compel private or bilateral lenders to forgive debts. chinh phu co the doi mat khoan tra no vuot nguon luc huy dong duoc neu khong gay bat on kinh te hay cat dich vu thiet yeu. neu ho tro thanh khoan tam thoi khong khoi phuc duoc lo trinh tra dang tin, tai co cau co the doi lai suat, ky han, tien goc hay dieu kien khac. chinh phu cung co the tai co cau truoc khi lo han de giam rui ro. lua chon tuy tinh ben vung no, tiep can thi truong, nang luc chinh sach va dieu kien xa hoi. tai co cau can thuong luong voi chu no; imf khong the tu buoc ben cho vay tu nhan hay song phuong xoa no. public debt can include bonds, bank loans, bilateral official loans, multilateral claims, domestic-currency debt and guaranteed liabilities of state enterprises. each contract has different governing law, maturity and coordination rules. some obligations may be hidden in arrears, collateralized borrowing or public-private partnerships. a comprehensive debt register helps authorities and creditors understand the perimeter before negotiating. the imf and world bank have emphasized transparency and debt-sustainability analysis, while the g20 common framework involves official bilateral creditors for eligible countries. private creditors still require separate legal and financial coordination. no cong co the gom trai phieu, vay ngan hang, khoan vay song phuong chinh thuc, no da phuong, no noi te va nghia vu bao lanh doanh nghiep nha nuoc. moi hop dong khac luat dieu chinh, ky han va quy tac phoi hop. mot so nghia vu co the an trong no qua han, vay the chap tai san hay hop tac cong tu. so dang ky no day du giup chinh quyen va chu no hieu pham vi truoc dam phan. imf va world bank nhan manh minh bach, phan tich ben vung no; khuon kho chung g20 gom chu no song phuong chinh thuc cho nuoc du dieu kien. chu no tu nhan van can phoi hop phap ly, tai chinh rieng. debt sustainability asks whether a country can meet current and future obligations without implausible fiscal adjustment, default or damagingly high inflation. it is not a single debt-to-gdp threshold. analysts consider interest rates, growth, exchange rates, primary balances, currency composition, maturity structure and contingent liabilities. a country with moderate debt can face stress if it owes foreign currency and loses market access; a higher ratio may be manageable under other conditions. forecasts are uncertain, so debt-sustainability analysis tests alternative scenarios rather than pretending to know a precise future. tinh ben vung no hoi quoc gia co the dap ung nghia vu hien tai va tuong lai ma khong can dieu chinh tai khoa phi thuc te, vo no hay lam phat gay hai hay khong. day khong phai mot nguong no/gdp duy nhat. nha phan tich xem lai suat, tang truong, ty gia, can can so cap, co cau tien te, ky han va nghia vu tiem an. nuoc co no vua phai van cang thang neu vay ngoai te roi mat tiep can thi truong; ty le cao hon co the quan ly duoc trong dieu kien khac. du bao bat dinh nen phan tich thu nhieu kich ban thay vi gia vo biet tuong lai chinh xac. a restructuring may extend maturities, reduce interest, lower principal or link payments to economic outcomes. creditors compare the proposed recovery with likely outcomes under delay or default. official and private creditors may need comparable treatment, but legal instruments and economic exposures differ. negotiations can stall over data, burden sharing or assurances that other lenders will participate. the global sovereign debt roundtable’s 2024–25 work sought common understanding and clearer processes; progress reports describe technical coordination, not a universal automatic mechanism. country-specific agreements remain essential. tai co cau co the keo dai ky han, giam lai, giam goc hoac gan khoan tra voi ket qua kinh te. chu no so muc thu hoi de xuat voi kich ban tri hoan hay vo no. chu no chinh thuc va tu nhan co the can doi xu tuong duong, nhung van ban phap ly va muc rui ro khac nhau. thuong luong co the dinh tre vi du lieu, chia ganh nang hay cam ket ben cho vay khac tham gia. cong viec ban tron no quoc gia cua g20/imf 2024–2025 tim dong thuan ky thuat va quy trinh ro hon; bao cao tien do khong phai co che tu dong cho moi nuoc. thoa thuan theo tung quoc gia van thiet yeu. debt service can crowd out health, education, infrastructure or climate adaptation, but restructuring also has costs: market exclusion, bank losses, litigation and uncertainty for citizens and firms. cutting public spending abruptly may deepen recession and reduce future tax revenue. a credible program balances fiscal repair with protection for vulnerable households and reforms that improve growth and revenue. creditor recovery matters, but so do public services and the country’s ability to return to sustainable borrowing. distributional impacts should be made explicit rather than hidden inside an aggregate debt ratio. tra no co the lan at y te, giao duc, ha tang hay thich ung khi hau, nhung tai co cau cung ton kem: mat tiep can thi truong, lo ngan hang, kien tung va bat dinh cho dan, doanh nghiep. cat chi cong dot ngot co the lam suy thoai sau hon, giam nguon thu tuong lai. chuong trinh dang tin can bang phuc hoi tai khoa voi bao ve ho de ton thuong va cai cach nang tang truong, thu ngan sach. thu hoi cua chu no quan trong, cung nhu dich vu cong va kha nang vay ben vung tro lai. tac dong phan phoi can neu ro, khong giau trong ty le no tong. a workable process publishes reliable debt data, explains assumptions, identifies creditors and establishes a timetable for engagement. authorities need domestic consultation and clear communication with citizens, while protecting sensitive negotiations when necessary. creditors benefit from comparable information and predictable steps. the world bank’s international debt report 2025 documented high external debt stocks and debt-service pressures in low- and middle-income countries; a global snapshot does not determine any one country’s solvency. for a live case, follow official country documents and current legal advice. the goal is a credible path that supports essential services and sustainable payments. quy trinh kha thi cong bo du lieu no dang tin, giai thich gia dinh, nhan dien chu no va dat lich trao doi. chinh quyen can tham van trong nuoc, truyen dat ro cho nguoi dan, dong thoi bao ve thuong luong nhay cam khi can. chu no duoc loi tu thong tin tuong duong va buoc du doan duoc. bao cao no quoc te world bank 2025 ghi nhan no nuoc ngoai cao va ap luc tra no o nuoc thu nhap thap, trung binh; buc tranh toan cau khong quyet dinh kha nang thanh toan cua mot nuoc cu the. voi vu dang dien ra, theo doi tai lieu chinh thuc quoc gia va tu van phap ly cap nhat. muc tieu la lo trinh dang tin, giu dich vu thiet yeu va thanh toan ben vung.
carbon-border-adjustment: cbam: dinh gia carbon nhung o bien gioi va tac dong len nha xuat khau carbon border adjustment: pricing embedded emissions at the border co che dieu chinh carbon bien gioi nham phan anh gia carbon cua mot so hang nhap khau so voi san pham noi dia, giam rui ro chuyen phat thai ra noi quy dinh yeu hon. eu buoc vao giai doan chinh thuc tu 1/1/2026; pham vi, cach tinh va nghia vu co the thay doi theo huong dan. a carbon border adjustment mechanism (cbam) seeks to address carbon leakage: production may move to jurisdictions with weaker carbon constraints, or domestic products may be replaced by more emissions-intensive imports. the policy aims to align the carbon cost on selected imports with the cost faced by domestic producers under a climate policy. it is not a universal tax on every imported product. the design must specify covered goods, emissions measurement, treatment of foreign carbon prices and how certificates or payments are handled. co che dieu chinh carbon bien gioi (cbam) nham xu ly ro ri carbon: san xuat co the chuyen den noi han che carbon yeu hon, hoac hang noi dia bi thay bang hang nhap phat thai nhieu hon. chinh sach tim cach dieu chinh chi phi carbon tren mot so hang nhap cho tuong xung voi chi phi nha san xuat noi dia chiu theo chinh sach khi hau. day khong phai thue pho quat len moi hang nhap. thiet ke can neu hang thuoc pham vi, cach do phat thai, xu ly gia carbon nuoc ngoai va chung chi hay khoan thanh toan. embedded emissions are greenhouse gases released in producing a covered good, including relevant production processes and, under the applicable methodology, certain inputs. for steel, for example, the production route and electricity source can change the measured footprint. importers may use verified actual data or default values where rules permit. data quality and verification are crucial: estimates based on a supplier’s unsupported claim may not qualify. small exporters can face significant reporting burdens, so shared measurement tools and clear guidance matter. phat thai nhung la khi nha kinh thai ra khi san xuat hang thuoc pham vi, gom quy trinh san xuat lien quan va mot so dau vao theo phuong phap ap dung. voi thep, chang han, quy trinh san xuat va nguon dien lam dau chan phat thai doi. nha nhap khau co the dung du lieu thuc duoc xac minh hoac gia tri mac dinh khi luat cho phep. chat luong du lieu va xac minh rat quan trong: uoc tinh dua loi nha cung cap khong chung minh co the khong hop le. nha xuat khau nho chiu ganh bao cao dang ke, nen cong cu do chung va huong dan ro rat can thiet. the european union’s cbam transitional period ran from october 2023 through 2025, focused on reporting embedded emissions for specified goods. the european commission states that the definitive regime applies from 1 january 2026, with financial obligations and detailed rules for covered operators. the initial sectors include cement, iron and steel, aluminium, fertilizers, electricity and hydrogen. the exact obligations, thresholds, default values and reporting steps may be updated, so exporters should use current commission guidance rather than older summaries. the timeline here is an eu-specific snapshot as of 2026. giai doan chuyen tiep cbam cua lien minh chau au keo dai tu thang 10/2023 den het 2025, tap trung bao cao phat thai nhung cua mot so hang hoa. uy ban chau au cho biet che do chinh thuc co hieu luc tu 1/1/2026, kem nghia vu tai chinh va quy tac chi tiet cho don vi thuoc pham vi. nganh ban dau gom xi mang, sat thep, nhom, phan bon, dien va hydro. nghia vu cu the, nguong, gia tri mac dinh, buoc bao cao co the duoc cap nhat; nha xuat khau can xem huong dan hien hanh cua uy ban thay vi tom tat cu. moc thoi gian nay la anh chup chinh sach eu tinh den 2026. an importer facing a cbam obligation may pay for certificates reflecting embedded emissions and the relevant carbon price, with deductions where a carbon price has already been paid abroad under the rules. that cost can affect contract prices, margins or the choice of supplier. exporters may respond by measuring emissions, changing energy sources or investing in cleaner production. the result differs by product, production method, verified data and market power; cbam does not mean every exporter faces the same charge. businesses should calculate exposure using the official method and scenario-test changes in carbon prices. nha nhap khau chiu nghia vu cbam co the phai mua chung chi phan anh phat thai nhung va gia carbon lien quan; quy tac cho phep khau tru phan gia carbon da nop o nuoc ngoai trong mot so truong hop. chi phi anh huong gia hop dong, bien loi nhuan hay lua chon nha cung cap. nha xuat khau co the do phat thai, doi nguon dien hoac dau tu san xuat sach hon. ket qua khac theo san pham, quy trinh, du lieu xac minh va quyen luc thi truong; cbam khong dong nghia moi nha xuat khau chiu cung khoan phi. doanh nghiep can tinh theo phuong phap chinh thuc va thu kich ban gia carbon. cbam can encourage emissions measurement beyond the regulating market, but it can also impose administrative and financial costs on exporters with limited monitoring capacity. countries may question whether the measure treats different development levels fairly or complies with trade rules. transparent calculation, recognition of carbon prices paid elsewhere and technical support can reduce disputes. revenue use also matters: support for decarbonization in exporting countries may be discussed, but it depends on the legal and political design. avoid assuming the measure is automatically protectionist or automatically climate-effective; evaluate emissions, trade and distribution outcomes. cbam co the thuc day do phat thai ngoai thi truong ap dung, nhung cung ap chi phi hanh chinh va tai chinh len nha xuat khau thieu nang luc giam sat. cac nuoc co the chat van cach doi xu giua muc phat trien khac nhau hay su phu hop voi luat thuong mai. tinh toan minh bach, cong nhan gia carbon da tra noi khac va ho tro ky thuat co the giam tranh chap. cach dung nguon thu cung quan trong: co the ban ho tro khu carbon tai nuoc xuat khau nhung tuy thiet ke phap ly, chinh tri. dung mac dinh bien phap tu dong la bao ho hay tu dong hieu qua khi hau; hay danh gia phat thai, thuong mai va phan phoi. map covered products and customs codes; identify the eu importer responsible for reporting or certificates; measure facility-level emissions; document energy use and input data; arrange verification; and track the carbon price paid in the country of production. check whether a default value would materially increase the liability compared with verified actual emissions. the commission updated guidance in 2026, including materials for the definitive period. small producers can coordinate through industry associations but remain responsible for accurate data supplied to customers. for legal obligations, consult current official rules and trade specialists. hay lap danh sach san pham thuoc pham vi va ma hai quan; xac dinh nha nhap khau eu chiu trach nhiem bao cao/chung chi; do phat thai cap co so; luu du lieu nang luong, dau vao; sap xep xac minh va theo doi gia carbon da nop o nuoc san xuat. kiem tra gia tri mac dinh co lam nghia vu cao hon du lieu thuc xac minh khong. uy ban chau au cap nhat huong dan nam 2026, gom tai lieu cho che do chinh thuc. nha san xuat nho co the phoi hop qua hiep hoi nganh nhung van chiu trach nhiem tinh chinh xac du lieu cung cap cho khach. voi nghia vu phap ly, hoi quy tac chinh thuc va chuyen gia thuong mai hien hanh.
remittance-costs: chi phi kieu hoi: mot khoan phi nho theo giao dich thanh ganh nang lon remittance costs: small fees, large cumulative effects chi phi gui tien xuyen bien gioi gom phi niem yet, chenh lech ty gia, phi nhan va chi phi thoi gian. world bank uoc tinh cuoi 2023 gui 200 usd toan cau ton trung binh 6.4%, cao hon muc tieu sdg 3%; day la snapshot theo hanh lang, thoi diem, kenh. a remittance is money sent by a migrant or other sender to a person or organization in another country. the visible transfer fee is only one part of the cost. a provider may also earn from the exchange-rate margin, charge a receiving fee or impose a delivery fee for cash pickup. the sender’s time and transport to an agent matter too. to compare offers, calculate how much the recipient actually receives from the same amount sent, using the same currencies and delivery method. kieu hoi la tien nguoi di cu hay nguoi gui chuyen cho ca nhan hoac to chuc o nuoc khac. phi chuyen hien thi chi la mot phan chi phi. nha cung cap co the kiem them tu chenh lech ty gia, tinh phi nhan hoac phi giao tien mat. thoi gian va chi phi di den dai ly cua nguoi gui cung dang ke. de so dich vu, hay tinh nguoi nhan thuc nhan bao nhieu tu cung so tien gui, dung cung loai tien va cach nhan. for a $200 transfer, a 6% total cost equals $12, while 3% equals $6. the difference may appear small once, but repeated monthly transfers compound into a substantial annual sum for a family. the world bank’s june 2024 release estimated a global average cost of 6.4% for sending $200 in late 2023, more than twice the sustainable development goal target of 3%. averages hide differences: some corridors and providers are far cheaper, while others remain costly. voi khoan gui 200 do, tong chi phi 6% la 12 do, con 3% la 6 do. chenh lech co ve nho mot lan nhung gui hang thang tich luy thanh khoan dang ke moi nam voi gia dinh. thong cao world bank thang 6/2024 uoc tinh chi phi trung binh toan cau de gui 200 do cuoi 2023 la 6,4%, hon gap doi muc tieu phat trien ben vung 3%. so trung binh che khac biet: mot so hanh lang, nha cung cap re hon nhieu, so khac van ton kem. prices can be high where few providers operate, cash dominates, compliance checks are costly or access to banking and settlement systems is limited. digital wallets may lower some costs but require a phone, data access, identification and a usable way for recipients to cash out. interoperability between payment systems can reduce dependence on multiple intermediaries. competition policy should also consider transparency and safe consumer redress; the lowest fee is not useful if the transfer is delayed or the provider is unreliable. gia co the cao khi it nha cung cap, tien mat pho bien, kiem tra tuan thu ton kem hoac kho tiep can ngan hang va he thong quyet toan. vi so co the giam mot so chi phi nhung can dien thoai, mang, giay to va cach rut tien phu hop cho nguoi nhan. kha nang tuong tac giua he thong thanh toan giam phu thuoc vao nhieu trung gian. chinh sach canh tranh can tinh minh bach va khieu nai an toan; phi thap khong huu ich neu tien tre hay nha cung cap khong dang tin. the cost of sending money depends on origin and destination, currency pair, amount, cash versus account delivery and the provider’s network. a global average cannot tell a specific worker what their family will receive. compare providers in the exact corridor, check the rate lock period and see whether the recipient must pay to withdraw. official world bank remittance prices worldwide data can support comparisons, but quotes change with the market. keep the date and method when using a published figure. chi phi chuyen tien tuy noi gui, noi nhan, cap tien te, so tien, nhan tien mat hay tai khoan va mang luoi nha cung cap. trung binh toan cau khong cho nguoi lao dong biet gia dinh minh se nhan bao nhieu. hay so dich vu dung hanh lang, kiem tra thoi gian giu ty gia va nguoi nhan co mat phi rut tax-gap-e-invoicing: khoang trong thue va hoa don dien tu: du lieu giup kiem tra cheo nhung khong tu chua moi van de tax gaps and e-invoicing: better data, not an automatic fix khoang trong vat uoc tinh chenh lech giua nghia vu thue tiem nang va so thuc thu, co the gom gian lan, khong tuan thu, pha san va lua chon chinh sach. hoa don dien tu giup doi chieu giao dich gan thoi gian thuc, nhung can chuan du lieu, bao mat, nang luc xu ly khieu nai. oecd 2024 ghi nhan cac nuoc tang dung uoc tinh tax gap va cong cu so. a tax gap is an estimate of the difference between tax legally due under a defined framework and revenue actually collected over a defined period. for vat, the gap can reflect fraud, under-reporting, non-registration, errors, bankruptcies and collection failures. it is not a direct count of deliberate evasion. different estimation methods may produce different numbers, and the estimate depends on the tax base, rate rules and national accounts. oecd’s tax administration 2024 report notes growing use of gap measurement to identify compliance risks and drivers. khoang trong thue la uoc tinh chenh lech giua khoan thue phai nop theo khuon kho xac dinh va so thu thuc te trong giai doan xac dinh. voi vat, khoang trong co the do gian lan, khai thieu doanh thu, khong dang ky, sai sot, pha san va that bai thu hoi. no khong phai con so truc tiep cua tron thue co y. phuong phap uoc tinh khac co the cho ket qua khac; con so tuy co so thue, quy tac thue suat va tai khoan quoc gia. bao cao oecd tax administration 2024 ghi nhan viec do khoang trong ngay cang dung de xac dinh rui ro va nguyen nhan khong tuan thu. e-invoicing creates an invoice in a structured digital format that can be transmitted to a buyer, seller or tax authority. systems range from post-audit models, where records are retained for later inspection, to clearance or near-real-time reporting, where authorities validate or receive transaction data earlier. matching seller output tax with buyer input claims can flag inconsistencies. technology does not guarantee that a transaction is real, correctly classified or paid. the rules for corrections, credit notes and cross-border transactions must be clear. hoa don dien tu tao hoa don o dinh dang so co cau truc, truyen cho ben mua, ban hoac co quan thue. he thong tu mo hinh hau kiem, luu ho so de kiem tra sau, den mo hinh thong quan hay bao gan thoi gian thuc, khi co quan xac nhan hoac nhan du lieu som. doi chieu thue dau ra cua nguoi ban voi khau tru dau vao cua nguoi mua giup phat hien bat nhat. cong nghe khong bao dam giao dich co that, phan loai dung hay da tra tien. quy tac sua hoa don, ghi giam va giao dich xuyen bien gioi can ro. if a supplier reports a sale and the purchaser reports a corresponding input credit, a tax system can cross-check the two records. a mismatch may indicate a data-entry error, timing difference, classification issue or fraud; it should trigger review, not an automatic accusation. oecd material on tax administration describes digital continuous transaction reporting as one tool used alongside audits and risk management. businesses need a correction path and clear deadlines so ordinary mistakes do not freeze legitimate refunds or create repeated penalties. neu nha cung cap khai ban hang con nguoi mua khai khau tru dau vao tuong ung, he thong thue co the doi chieu hai ho so.
