la mot cong cu cung kiem toan, quan tri rui ro. doanh nghiep can duong sua sai va han ro de loi binh thuong khong dong bang hoan thue hop phap hay gay phat lap. digital invoices can reduce manual data entry, improve audit trails and support faster tax analysis. they can also impose setup costs, software fees and training burdens, particularly on small businesses. a tax authority needs interoperable standards, secure storage, cyber resilience and staff who can interpret alerts. if systems are unreliable, businesses may face duplicate filings or downtime. oecd’s 2024 review highlighted digital reporting measures in multiple jurisdictions but does not imply that every rollout caused a specific reduction in tax gaps. evaluate local outcomes and the baseline. hoa don so co the giam nhap lieu thu cong, cai thien dau vet kiem toan va ho tro phan tich thue nhanh hon. chung cung tao chi phi thiet lap, phan mem, dao tao, nhat la voi doanh nghiep nho. co quan thue can chuan tuong thich, luu tru an toan, chong su co mang va nhan vien biet doc canh bao. neu he thong khong on dinh, doanh nghiep co the khai trung hay bi gian doan. danh gia oecd 2024 neu bien phap bao cao so o nhieu tham quyen, nhung khong ham y moi dot trien khai deu gay muc giam khoang trong thue cu the. can do ket qua dia phuong va moc nen. tax data can reveal a company’s customers, suppliers and transactions. authorities should limit collection to a lawful purpose, restrict access, retain records only as needed and protect against breaches. taxpayers should be able to see notices, correct errors, appeal decisions and receive human review where automated risk scoring affects enforcement. a mismatch score is a signal for inquiry, not proof of wrongdoing. transparent governance strengthens compliance because people are more likely to use a system they trust and understand. du lieu thue co the tiet lo khach hang, nha cung cap va giao dich doanh nghiep. co quan can gioi han thu thap theo muc dich hop phap, han che number of e-invoices. compare results with a plausible counterfactual and account for tax-rate or economic changes. as of oecd 2024 guidance, gap measurement is increasingly part of compliance management; each country’s vat rules and legal safeguards remain distinct. cai cach can neu khoang trong nao muon giam, cach uoc tinh, chuan hoa don nao dung va doanh nghiep nho tuan thu ra sao. theo doi thoi gian khai, cham hoan thue, ty le loi, chi phi tuan thu va so thu chu khong chi luot dang ky hay so hoa don dien tu. so ket qua voi doi chung hop ly, tinh thay doi thue suat va kinh te. theo personalized-pricing: dinh gia ca nhan hoa: du lieu co the tuy bien gia, nhung khong phai moi gia khac nhau deu do thuat toan personalized pricing: data, fairness and consumer choice dinh gia ca nhan hoa dung du lieu de dua muc gia hoac uu dai khac nhau cho nguoi tieu dung dua tren suy doan muc san long tra. can phan biet voi gia thay doi theo thoi gian, vi tri hay chi phi chung. nghien cuu oecd 2025–2026 nhan manh tac dong cua ai, du lieu va thuat toan len lua chon, canh tranh va tinh minh bach. airfares rising near a holiday, a discount offered to all new customers and a price tailored to one person’s purchase history are not the same practice. dynamic pricing changes with time, stock or market demand. personalized pricing uses information about a particular consumer or group to estimate willingness to pay and tailor an offer. price discrimination is a broader economic concept for charging different prices not fully explained by cost differences. the data and decision process matter when assessing fairness or regulation. gia ve may bay tang gan ky nghi, uu dai ap dung cho moi khach moi va gia tuy theo lich su mua cua mot nguoi khong phai cung mot cach lam. dinh gia dong doi theo thoi gian, ton kho hay nhu cau thi truong. dinh gia ca nhan hoa dung thong tin ve nguoi hay nhom cu the de uoc luong muc san long tra roi tuy bien de nghi. phan biet gia la khai niem kinh te rong hon ve viec tinh gia khac nhau ma khong hoan toan do chi phi. du lieu va quy trinh quyet dinh quan trong khi danh gia cong bang hay quan ly. a retailer can use browsing history, location, device or past purchases to predict which product or discount a user may accept. algorithms can personalize the offer without the consumer seeing the model. a higher price is not the only possibility: some people may receive a lower price or a targeted coupon. the impact depends on data accuracy, market competition, consumer alternatives and whether the offer is transparent. oecd work on digital markets in 2026 notes that data-driven personalization can affect consumer agency and market dynamics; actual use varies by firm and market. nha ban le co the dung lich su duyet, vi tri, thiet bi hay lan mua truoc de du doan nguoi dung chap nhan san pham hay giam gia nao. thuat toan co the ca nhan hoa de nghi ma khach khong thay mo hinh. gia cao hon khong phai kha nang duy nhat: mot so nguoi duoc gia thap hay phieu giam muc tieu. tac dong tuy do chinh xac du lieu, canh tranh, lua chon cua khach va tinh minh bach. nghien cuu oecd ve thi truong so nam 2026 neu ca nhan hoa dua du lieu co the anh huong quyen chu dong tieu dung va dong luc thi truong; thuc te khac theo cong ty, linh vuc. personalized offers can match a product to a consumer’s needs, provide discounts to price-sensitive customers or help firms manage inventory. risks include opaque price differences, inference from sensitive data, exclusion of vulnerable groups and reduced ability to compare offers. if users cannot tell whether a difference reflects a sale or their profile, they may perceive the market as unfair. a price that is affordable for one buyer and high for another can also raise distributional questions even when no law is broken. benefits and risks depend on context. de nghi ca nhan hoa co the khop san pham voi nhu cau, giam gia cho nguoi nhay cam voi gia hoac giup quan ly ton kho. rui ro gom chenh lech gia mo am, suy luan tu du lieu nhay cam, loai tru nhom de ton thuong va giam kha nang so sanh. neu khach khong biet khac biet do khuyen mai hay ho so ca nhan, ho co the thay thi truong bat cong. gia vua kha nang voi nguoi nay nhung cao voi nguoi khac cung dat cau hoi phan phoi du khong vi pham luat. loi ich va rui ro tuy boi canh. showing a notice that prices are personalized may improve transparency, but consumers can overlook disclosures or lack a practical alternative. disclosure should explain what data are used, whether a price is tailored, how to opt out and where to complain. it should not bury information in a long policy. regulators may also examine competition, privacy and anti-discrimination law, because a notice cannot legitimize every data practice. oecd consumer research has found that people may not notice some disclosures, so effectiveness should be tested rather than assumed. hien thong bao gia duoc ca nhan hoa co the tang minh bach, nhung nguoi dung co the bo qua hoac khong co lua chon thuc te. cong bo nen giai thich du lieu nao duoc dung, gia co tuy bien khong, cach tu choi va noi khieu nai. dung giau trong chinh sach dai. co quan quan ly cung co the xem luat canh tranh, rieng tu, chong phan biet doi xu vi thong bao khong hop phap hoa moi cach dung du lieu. nghien cuu nguoi tieu dung oecd cho thay nguoi dan co the khong de y mot so thong bao; hieu qua can duoc thu chu khong mac dinh. use an independent browser or device only if that fits the service’s terms and privacy rules; do not assume incognito mode prevents tracking. compare the total price, including delivery, membership and financing charges, across providers. check whether a coupon is limited to a user profile and whether opting out affects service access. avoid sharing unnecessary personal information, review privacy settings and ask customer support about unexplained differences. screenshots and timestamps can help document a complaint, but one price discrepancy does not by itself prove unlawful discrimination. hay dung trinh duyet hay thiet bi doc lap neu phu hop dieu khoan, quyen rieng tu; dung nghi che do an danh ngan moi theo doi. so tong gia gom giao hang, thanh vien, phi tra gop giua nha cung cap. kiem tra ma giam gioi han theo ho so va tu choi co anh huong tiep can dich vu khong. tranh chia se du lieu khong can, xem cai dat rieng tu va hoi ho tro ve chenh lech khong ai can make dynamic and personalized pricing more granular, but evidence of use and welfare impact differs by sector. a sound assessment separates what is technically possible from what a firm actually does. doanh nghiep can ghi ro muc dich, nguon du lieu, thu nghiem va tac dong nguoi tieu dung du kien cua mo hinh gia. kiem tra loi hay ket qua chenh lech, han che du lieu nhay cam, cong bo de hieu va giu giam sat con nguoi cho quyet dinh he trong. co quan canh tranh co the xem ca nhan hoa cung co quyen luc thi truong hay loai doi thu khong; co quan tieu dung quan tam minh bach, hanh vi development-finance-debt: tai chinh phat trien va no: von uu dai co the mo du an, nhung phai tinh nghia vu tuong lai development finance: funding investment without hiding debt costs tai chinh phat trien gom khoan vay, vien tro, bao lanh va cong cu giam rui ro de ho tro dau tu ha tang, dich vu cong, doanh nghiep. no co the tao tai san va nang luc sinh loi, nhung tra no cao co the lan at chi tieu phat trien. world bank idr 2025 neu dong tra no rong lon o cac nuoc thu nhap thap, trung binh. development finance is funding intended to support economic and social outcomes, including roads, power, health, education, climate adaptation and private investment. it can come as grants, concessional loans, market-rate loans, guarantees, equity or blended finance that combines public and private capital. each instrument has different repayment, risk and accountability features. a grant does not create a debt payment, while a loan does; a guarantee may create a contingent liability even if no cash is paid initially. compare the legal commitment, not just the project’s label. tai chinh phat trien la nguon von huong den ket qua kinh te, xa hoi nhu duong sa, dien, y te, giao duc, thich ung khi hau va dau tu tu. nguon gom vien tro, vay uu dai, vay lai thi truong, bao lanh, von co phan hay tai chinh pha tron giua cong va tu. moi cong cu khac nghia vu tra, rui ro, trach nhiem. vien tro khong tao khoan tra no, con khoan vay thi co; bao lanh tao nghia vu tiem an du chua chi tien ngay. hay so cam ket phap ly chu khong chi nhan du an. a concessional loan generally offers a lower interest rate, longer maturity or grace period compared with market terms. its grant element approximates the value of that financial advantage. lower-cost borrowing can fund projects whose social returns exceed direct revenue, such as public health or climate resilience. yet concessional funds are limited and may still require repayment, co-financing or policy conditions. assess the currency, interest reset, grace-period end and repayment schedule. “soft loan” does not mean free money or automatically affordable debt. khoan vay uu dai thuong co lai thap hon, ky han dai hon hay thoi gian an han so voi thi truong. thanh to vien tro uoc luong gia tri uu dai do. vay re co the tai tro du an loi ich xa hoi cao hon doanh thu truc tiep nhu y te cong hay chong chiu khi hau. tuy nhien, von uu dai huu han va van co the can hoan tra, dong tai tro hay dieu kien chinh sach. danh gia dong tien, dieu chinh lai, luc het an han va lich tra. “vay mem” khong co nghia cho khong hay tu dong vua kha nang. borrowing is more defensible when it supports a well-designed asset or service that raises future capacity, and when expected benefits justify financial and social costs. a road may lower logistics costs; a power grid can enable firms to operate; a school can raise skills over decades. but poor procurement, land disputes, weak maintenance or low demand can leave debt without the expected return. project appraisal should test demand, environmental effects, distribution and operation costs before construction, then publish performance after completion. vay no co co so hon khi ho tro tai san hay dich vu duoc thiet ke tot, tang nang luc tuong lai va loi ich ky vong xung chi phi tai chinh, xa hoi. duong co the giam logistics; luoi dien giup doanh nghiep hoat dong; truong hoc nang ky nang nhieu thap ky. nhung mua sam yeu, tranh chap dat, thieu bao tri hay nhu cau thap co the de lai no ma khong co loi ich ky vong. tham dinh du an can thu nhu cau, moi truong, phan phoi, van hanh truoc xay, roi cong bo ket qua sau hoan thanh. a country must use revenue or refinance debt to pay principal and interest. if servicing costs rise, budgets may have less room for health, education, social protection and climate investment. the world bank’s international debt report 2025 found developing countries paid substantially more in external debt service than they received in new financing over 2022–24, while external debt stocks reached records in 2024. these are aggregate findings, not a verdict about every borrower. country-level analysis should examine maturity, currency and creditor mix, as well as the development return on borrowing. quoc gia can dung nguon thu hoac vay lai de tra goc va lai. neu chi phi tra no tang, ngan sach con it cho hon cho y te, giao duc, an sinh va dau tu khi hau. bao cao no quoc te world bank 2025 nhan thay cac nuoc dang phat trien tra no nuoc ngoai nhieu hon dang ke luong von vay moi nhan trong 2022–2024; du no nuoc ngoai dat ky luc nam 2024. day la phat hien tong hop, khong phai phan quyet cho tung ben vay. phan tich quoc gia can xem ky han, dong tien, co cau chu no va loi ich phat trien tu von vay. blended finance uses public or concessional funds to mobilize private investment, for example through a first-loss tranche or guarantee. it can make a project investable where risks are high but public benefits are broad. however, public support may subsidize investors who would have invested anyway or hide a government liability. report how much private capital was genuinely additional, who bears losses, what return investors receive and what happens if the project underperforms. the world bank describes multiple innovative financing tools, but the proper structure depends on project cash flows and governance. tai chinh pha tron dung von cong hoac uu dai de huy dong dau tu tu, chang han lop chiu lo dau tien hay bao lanh. no co the giup du an du kha nang dau tu khi rui ro cao nhung loi ich cong rong. tuy nhien, ho tro cong co the tro cap nha dau tu von van dau tu, hoac che nghia vu chinh phu. hay cong bo luong von tu thuc su bo sung, ai chiu lo, loi nhuan nha dau tu nhan va dieu gi xay ra khi du an kem. world bank mo ta nhieu cong cu sang tao, nhung cau truc phu hop tuy dong tien va quan tri du an. before approving development finance, publish the total project cost, currency and repayment terms; include guarantees, state-enterprise obligations and maintenance costs. run stress tests for lower growth, higher interest rates, currency depreciation and construction delays. compare a loan with grants, domestic revenues or phased construction. track jobs, service access, productivity and climate resilience alongside debt repayment. the world bank’s 2025 debt reporting emphasizes timely and comprehensive data; transparent accounting helps citizens see whether an investment supports development or shifts hidden costs to future taxpayers. truoc khi duyet von phat trien, cong bo tong chi phi, dong tien va dieu khoan tra; tinh ca bao lanh, nghia vu doanh nghiep nha nuoc va bao tri. thu kich ban tang truong thap, lai cao, mat gia tien te va cham thi cong. so khoan vay voi vien tro, thu trong nuoc hay xay theo giai doan. theo doi viec lam, tiep can dich vu, nang suat, chong chiu khi hau cung khoan tra no. bao cao no world bank 2025 nhan manh du lieu kip thoi, toan dien; hach toan minh bach giup nguoi dan thay dau tu ho tro phat trien hay chuyen chi phi an sang nguoi nop thue tuong lai.
ai-tutoring-evidence: gia su ai: hua hen can duoc kiem chung ai tutoring needs careful evidence mot thu nghiem nam 2025 cho thay tiem nang, nhung ket qua chua dai dien cho moi lop hoc. a tutor can adapt an explanation to a learner’s question, pace and previous answer. generative ai makes this interaction available through ordinary text or voice interfaces, so researchers are testing whether it can support learning at scale. the important question is not whether a chatbot sounds helpful, but whether students learn more, retain the material and can use it later. in 2025, a randomized study at harvard compared a carefully designed ai physics tutor with an active classroom lesson. its result is encouraging, but it answers a specific question in one course, not whether every ai tutor works. gia su co the dieu chinh loi giai thich theo cau hoi, toc do va cau tra loi truoc do cua nguoi hoc. ai tao sinh dua tuong tac nay vao giao dien chu hoac giong noi pho bien, nen cac nha nghien cuu dang kiem tra lieu no co ho tro hoc tap tren quy mo lon khong. cau hoi quan trong khong phai chatbot nghe co ve huu ich, ma la hoc sinh co hoc duoc nhieu hon, nho lau hon va van dung duoc ve sau khong. nam 2025, mot thu nghiem ngau nhien tai harvard so sanh gia su ai vat ly duoc thiet ke ky voi bai hoc tuong tac tren lop. ket qua dang khich le nhung chi tra loi mot cau hoi cu the trong mot khoa hoc, khong chung minh moi gia su ai deu hieu qua. the study involved 194 undergraduate students and used two short lessons in introductory physics. students were assigned to learn through the ai tutor or through an active-learning class, then completed quizzes. the reported learning gains favored the tutor condition, and students also described greater engagement. the tutor was not an unstructured chatbot: it used instructional prompts intended to ask guiding questions, explain concepts and give feedback. this design detail matters. a tool that encourages a learner to reason through a problem is different from one that simply supplies a finished answer, even if both use the same underlying language model. nghien cuu co 194 sinh vien dai hoc va su dung hai bai hoc ngan ve vat ly nhap mon. sinh vien duoc phan vao nhom hoc qua gia su ai hoac lop hoc chu dong, sau do lam bai kiem tra. muc hoc tien bo duoc bao cao cao hon o nhom gia su, dong thoi sinh vien mo ta muc tham gia cao hon. gia su khong phai chatbot tu do: no dung chi dan su pham nham dat cau hoi goi mo, giai thich khai niem va phan hoi. chi tiet thiet ke rat quan trong. cong cu khuyen khich nguoi hoc tu suy luan khac voi cong cu chi dua dap an hoan chinh, du ca hai dung cung mo hinh ngon ngu nen tang. a well-designed tutor can offer immediate, private feedback. learners may ask a question without worrying that classmates will judge them, request another example, or work through a mistake at their own pace. teachers may use the system to provide extra practice while they spend class time on discussion and individual support. in language learning, a tutor might prompt a student to revise a sentence rather than replace it with a polished version. these are plausible benefits, not automatic outcomes. they giac ngu co lien he voi cung co tri nho, tuc on dinh va sap xep lai mot so ky uc sau hoc. dieu nay khong co nghia nao phat lai moi su that trong dem hay giac ngu bien buoi hoc yeu thanh thanh thao. thay vao do, giac ngu tao dieu kien de dau vet ky uc moi co the duoc tang cuong va ket noi voi kien thuc san co. nha nghien cuu xem xet cac giai doan ngu va loai tri nho khac nhau, nen khong co mot co che duy nhat giai thich moi ket qua. diem thuc te la ngu du ho tro hoc cung voi luyen tap va phan hoi. a systematic review and meta-analysis published in 2024 examined experimental studies of sleep restriction and memory formation. the review reported that restricting sleep can impair both encoding, the initial learning of information, and consolidation, the later stabilisation of memory. this matters because students sometimes treat sleep as optional time that can be exchanged for last-minute study. yet staying awake longer does not guarantee that more material will be learned accurately. the review combines results from multiple studies, which gives a broader estimate than one experiment, but findings still depend on the tasks, participants and definitions of restricted sleep used by the researchers. mot tong quan he thong va phan tich gop cong bo nam 2024 xem xet thi nghiem ve han che ngu va hinh thanh ky uc. bai tong quan bao cao han che ngu co the lam suy giam ca ma hoa — buoc hoc thong tin ban dau — lan cung co, tuc on dinh tri nho ve sau. dieu nay quan trong vi doi khi hoc sinh xem ngu la thoi gian co the doi lay on gap. nhung thuc lau hon khong dam bao hoc chinh xac duoc nhieu hon. phan tich gop ket hop nhieu nghien cuu, cho uoc luong rong hon mot thi nghiem, song ket qua van phu thuoc nhiem vu, nguoi tham gia va dinh nghia ve thieu ngu ma nghien cuu dung. sleep and the next day. stress, illness, shift work, caregiving and environmental noise can make regular sleep difficult; advice should recognise these circumstances rather than blame individuals. for students, a consistent routine and a realistic study plan are more practical than trying to force an exact bedtime every night. if sleep problems are persistent or severe, professional health advice is more appropriate than treating them as a simple productivity issue. giac ngu va viec hoc lien ket hai chieu. hoc tao thong tin de cung co sau do, con ngu kem co the khien hom sau kho duy tri chu y, dieu hoa cam xuc va ma hoa thong tin moi. cang thang, benh tat, lam ca, cham soc nguoi than va tieng on khien ngu deu dan kho khan; loi khuyen nen ghi nhan hoan canh thay vi do loi ca nhan. voi hoc sinh, ne nep on dinh va ke hoach hoc thuc te huu ich hon co ep gio di ngu chinh xac moi dem. neu van de giac ngu keo dai hoac nghiem trong, tu van y te chuyen mon phu hop hon xem do chi la van de nang suat. lai va phan hoi van quan trong. giac ngu khong the tu sua dang tin cay mot hieu sai chua duoc phat hien. nguoi hoc khai niem, thu giai thich, kiem tra loi roi ngu du co quy trinh tot hon nguoi doc thu adolescent-brain-development: nao tuoi vi thanh nien dang phat trien, khong phai “hong” adolescent brains develop through experience nao tiep tuc thay doi trong tuoi vi thanh nien; khac biet phat trien khong dong nghia moi thanh thieu nien deu boc dong. adolescence is a period of continuing physical, emotional and social development. the brain does not suddenly switch from “unfinished” to “adult” on one birthday. different neural systems change along overlapping timelines, and connections are refined as people learn and experience new environments. development includes both biological processes and interaction with family, peers, school and culture. this makes adolescence a window of adaptation, not simply a deficit stage. young people can show strong reasoning in familiar, calm settings while making different choices under pressure, emotion or peer influence. a single stereotype cannot describe every teenager or every decision. tuoi vi thanh nien la giai doan phat trien the chat, cam xuc va xa hoi tiep dien. nao khong dot ngot chuyen tu “chua hoan thien” sang “nguoi lon” vao mot sinh nhat. cac he than kinh thay doi theo nhung moc thoi gian chong lan, ket noi duoc tinh chinh khi con nguoi hoc va trai nghiem moi truong moi. phat trien gom ca qua trinh sinh hoc lan tuong tac voi gia dinh, ban be, truong hoc va van hoa. vi vay day la giai doan thich nghi, khong chi la thoi ky thieu hut. nguoi tre co the suy luan tot trong boi canh quen, yen tinh nhung quyet dinh khac khi chiu ap luc, cam xuc hoac anh huong ban be. mot khuon mau khong the mo ta moi thieu nien hay quyet dinh. brain development is often simplified into the claim that the emotional brain matures early while the rational brain is not ready until the mid-twenties. this story is memorable but too neat. research examines networks, specific abilities and individual development rather than a single maturity switch. executive skills such as planning and impulse control develop through adolescence, but performance depends on context and experience. teenagers already make thoughtful choices and can take responsibility; they also benefit from support when consequences are complex or immediate rewards are strong. avoid using age-based neuroscience as an excuse to dismiss young people’s views or to assume that every adolescent behaves recklessly. su phat trien nao thuong bi don gian hoa thanh cau chuyen nao cam xuc truong thanh som con nao ly tri chua san sang den giua tuoi doi muoi. cau chuyen de nho nhung qua gon. nghien cuu xem xet mang luoi, nang luc cu the va phat trien ca nhan chu khong phai cong tac truong thanh duy nhat. ky nang dieu hanh nhu lap ke hoach, kiem soat boc dong tien trien trong tuoi vi thanh nien, nhung the hien tuy boi canh va kinh nghiem. thanh thieu nien van co the quyet dinh suy nghi va chiu trach nhiem; ho cung duoc loi tu ho tro khi hau qua phuc tap hoac phan thuong truoc mat hap dan. dung dung than kinh hoc theo tuoi de gat bo y kien nguoi tre hay mac dinh ho lieu linh. peers can influence risk-taking, but social influence is not always harmful. friends may encourage dangerous behaviour, yet they can also support exercise, study, belonging and help-seeking. the effect depends on the group, activity and setting. a teenager deciding in front of friends may weigh immediate social approval differently from when thinking privately; that does not mean the person lacks values. adults can reduce avoidable risk by offering clear boundaries, opportunities for meaningful choice and spaces where young people can discuss consequences without humiliation. supportive relationships create practice in decision-making rather than removing all independence. ban be co the anh huong hanh vi rui ro, nhung anh huong xa hoi khong luon co hai. nhom ban co the khuyen khich hanh vi nguy hiem, cung co the ho tro van dong, hoc tap, cam giac thuoc ve va tim tro giup. tac dong tuy nhom, hoat dong va boi canh. thieu nien quyet dinh truoc mat ban co the can nhac su chap nhan tuc thoi khac luc suy nghi rieng; dieu do khong co nghia ho thieu gia tri song. nguoi lon co the giam rui ro co the tranh bang gioi han ro, co hoi lua chon co y nghia va khong gian de nguoi tre ban hau qua ma khong bi lam nhuc. quan he ho tro tao co hoi luyen quyet dinh thay vi tuoc bo doc lap. recent developmental science emphasises variation rather than a single timetable. two people of the same age can differ in experience, stress exposure, sleep, health and support, all of which shape behaviour and learning. brain-imaging measures are not mind-reading devices: observing a group-level pattern does not tell us exactly what one young person will do. researchers also distinguish statistical trends from moral or legal judgments about responsibility. when evidence is used in policy, it should inform environments that help adolescents thrive, not become a deterministic label. good explanations state what a study measured and avoid claiming that one brain region alone causes a complex choice. khoa hoc phat trien gan day nhan manh khac biet ca nhan thay vi mot lich trinh duy nhat. hai nguoi cung tuoi co the khac kinh nghiem, muc cang thang, giac ngu, suc khoe va ho tro, tat ca deu dinh hinh hanh vi va viec hoc. anh chup nao khong doc duoc suy nghi: mau hinh o cap nhom khong cho biet chinh xac mot nguoi tre se lam gi. nha nghien cuu cung phan biet xu huong thong ke voi phan xet dao duc hay phap ly ve trach nhiem. khi dung bang chung cho chinh sach, muc tieu la tao moi truong giup thanh thieu nien phat trien, khong dan nhan dinh menh. giai thich tot neu nghien cuu do gi va khong khang dinh mot vung nao don le gay ra lua chon phuc tap. families and schools can apply this knowledge by pairing autonomy with structure. let young people practise making choices, explain the reasons behind boundaries and provide reliable adults they can consult when plans change. teach concrete skills such as breaking a goal into steps, considering a second outcome and delaying a response during conflict. these are learnable abilities, not traits that either appear fully formed or never develop. sleep, safety, belonging and access to mental-health gia dinh va truong hoc co the ung dung hieu biet nay bang cach ket hop tu chu voi cau truc. hay cho nguoi tre luyen chon lua, giai thich ly do dat gioi han va duy tri nguoi lon dang tin de hoi khi ke hoach thay doi. day ky nang cu the nhu chia muc tieu thanh buoc, can nhac he qua thu hai va tri hoan phan ung luc xung dot. day la nang luc co the hoc, khong phai tinh cach hoac tu nhien xuat hien hoan chinh hoac khong bao gio phat trien. giac ngu, an toan, cam giac thuoc ve va tiep can ho tro suc khoe tinh than cung dinh hinh phat trien. than kinh hoc khong dua kich ban nuoi day con, nhung ung ho kien nhan, ky vong nhat quan va co hoi xay nang luc qua trai nghiem co huong dan. a balanced account of the adolescent brain avoids two errors: treating teenagers as miniature adults with no need for support, and treating them as incapable of reason. development continues, but young people also learn, contribute and make meaningful decisions now. good policies provide safety while preserving voice and participation. in ielts writing, one can argue that schools should teach decision-making and emotional regulation rather than relying only on punishment. such a view recognises biological development without reducing a person to biology. the strongest evidence-based claim is modest: abilities change through adolescence, people vary widely, and supportive settings can help them practise sound judgment. cach nhin can bang tranh hai loi: xem thieu nien nhu nguoi lon thu nho khong can ho tro, hoac coi ho khong co kha nang ly tri. phat trien van tiep dien, nhung nguoi tre dang hoc, dong misinformation-correction: sua tin sai: bac bo, giai thich va thay the how corrections can address misinformation thu nghiem nam 2024 cho thay cach trinh bay dinh chinh co the anh huong muc nguoi doc tuong tac voi no. misinformation is inaccurate or misleading information, whether it spreads intentionally or by mistake. once people have encountered a false claim, simply repeating it with the word “false” may not fully remove its influence. a correction needs to help readers understand what happened and what account is better supported. it can identify the inaccurate claim, state the accurate information and explain why the original account fails. this provides a replacement explanation rather than leaving a gap. corrections work in a crowded information environment where people may skim, distrust the source or remember the repeated claim more easily than the rebuttal. thong tin sai lech la thong tin khong chinh xac hoac gay hieu lam, du lan truyen co chu y hay do nham lan. sau khi gap tuyen bo sai, chi lap lai no kem chu “sai” co the chua loai bo het anh huong. dinh chinh can giup nguoi doc hieu dieu gi xay ra va cach giai thich nao co bang chung tot hon. co the chi ra tuyen bo khong chinh xac, neu thong tin dung va giai thich vi sao cau chuyen ban dau khong dung vung. nhu vay co loi giai thay the thay vi de khoang trong. viec dinh chinh dien ra trong moi truong thong tin chat choi, noi nguoi doc luot nhanh, nghi nguon hoac nho tuyen bo lap lai hon phan bac bo. a useful correction usually makes the accurate account clear and gives readers a reason to trust it. for example, instead of only saying that a photograph does not show a current event, explain when and where the image was originally taken and link to evidence. specific details let a reader check the claim independently. the correction should be visible near the misleading content and should avoid adding unnecessary repetition of a vivid false statement. this does not require a long lecture every time. the right level of detail depends on the complexity of the claim, the audience’s prior knowledge and the risk of further spreading it. mot dinh chinh huu ich thuong lam ro loi giai dung va dua ly do de nguoi doc tin. thay vi chi noi anh khong mo ta su kien hien tai, hay giai thich anh duoc chup khi nao, o dau va dan bang chung. chi tiet cu the giup doc gia tu kiem tra. dinh chinh nen xuat hien gan noi dung gay hieu lam va tranh lap khong can thiet tuyen bo sai gay an tuong manh. khong phai lan nao cung can bai giang dai. muc chi tiet phu hop tuy do phuc tap, kien thuc san co cua doc gia va nguy co tiep tuc lan truyen. research in 2024 tested how fact-check framing affected engagement across four countries. the study found that presenting a fact-check as confirmation of accurate information could attract more engagement than framing it only as a refutation. this does not mean people should avoid correcting falsehoods or that one wording will work everywhere. the outcome measured engagement with corrections in a particular experimental context, not whether every participant permanently changed a belief. the finding suggests that communicators may gain attention by foregrounding what is known, while still clearly explaining which claim is inaccurate. audience, platform and issue can alter the effect. nghien cuu nam 2024 kiem tra cach dong khung kiem chung su that anh huong tuong tac tai bon quoc gia. nghien cuu thay trinh bay bai kiem chung nhu xac nhan thong tin chinh xac co the thu hut tuong tac hon chi dong khung nhu bac bo. dieu nay khong co nghia nen tranh sua sai hoac mot cach dien dat hieu qua o moi noi. ket qua do muc tuong tac voi bai dinh chinh trong boi canh thi nghiem cu the, khong do viec moi nguoi thay doi niem tin lau dai. phat hien goi y nguoi truyen thong co the thu hut chu y bang dieu da biet, dong thoi giai thich ro tuyen bo nao sai. doi tuong, nen tang va van de co the lam doi tac dong. corrections can sometimes have side effects. a 2024 multi-country experiment on prominent misinformation interventions found that some strategies reduced misperceptions but also increased scepticism more broadly. broad scepticism may cause people to distrust reliable information along with false claims. this is not an argument for withholding corrections; it is a reason to design them carefully. communicators should distinguish “this specific claim lacks evidence” from “nothing can be trusted,” show how sources were checked and avoid suggesting that all accounts are equally uncertain. measuring both accuracy and wider trust helps detect whether an intervention fixes one problem while creating another. dinh chinh doi khi co tac dung phu. mot thi nghiem da quoc gia nam 2024 ve can thiep thong tin sai noi bat cho thay vai chien luoc giam nhan thuc sai nhung cung tang hoai nghi rong hon. hoai nghi chung co the khien nguoi ta mat niem tin ca thong tin dang tin cung voi tuyen bo sai. day khong phai ly do giau dinh chinh ma la ly do thiet ke can than. nguoi truyen thong nen phan biet “tuyen bo cu the nay thieu bang chung” voi “khong gi dang tin”, cho thay cach kiem tra nguon va tranh am chi moi loi ke deu bat dinh nhu nhau. do ca do chinh xac lan niem tin rong giup nhan ra can thiep sua van de nay nhung tao van de khac. before sharing a surprising post, a reader can pause and check the original source, publication date, location and independent reporting. search for the claim outside the page where it appeared; this reduces reliance on a post’s own presentation. images may be old or taken from another event, and a genuine quotation may be missing context. if the claim concerns health or public safety, consult a relevant expert agency rather than a viral comment. these habits are not a guarantee of certainty. they slow down impulsive sharing and make it more likely that a correction will be based on verifiable evidence rather than a competing rumour. truoc khi chia se bai gay bat ngo, nguoi doc co the dung lai va kiem tra nguon goc, ngay dang, dia diem va tin doc lap. tim tuyen bo ben ngoai trang noi no xuat hien de khong chi dua vao cach bai dang tu trinh bay. anh co the cu hoac lay tu su kien khac; trich dan that co the thieu ngu canh. neu tuyen bo lien quan suc khoe hay an toan cong cong, hay tim co quan chuyen mon phu hop thay vi binh luan lan truyen. cac thoi quen nay khong bao dam chac chan tuyet doi. chung lam cham chia se boc dong va tang kha nang dinh chinh dua tren bang chung kiem chung duoc thay vi tin don doi lap. effective responses combine clear evidence with respectful communication. people are less likely to engage if a correction humiliates them or attacks their identity. acknowledge uncertainty where it exists, explain what evidence would change the conclusion and update the correction if facts change. for schools, media and public agencies, media-literacy education can teach source checking and common manipulation tactics before a crisis occurs. in ielts writing, one can argue that fact-checking is essential but should be transparent and context-sensitive. the central lesson is to correct the claim and offer a credible replacement account, while checking that the intervention does not create sweeping distrust. phan hoi hieu qua ket hop bang chung ro voi giao tiep ton trong. nguoi ta it tuong tac neu phan dinh chinh lam nhuc ho hoac cong kich can tinh. hay thua nhan bat dinh hien huu, giai thich bang chung nao co the lam thay doi ket luan va cap nhat neu su that doi. truong, truyen thong va co quan cong co the day kiem tra nguon cung thu thuat thao tung pho bien truoc khung hoang. trong ielts, co the lap luan kiem chung rat can nhung phai minh bach va phu hop ngu canh. bai hoc la sua tuyen bo va dua loi giai thay the dang tin, dong thoi kiem tra can thiep khong tao hoai nghi bao trum.
social-isolation-networks: co lap xa hoi: khi mang luoi ket noi qua mong social isolation is a structural lack of contact co lap xa hoi mo ta ket noi han che; khac phuc thuong can co hoi tham gia va dich vu de tiep can. social isolation describes a limited number or frequency of social contacts. it is different from loneliness, which is the distress someone may feel when their relationships do not match what they want. a person can live alone and feel content, or have many acquaintances and still feel disconnected. measuring isolation may involve household status, contact frequency, network size and participation in community activities. no single measure captures every kind of relationship. this distinction matters because an intervention that creates more contact may help one person but feel intrusive or irrelevant to someone whose main need is a closer, more supportive relationship. co lap xa hoi mo ta so luong hoac tan suat tiep xuc xa hoi han che. no khac co don, la cam giac dau buon khi quan he hien co khong dap ung mong muon. mot nguoi song mot minh co the thay on, con nguoi nhieu nguoi quen van thay mat ket noi. do co lap co the xet tinh trang song, tan suat lien lac, quy mo mang luoi va tham gia hoat dong cong dong. khong phep do nao nam het moi dang quan he. phan biet nay quan trong vi can thiep tao them tiep xuc co the giup nguoi nay nhung gay kho chiu hoac khong lien quan voi nguoi can quan he gan gui, ho tro hon. social connection exists in different forms: close relationships, supportive friendships, family ties, work contacts and participation in groups. the number of contacts alone does not show whether they are safe, reciprocal or meaningful. a practical assessment asks who a person can call for help, whether they have regular opportunities to meet others and whether transport, disability, language or cost limits participation. isolation may result from bereavement, illness, caregiving, relocation or exclusion, so the cause differs by person. effective responses therefore begin by listening rather than assuming that everyone wants the same club, activity or amount of social contact. ket noi xa hoi co nhieu dang: quan he than thiet, ban be ho tro, gia dinh, dong nghiep va tham gia nhom. chi dem so lien he khong cho biet quan he co an toan, tuong ho hay y nghia khong. danh gia thuc te can hoi nguoi do co the goi ai khi can, co co hoi gap nguoi khac thuong xuyen khong, va di lai, khuyet tat, ngon ngu hay chi phi co can tro tham gia khong. co lap co the den tu tang che, benh tat, cham soc nguoi than, chuyen noi o hoac bi loai tru; nguyen nhan khac nhau. vi vay, phan ung hieu qua bat dau bang lang nghe thay vi gia dinh ai cung muon cung cau lac bo hay muc giao tiep. who’s 2025 commission on social connection framed social connection as a public-health and social issue, not merely a private feeling. its report calls for action across policy, research, intervention, measurement and public engagement. that broad agenda reflects how connection is shaped by homes, neighbourhoods, schools, workplaces, transport and digital services. a community centre cannot solve every barrier if a person cannot reach it, and an online group may not replace practical help. the report also encourages better data because countries use different measures. as of 2025, the key message is to treat connection as part of wellbeing tu. bao cao keu goi hanh dong ve chinh sach, nghien cuu, can thiep, do luong va tham gia cong chung. chuong trinh rong phan anh ket noi chiu anh huong tu nha o, khu pho, truong, noi lam viec, giao thong va dich vu so. trung tam cong dong khong giai quyet duoc moi rao can neu nguoi dan khong den duoc; nhom truc tuyen cung khong thay the tro giup thiet thuc. bao cao keu goi du lieu tot hon vi cac nuoc do khac nhau. tinh den 2025, thong diep la xem ket noi la mot phan cua phuc loi nhung tranh don gian hoa rang ai cung can giao tiep nhieu hon. public design can make everyday contact easier without forcing people into social activities. libraries, accessible parks, safe walking routes, community health services and affordable public transport create places where people can meet naturally. flexible opening hours matter for shift workers and caregivers. local organisations can offer low-pressure activities with a clear purpose, such as shared meals, skills classes or help with loneliness-and-health: co don la trai nghiem chu quan, khong phai so luong ban be loneliness and health are linked in complex ways who nam 2025 nhan manh tac dong suc khoe cua co don va co lap, dong thoi keu goi cach tiep can rong hon. loneliness is the distressing feeling that one’s social relationships are insufficient in quality or closeness. it is subjective: two people with the same number of contacts may feel very differently. someone may feel lonely in a busy household, while another person living alone feels connected through a few reliable relationships. loneliness can change over whether the feeling is persistent, unwanted and affecting wellbeing or daily life. co don la cam giac dau buon rang quan he xa hoi thieu ve chat luong hoac do than mat. day la trai nghiem chu quan: noi xa hoi who bao cao nam 2025 rang co don va co lap pho bien, anh huong suc khoe va xa hoi nhung chua duoc nhan dien du. bao cao lien he quan he xa hoi voi phuc loi va keu goi phoi hop dich vu y te, demographic-ageing: dan so gia hoa: thach thuc nam o cach xa hoi thich ung population ageing reshapes societies du bao 2024 cua lien hop quoc cho thay dan so va co cau tuoi thay doi khac nhau giua cac quoc gia. population ageing means that older age groups make up a larger share of a population, often because people live longer and have fewer children on average. it does not mean every country is shrinking or that older people are dependent. nations differ in timing, health, migration and economic conditions. the united nations’ world population prospects 2024 projects that global population may rise from about 8.2 billion in 2024 to roughly 10.3 billion in the mid-2080s, then gradually decline. this projection is not a certainty; it depends on assumptions about fertility, mortality and migration. the key change is increasingly diverse age structures across places. gia hoa dan so nghia la nhom tuoi cao chiem ty trong lon hon, thuong do nguoi song lau hon va so con trung binh giam. dieu do khong co nghia moi quoc gia deu suy giam dan so hay nguoi cao tuoi deu phu thuoc. cac nuoc khac nhau ve thoi diem, suc khoe, di cu va kinh te. trien vong dan so the gioi 2024 cua lien hop quoc du bao dan so toan cau co the tang tu khoang 8,2 ty nam 2024 len gan 10,3 ty vao giua thap nien 2080, roi giam dan. day khong phai dieu chac chan; du bao phu thuoc gia dinh ve sinh, tu va di cu. thay doi cot loi la co cau tuoi giua cac noi ngay cang da dang. a rising share of older residents can affect demand for health care, long-term support, accessible housing and transport. it may also change labour markets, family care responsibilities and the tax base. these effects are not determined by age structure alone. healthy life expectancy, employment opportunities, retirement rules, productivity and the design of public services all matter. older adults contribute as workers, caregivers, volunteers and family members, so a narrative that treats ageing only as a cost misses important value. planning should examine local needs and resources rather than assume a single “ageing crisis” will occur in the same way everywhere. ty trong nguoi cao tuoi tang co the anh huong nhu cau cham soc suc khoe, ho tro dai han, nha o va giao thong de tiep can. no cung doi thi truong lao dong, trach nhiem cham soc trong gia dinh va co so thue. tac dong khong do co cau tuoi quyet dinh mot minh. tuoi tho khoe manh, co hoi viec lam, quy dinh nghi huu, nang suat va thiet ke dich vu cong deu quan trong. nguoi lon tuoi dong gop voi vai tro lao dong, nguoi cham soc, tinh nguyen vien va thanh vien gia dinh; xem gia hoa chi la ganh nang bo sot gia tri. quy hoach nen xet nhu cau va nguon luc dia phuong thay vi gia dinh mot “khung hoang gia hoa” giong nhau khap noi. the 2024 united nations projections also show why global averages can mislead. some countries have already passed their population peak; others are growing rapidly and have younger populations. in some places, international migration is projected to offset population decline, while elsewhere it makes a smaller difference. a national average can conceal regional contrasts, such as young adults leaving rural areas while cities age differently. policymakers should use age-specific and local data, state the projection year and compare alternative scenarios. a projection is a planning tool, not a forecast of exactly what will happen. new fertility or migration trends can change the path. du bao lien hop quoc nam 2024 cung cho thay trung binh toan cau de gay hieu lam. mot so nuoc da qua dinh dan so; noi khac tang nhanh va co dan so tre hon. o mot so noi, di cu quoc te duoc du bao bu suy giam, con noi khac tac dong nho hon. trung binh quoc gia co the che tuong phan vung mien, nhu nguoi tre roi nong thon trong khi do thi gia hoa theo cach khac. nha hoach dinh nen dung du lieu theo tuoi va dia phuong, neu nam du bao va so kich ban thay the. du bao la cong cu hoach dinh, khong phai khang dinh chinh xac tuong lai. xu huong sinh hay di cu moi co the doi duong di. an ageing society can respond by making work and care more adaptable. lifelong learning can help people update skills, while flexible working arrangements may allow some older adults to remain employed if they choose. accessible streets, housing modifications and primary care can support independence. families may need affordable respite and long-term care services rather than relying entirely on unpaid relatives. these measures benefit people with disabilities and parents of young children too. the aim is not to make everyone work longer or remain at home; it is to create choices and ensure support is available when needed. policies should be shaped with older people, not only for them. xa hoi gia hoa co the ung pho bang cach lam cong viec va cham soc linh hoat hon. hoc suot doi giup cap nhat ky nang; che do lam linh hoat cho phep mot so nguoi lon tuoi tiep tuc lam neu ho muon. duong pho de tiep can, cai tao nha va cham soc ban dau ho tro tu chu. gia dinh co the can dich vu nghi thay va cham soc dai han gia hop ly, thay vi hoan toan dua vao nguoi than khong luong. cac bien phap cung giup nguoi khuyet tat va cha me con nho. muc tieu khong phai buoc ai cung lam lau hon hay o nha, ma tao lua chon va bao dam ho tro khi can. chinh sach nen duoc xay cung nguoi cao tuoi, khong chi danh cho ho. public finance debates often focus on pensions and health budgets, but the balance depends on policy choices and economic participation. preventive care may help preserve function, although it cannot eliminate all illness or care needs. a larger older population can also create demand for new services, products and jobs. fair discussion looks at who provides care, how it is funded and whether workers can access decent jobs. intergenerational fairness does not require setting young and old against one another; both groups depend on stable families, services and opportunities. transparent long-term projections can make trade-offs visible and encourage adjustments before systems face acute pressure. tranh luan tai chinh cong thuong tap trung luong huu va ngan sach y te, nhung can doi phu thuoc lua chon chinh sach va tham gia kinh te. cham soc phong ngua co the duy tri chuc nang, du khong xoa moi benh tat hay nhu cau cham soc. dan so lon tuoi hon cung tao nhu cau dich vu, san pham va nghe nghiep moi. thao luan cong bang xet ai cung cap cham soc, nguon tai chinh tu dau va nguoi lao dong co viec tu te khong. cong bang lien the he khong doi hoi dat tre va gia doi dau; ca hai can gia dinh, dich vu va co hoi on dinh. du bao dai han minh bach giup thay danh doi va dieu chinh truoc khi he thong chiu ap luc lon. the un’s 2024 projection is best treated as a range of possible futures informed by current demographic data. governments can prepare for longer lives by reducing age discrimination, making communities accessible and aligning health and care services with actual needs. individuals can plan financially and maintain social ties, but policy should not transfer all responsibility to households. in ielts writing, a strong response avoids claiming that ageing inevitably causes economic decline. outcomes depend on health, productivity, inclusion and support systems. the central question is how societies can help people live longer lives with autonomy and dignity while sharing care fairly across generations. du bao 2024 cua lien hop quoc nen duoc xem nhu cac tuong lai co the xay ra dua tren du lieu dan so hien tai. chinh phu co the chuan bi cho tuoi tho dai hon bang cach giam phan biet tuoi tac, lam cong dong de tiep can va dieu chinh y te, cham soc theo nhu cau that. ca nhan co the hoach dinh tai chinh va giu quan he xa hoi, nhung chinh sach khong nen chuyen het trach nhiem cho ho gia dinh. trong ielts, tranh khang dinh gia hoa tat yeu gay suy thoai kinh te. ket qua phu thuoc suc khoe, nang suat, hoa nhap va he thong ho tro. cau hoi cot loi la xa hoi giup nguoi dan song lau hon tu chu, co pham gia va chia se cham soc cong bang giua the he ra sao.
fertility-transitions: ty suat sinh giam khong tao mot ket qua duy nhat fertility transitions reshape age structures du lieu lien hop quoc nam 2024 cho thay nhieu nuoc duoi muc thay the, nhung chinh sach can xet dong luc dia phuong. fertility transition describes a long-term shift from high birth rates toward smaller family sizes. it usually accompanies changes in child survival, education, urbanisation, employment, access to health care and people’s ability to decide whether and when to have children. the pattern differs across countries and is not a simple story of one cause. some populations remain young because of past high fertility even after birth rates fall; others age quickly. the un’s world population prospects 2024 reports that more than half of countries and areas were below the approximate replacement level of 2.1 births per woman, although migration and mortality also shape population size. chuyen tiep muc sinh mo ta thay doi dai han tu ty le sinh cao sang gia dinh it con hon. qua trinh thuong di cung cai thien song sot tre em, giao duc, do thi hoa, viec lam, tiep can y te va kha nang quyet dinh co con khi nao. mau hinh khac nhau giua nuoc va khong phai cau chuyen mot nguyen nhan. mot so dan so van tre do muc sinh cao trong qua khu du hien tai da giam; noi khac gia hoa nhanh. trien vong dan so the gioi 2024 cua lien hop quoc cho biet hon nua quoc gia va vung lanh tho duoi muc thay the xap xi 2,1 con moi phu nu, du di cu va tu vong cung dinh hinh quy mo dan so. replacement-level fertility is a useful demographic benchmark: roughly the level at which a population would eventually replace itself in the absence of migration, under assumptions about mortality and sex ratio at birth. it is not a target that every family should meet, nor does a rate below 2.1 cause immediate population decline. age structure creates momentum. a large generation entering childbearing ages can keep births numerous even when each woman has fewer children, while a small generation can produce fewer births despite a similar rate. population projections therefore examine both fertility rates and the number and age of people likely to have children. muc sinh thay the la chuan nhan khau hoc huu ich: xap xi muc dan so thay the chinh no ve lau dai neu khong co di cu, voi gia dinh ve tu vong va ty le gioi tinh khi sinh. day khong phai muc tieu moi gia dinh can dat; ty suat duoi 2,1 cung khong lap tuc lam dan so giam. co cau tuoi tao da. the he lon buoc vao tuoi sinh con co the khien tong ca sinh van nhieu du moi phu nu sinh it hon; the he nho hon co the tao it ca sinh du ty suat tuong tu. vi vay du bao dan so xet ca ty suat sinh lan so luong, do tuoi nguoi co kha nang sinh con. in 2024, the un reported substantial variation in fertility: many countries were below replacement, and some had very low rates, while other populations remained much younger. a global average can hide these differences. the report also projects that international migration will be a major driver of future population growth in some countries. these figures are estimates and projections, not a verdict on a society’s future. they depend on assumptions and can change as new census, birth-registration and migration data become available. when quoting a fertility statistic, specify the country, year and measure; do not treat it as a timeless cultural fact. nam 2024, lien hop quoc bao cao muc sinh khac biet dang ke: nhieu nuoc duoi muc thay the, mot so rat thap, trong khi dan so noi khac con tre hon. trung binh the gioi che khuat khac biet do. bao cao con du bao di cu quoc te la dong luc tang dan so chinh o mot so nuoc. con so la uoc tinh va du bao, khong phai phan quyet tuong lai xa hoi. chung phu thuoc gia dinh va co the doi khi du lieu dieu tra dan so, dang ky sinh va di cu moi xuat hien. khi trich so lieu sinh, hay neu quoc gia, nam va thuoc do; dung xem do la su that van hoa bat bien. fertility choices are shaped by both personal preferences and constraints. people may delay or avoid parenthood because of housing costs, insecure work, unequal caregiving, health concerns or a lack of suitable childcare; others may freely prefer smaller families. these factors interact, and not every person responds in the same way. governments should avoid coercive policies that pressure people to have more or fewer children. a rights-based approach supports reproductive health, affordable childcare, equal opportunity and economic security while leaving decisions with individuals and families. policies should be evaluated by whether they expand people’s choices, not only by whether a birth-rate target moves. lua chon sinh con chiu anh huong so thich ca nhan va rang buoc thuc te. nguoi ta co the tri hoan hoac khong sinh vi nha o dat, viec lam bap benh, cham soc bat binh dang, lo suc khoe hay thieu dich vu trong tre; nguoi khac tu nguyen muon gia dinh nho. yeu to tuong tac va moi nguoi phan ung khac nhau. chinh phu nen tranh chinh sach cuong ep gay ap luc phai sinh nhieu hay it. cach tiep can dua tren quyen ho tro suc khoe sinh san, cham soc tre gia hop ly, co hoi binh dang va an toan kinh te, dong thoi de ca nhan, gia dinh quyet dinh. danh gia chinh sach theo viec mo rong lua chon chu khong chi chi tieu ty le sinh. a lower birth rate can alter the ratio between working-age people and dependants, but this ratio does not by itself determine prosperity. investment in education, health, decent jobs, productivity and gender equality influences whether a country can benefit from its age structure. in some settings, a growing working-age share may create a demographic dividend; in others, unemployment or limited opportunities can prevent that potential from being realised. ageing later requires planning for care and pensions, while a youthful population needs education and employment. there is no universal “ideal” population size. policy must respond to the stage and needs of each society. ty le sinh thap hon co the doi ty le giua nguoi trong do tuoi lao dong va nguoi phu thuoc, nhung ty le nay khong tu quyet dinh thinh vuong. dau tu giao duc, y te, viec lam tu te, nang suat va binh dang gioi anh huong kha nang tan dung co cau tuoi. o vai noi, ty trong nguoi lao dong tang co the tao loi tuc dan so; o noi khac, that nghiep hay thieu co hoi ngan tiem nang thanh hien thuc. gia hoa sau nay doi hoi hoach dinh cham soc va huu tri; dan so tre can giao duc va viec lam. khong co quy mo dan so “ly tuong” chung. chinh sach phai phan ung voi giai doan va nhu cau tung xa hoi. a careful discussion separates fertility rates, total births, population growth and family size. they are related but not interchangeable measures. a country can have low fertility and still grow because of migration or age structure; another can have a higher rate but fewer total births because its population is smaller. the un’s 2024 projections provide an updated global baseline, while national data are needed for local planning. in ielts writing, it is stronger to discuss housing, childcare, work security and personal choice than to blame a single generation. fertility change is a demographic process; how societies respond is a matter of rights, opportunity and planning. thao luan can trong phan biet ty suat sinh, tong so ca sinh, tang dan so va quy mo gia dinh. chung lien quan nhung khong the thay the nhau. mot nuoc co muc sinh thap van tang dan so nho di cu hoac co cau tuoi; noi khac ty suat cao hon nhung tong ca sinh it hon vi dan so nho. du bao un 2024 cung cap moc toan cau moi, con hoach dinh dia phuong can du lieu quoc gia. trong ielts, thao luan nha o, cham soc tre, on dinh viec lam va quyen lua chon tot hon do loi mot the he. thay doi muc sinh la qua trinh nhan khau; phan ung cua xa hoi lien quan quyen, co hoi va hoach dinh.
migration-integration: hoi nhap nguoi di cu can nhieu hon viec tim duoc viec lam migrant integration has many dimensions oecd 2025 nhan manh ket qua lao dong cua nguoi di cu khac nhau giua cac nuoc va can xem xet nhieu chi bao. migration moves people across borders for work, safety, family, education or other reasons. integration describes how newcomers and established residents participate in society over time; it is not the same as assimilation, which can imply giving up cultural identity. integration has several dimensions, including language access, education, employment, housing, health care, civic participation and a sense of belonging. a person may do well in one area and face barriers in another. for example, a highly educated newcomer may find work below their qualifications because credentials are not recognised. looking at only one measure can therefore give an incomplete picture of inclusion. di cu dua con nguoi qua bien gioi de lam viec, an toan, gia dinh, hoc tap hoac ly do khac. hoi nhap mo ta cach nguoi moi den va cu dan lau nam tham gia xa hoi theo thoi gian; khac dong hoa, von co the ham y tu bo ban sac van hoa. hoi nhap nhieu chieu, gom tiep can ngon ngu, giao duc, viec lam, nha o, y te, tham gia cong dan va cam giac thuoc ve. mot nguoi co the thuan loi o mat nay nhung gap rao can o mat khac. chang han, nguoi moi den co hoc van cao van lam duoi trinh do vi bang cap chua duoc cong nhan. chi xem mot thuoc do se cho buc tranh chua day du. oecd’s international migration outlook 2025 reported mixed labour-market trends for immigrants in 2024: employment rates improved further in only about half of oecd countries. the 2025 edition also examined how firms contribute to immigrant integration and the migration of health professionals. these findings are time-specific and apply to oecd settings; they should not be presented as a global rule. employment matters, but job quality, pay, security and skills use also matter. a person employed in unstable work may still face exclusion or underuse of qualifications. good comparisons state the year, destination country and indicator rather than relying on broad claims that migration always helps or harms an economy. trien vong di cu quoc te oecd 2025 bao cao xu huong lao dong cua nguoi di cu trong nam 2024 khong dong nhat: ty le co viec tiep tuc tang o khoang mot nua so nuoc quan trong, nhung chat luong, luong, on dinh va su dung ky nang cung vay. nguoi co viec bap benh van co the bi loai tru hoac khong dung het bang cap. so sanh tot neu nam, nuoc den va chi bao thay vi intergenerational-mobility: co hoi cua con cai khong chi phu thuoc no luc intergenerational mobility and opportunity nghien cuu oecd nam 2026 dung khao sat ky nang nguoi truong thanh de so sanh muc do ket qua xa hoi gan voi xuat than cha me. intergenerational mobility describes how a person’s social or economic position compares with that of their parents. researchers may study income, education, occupation, health or social class. absolute mobility asks whether people do better than their parents in a particular measure; relative mobility asks how strongly a person’s rank is associated with family background. a society can have rising average income while relative mobility remains limited. these definitions matter because slogans about “moving up” often mix different outcomes. mobility is not a direct measure of whether every person has equal opportunity, but it helps reveal how strongly early-life circumstances shape later possibilities. dich chuyen lien the he mo ta vi tri xa hoi hoac kinh te cua mot nguoi so voi cha me. nha nghien cuu co the xet thu nhap, hoc van, nghe nghiep, suc khoe hoac tang lop. dich chuyen tuyet doi hoi nguoi tre co lam tot hon cha me theo thuoc do nao do khong; dich chuyen tuong doi hoi thu hang ca nhan lien he chat den dau voi xuat than. xa hoi co the tang thu nhap trung binh nhung dich chuyen tuong doi van han che. dinh nghia quan trong vi khau hieu “doi doi” thuong tron cac ket qua khac nhau. dich chuyen khong truc tiep do co hoi binh dang cho moi nguoi, nhung giup thay hoan canh dau doi dinh hinh kha nang tuong lai manh den dau. the oecd generations in participating countries. the new analysis offers a timely comparison, but its coverage and measures should be read carefully: a survey of adults cannot capture every life pathway, and countries differ in institutions and data quality. the results are not a ranking of individual effort. they help identify whether family background remains associated with later outcomes and where education, training or labour-market policies might widen opportunity. oecd cong bo nghien cuu lien quoc gia ve dich chuyen xa hoi giua the he nam 2026, su dung khao sat ky nang nguoi truong thanh. nghien cuu xem xet mau hinh hoc van va ket qua xa hoi lien he giua cac the he o nuoc tham gia. phan tich moi giup so sanh kip thoi, nhung can doc ky pham vi va thuoc do: khao sat nguoi truong thanh khong nam moi con duong doi, con the che va chat luong du lieu moi nuoc khac nhau. ket qua khong phai bang xep hang no luc ca nhan. chung giup nhan dien xuat than gia dinh con lien quan ket qua ve sau khong va chinh sach giao duc, dao tao hay lao dong co the mo rong co hoi o dau. family resources can affect a child through several routes: access to safe housing, nutrition, time, books, networks, tutoring and schools. parents’ education may also influence their familiarity with institutions and ability to navigate applications. these pathways do not determine an individual’s future, but they scholarships and supportive mentors can interrupt the link between background and outcomes. a useful explanation focuses on structures and mechanisms rather than assuming success or poverty reflects character alone. nguon luc gia dinh anh huong tre qua nhieu duong: nha an toan, dinh duong, thoi gian, sach, mang luoi, gia su va truong hoc. hoc van cha me cung anh huong hieu biet ve the che va kha nang xu ly thu tuc. nhung con duong nay khong dinh doat tuong lai ca nhan nhung co the tich luy loi the hoac bat loi. tre co tai van gap rao can neu phai di lam, thieu phuong tien hoac hoc o truong thieu nguon luc. nguoc lai, giao duc cong, hoc bong va co van ho tro co the cat lien he giua xuat than va ket qua. giai thich huu ich tap trung vao co che cau truc thay vi cho rang thanh cong hay ngheo kho chi phan anh tinh cach. education is important, but schooling alone does not guarantee mobility. quality, completion, subject choice, career guidance and the link between qualifications and available jobs all matter. if access to high-quality early education is unequal, later examinations may reproduce earlier differences. training can help adults adapt to economic change, although pathway from childhood to work, not only enrolment rates. tracking who benefits from programmes can reveal whether support reaches people with fewer initial advantages. giao duc quan trong nhung rieng viec di hoc khong bao dam dich chuyen. chat luong, hoan tat, lua chon mon, huong nghiep va lien he giua bang cap voi viec lam deu quan trong. neu tiep can giao duc dau doi chat luong khong cong bang, nha cung han che lua chon sau hoc. chinh sach nen xet toan bo duong di tu tuoi tho den viec lam, khong chi ty le nhap hoc. theo doi ai duoc loi giup biet ho tro co den nhom it loi the ban dau khong. incentives influence what people see. in an ai-shaped information environment, a realistic skill is not spotting every fake image by eye; synthetic content can look convincing, and authentic content mot ty bua an bi lang phi moi ngay nam 2022 o ho gia dinh, dich vu an uong va ban le. ho gia dinh chiem khoang 60% luong lang phi duoc do, phan con lai tu dich vu an va ban le. day la uoc tinh toan don va lua chon khau phan. quyen gop huu ich nhung can kho lanh, van chuyen on dinh va kiem soat an toan. no khong nen tro thanh ly do tiep tuc san xuat du. ngan du thua tai nguon thuong tranh nhieu so u compost hoac phan huy ky khi xu ly duoc. thu gom rieng ngan mot phan thuc an vao bai chon lap, du xu ly van dung nang luong va can kiem soat mui, nhiem ban. food-waste policy also needs to packaging-reuse-systems: he thong bao bi tai su dung va dieu kien hieu qua making packaging reuse systems work quy dinh bao bi eu 2025/40 bat dau ap dung tu thang 8/2026, mo rong muc tieu giam rac va usually has a higher manufacturing footprint than a disposable equivalent, so it must complete enough safe trips to repay that initial impact. the result depends on material, washing, transport avoid collecting unnecessary personal data. successful reuse depends on service design as much as the container itself. he thong tai dung can diem tra tien loi, tien dat coc hay uu dai ro, phan loai, backside-power-delivery: cap dien tu mat sau: giai phong khong gian day noi tren chip backside power delivery: freeing frontside wiring giai thich vi sao dua mang cap nguon xuong mat sau wafer co the giam nghen day; xem powervia nhu trien khai thuong mai cua intel 2024, cung chi phi xu ly wafer va gioi han loi ich. a modern chip carries power and data through dense metal wiring above its transistors. as wiring layers become crowded, power lines compete with signal routes for space, and voltage drop can harm timing. backside power delivery moves much of the power network to the wafer’s rear surface, leaving the frontside wiring stack more room for signals. intel described powervia as its backside-power technology and said it would enter manufacturing with its intel 20a node in 2024. that is a company-specific implementation milestone; the general design principle is useful across the industry, but adoption and measured gains vary. chip hien dai dan dien nguon va du lieu qua cac lop day kim loai day phia tren transistor. khi lop day chat, duong nguon canh tranh cho voi tin hieu va sut ap co the lam sai thoi gian. cap nguon mat sau chuyen phan lon mang nguon ra mat sau wafer, de mat truoc co them cho cho tin hieu. intel mo ta powervia la cong nghe cap nguon mat sau va cho biet dua vao san xuat cung nut intel 20a nam 2024. do la cot moc trien khai rieng cua cong ty; nguyen ly thiet ke co ich cho ca nganh nhung muc ap dung va loi ich do duoc khac nhau. the process typically requires thinning a wafer and making small connections that pass through silicon to join frontside devices with backside metal. alignment must be precise because each contact must land on its intended electrical region. thin wafers are harder to handle, and additional processing can create contamination, stress, or defects. designers also divide responsibility between frontside signal routing and backside power delivery, which means the chip architecture, standard-cell libraries, and design tools must support the change. it is not a simple final-layer swap: the whole design and fabrication flow must be co-optimised. quy trinh thuong can lam mong wafer va tao ket noi nho xuyen silicon de noi linh kien phia truoc voi kim loai mat sau. can chinh phai chinh xac vi moi tiep diem can cham dung vung dien. wafer mong kho xu ly hon; noncarbonate-cement-feedstocks: xi mang tu khoang khong carbonat: thay doi nguyen lieu nen non-carbonate cement feedstocks: changing the raw materials gioi thieu lo trinh san xuat chat ket dinh tu nguyen lieu khong phai da voi nham tranh co2 phan ung; phan biet du an brimstone 2024 voi san pham thuong mai va yeu cau khoang, hoa hoc, tieu chuan. most portland cement clinker begins with limestone, which releases carbon dioxide when calcium carbonate is heated and decomposes. one alternative research pathway uses non-carbonate calcium silicate rocks as feedstock, aiming to make cement chemistry without that process-emission step. in 2024, the u.s. department of energy described a commercial-scale demonstration project led by brimstone that planned to make ordinary portland cement and supplementary materials from alternative mineral inputs. it was a proposed demonstration, not proof that the process has reached sustained commercial production. the scientific question is whether the raw materials can yield standard cement phases consistently. phan lon clinker portland bat dau tu da voi, giai phong co2 khi nung phan huy calcium carbonate. mot lo trinh nghien cuu khac dung da calcium silicate khong carbonat, nham tao hoa hoc xi mang ma tranh buoc phat thai quy trinh do. nam 2024, bo nang luong hoa ky mo ta du an trinh dien quy mo thuong mai do brimstone dan dau, du kien san xuat xi mang portland thong thuong cung vat lieu bo sung tu khoang thay the. do la du an trinh dien duoc de xuat, khong chung minh san xuat thuong mai lien tuc. cau hoi khoa hoc la lieu nguyen lieu co tao pha xi mang chuan on dinh khong. the feedstock must contain the needed elements in proportions that allow clinker minerals to form after heating. a manufacturer may need to mine, crush, separate, and blend different rocks, then control kiln chemistry and cooling. silicate minerals behave differently from limestone and clay; sat, du an doe 2024 ve quang va nuoc bien; phan tich dien cuc, nang luong, chat luong sat, quy mo va chua truong thanh thuong mai. electrochemical ironmaking seeks to use electrical current to remove oxygen from iron oxide, producing iron without relying on coke as the chemical reductant. the exact route varies: some concepts dissolve iron species in an electrolyte, while others use solid-state or molten electrolysis. doe documented a 2024 project to test electrodes and ore refinement for producing iron from different oxides using electrochemical methods. this is early process development, not equal plant energy use because pumps, heating, separation, and gas handling also consume power. a process that produces clean iron slowly may require a large cell farm and expensive materials. defect. in february 2025, imec reported electrical test results on 20-nanometre-pitch metal lines patterned with a single high-na euv exposure. the result validated an early ecosystem, not a anh ve tinh mo rong pham vi nhung khong thay kiem tra hien truong. after an earthquake, responders need to know where the rupture occurred, which areas shook strongly, and where roads or buildings may be damaged. satellite imagery offers a wide view when ground access is blocked or dangerous. optical sensors show visible changes such as fresh landslides, collapsed roofs, or surface rupture, while radar can collect data through clouds and at night. comparing images acquired before and after the event reveals change over large areas. the result is not automatically a building-by-building safety inspection; energy, its heat output can exceed the electricity it consumes; the ratio is called a coefficient of performance. this does not mean performance is constant: outdoor temperature, defrost cycles, duct leakage, controls, and installation quality all change the seasonal result. a product label is a starting point, not a forecast for every house. may bom nhiet van chuyen nhiet thay vi tao nhiet bang capacity, sometimes allowing a smaller unit. but sealing a home without considering ventilation can trap moisture and indoor pollutants. a sound retrofit therefore coordinates insulation, controlled ventilation, and heating equipment. in an older house, a room-by-room heat-loss calculation is more useful than copying the capacity of a neighbor’s system, because floor area alone does not describe the load. lop vo cong trinh quyet dinh he thong suoi phai hoat dong vat va den dau. vat lieu cach nhiet lam cham nhiet thoat qua mai va tuong; bit kin khe ho giam gio lua; kich thuoc cua so va mai che bills. good selection uses local design temperatures and manufacturer performance tables, not only a mild-weather efficiency rating. the u.s. department of energy’s purchasing guidance, updated in wildfire-smoke-clean-room: ung pho voi khoi chay rung ngay trong nha building a cleaner-air room during wildfire smoke khoi chay rung co the lot vao nha va mang theo bui min. ket hop canh bao chat luong khong khi, loc phu hop, giam nguon o nhiem trong nha va ke hoach lam mat an toan. wildfire smoke is a changing mixture of gases and particles. fine particulate matter, often called pm2.5, can travel deep into the respiratory system, and smoke may drift far beyond the burn area. staying indoors can lower exposure, but a closed home is not automatically clean: smoke enters through gaps, open doors, and ventilation intakes. the u.s. environmental protection agency’s cleaner-air guidance, updated in 2026, recommends preparing a room where people can spend time with windows and doors closed and an appropriately sized air cleaner operating. local air-quality alerts help determine when to use that room. khoi chay rung la hon hop thay doi gom khi va hat bui. bui min thuong goi la pm2.5 co the di sau vao he ho hap, va khoi co the bay xa khoi khu vuc chay. o trong nha co the giam muc phoi nhiem, nhung nha dong kin khong mac nhien sach: khoi lot qua khe ho, cua mo va cua lay gio thong gio. huong dan tao khong gian khong khi sach hon cua co quan bao ve moi truong hoa ky, duoc cap nhat nam 2026, khuyen chuan bi mot phong de moi nguoi o trong khi dong cua so, cua ra vao va bat may loc co cong suat phu hop. canh bao chat luong khong khi dia phuong giup xac dinh luc nao can dung can phong nay. choose the room before smoke arrives. a smaller room with few windows and doors is easier to clean than a large open-plan space. make it comfortable enough to use: keep water, chargers, medication people already use, and activities nearby, while ensuring exits remain accessible. place a portable cleaner where air can circulate around its intake and outlet; do not hide it behind furniture. a clean-air room is a temporary exposure-reduction measure, not a sealed shelter for every emergency. if a fire threatens the property, evacuation instructions and immediate safety take priority over staying indoors to filter air. hay chon phong truoc khi khoi tran den. phong nho co it cua so va cua ra vao thuong de loc hon khong gian rong thong suot. bo tri du tien nghi de co the o lau: nuoc uong, bo sac, thuoc nguoi trong nha von dang su dung va hoat dong giai tri; during a smoky episode, postpone them when practical. keep doors and windows closed while outdoor air is poor, but reopen and ventilate when conditions improve, particularly if indoor heat or pollutants build up. air conditioners usually cool rather than remove fine particles, so check whether they draw outdoor air. a fan alone does not filter smoke. monitor both outdoor conditions and indoor comfort because a tightly closed room can become dangerously hot. if heat and smoke occur together, seek a cooled cleaner-air location when home equipment cannot manage both risks. hoat dong trong nha cung co the lam giam hieu qua loc. hut thuoc, thuoc la dien tu, nen, chien ran va mot so binh xit ve sinh tao them hat hoac khi; smart-device-update-lifecycle: danh gia thiet bi thong minh qua thoi han cap nhat phan mem smart devices need a clear software-support life thiet bi ket noi van co the hoat dong sau khi nha san xuat ngung cap nhat, nhung rui ro bao mat va mat tinh nang tang. nguoi mua nen kiem tra thoi han ho tro, du lieu thu thap va kha nang dung ngoai tuyen. a connected appliance is partly a software product. a doorbell, camera, thermostat, or speaker may depend on cloud services, an account, and an app that changes over time. security updates repair newly discovered weaknesses; compatibility updates help devices continue working with phones and routers. when support ends, the product may still switch on, but it can become easier to attack or lose remote features. the federal trade commission warned consumers in november 2024 that manufacturers do not always make support duration obvious. a device’s useful life should therefore include the promised software-support period, not only the physical warranty. thiet bi gia dung ket noi mot phan la san pham phan mem. chuong cua, camera, bo dieu nhiet hay loa co the phu thuoc dich vu dam may, tai khoan va ung dung thay doi theo thoi gian. ban cap nhat bao mat sua cac lo hong moi duoc phat hien; moi moc tao ra thoi gian ho tro con lai khac nhau doi voi mau cu duoc giam gia. dong thoi kiem tra cam ket ho tro phan mem co duoc ghi bang van ban khong, tinh nang thiet yeu co hoat dong khi khong dang ky thue bao khong, va ung dung co tuong thich voi he dieu hanh dien thoai hien tai khong. neu nguoi ban khong tra loi duoc, hay xem su khong chac chan la mot chi phi khi so sanh san pham. data collection is another part of the life-cycle decision. a camera may process video locally or upload clips to a cloud account;
