tro ly giong noi co the luu ban ghi hoac nhat ky tuong tac. hay doc phan kiem soat quyen rieng tu de biet du lieu nao duoc thu thap, luu trong bao lau, co duoc chia se hay khong va cach xoa du lieu. dung mat khau rieng biet, bat xac thuc nhieu yeu to neu co va bao ve bo dinh tuyen tai nha. ftc khuyen nguoi dung tan dung tinh nang bao mat cua thiet bi va duy tri phan mem moi. nhung buoc nay giam rui ro co the tranh, nhung khong khien thiet bi ket noi mien nhiem voi loi hoac ngan duoc moi hinh thuc su dung du lieu sai muc dich. a home network is safer when devices are separated by purpose. if a router supports a guest or internet-of-things network, placing cameras and appliances there can limit their access to computers containing financial or work files. change default passwords, disable remote access that is not needed, and install updates through the official app or manufacturer site. if support ends, consider disconnecting a device from the internet while retaining local functions, if the product permits it. do not assume that a factory reset removes account data stored by the company; many cases. if a system labels 100 answers as “80% confident,” roughly 80 should be correct for that confidence level to be calibrated. a fluent language model may produce confident wording without a well-grounded probability of truth. in 2024, emnlp research proposed methods to elicit and assess language-model confidence, showing that confidence estimation is an active technical problem. the selective-prediction-abstention: ai biet tu choi luc can: selective prediction va nguong chuyen nguoi selective prediction: when an ai should abstain phan tich he thong tra loi hoac abstain, do bao phu–rui ro va chi phi tu choi; dua tren nghien cuu neurips 2024 ve token “i don’t know”, phan biet co che ky thuat voi hanh vi trien khai. a prediction system does not always need to answer every question. selective prediction lets it provide an answer when its estimated risk is acceptable and abstain otherwise. in a chat product, abstention might mean asking for a missing detail, saying it lacks evidence, or routing the case to a person. a neurips 2024 paper studied explicit uncertainty modelling with an “i don’t know” token and evaluated whether models could express uncertainty on factual tasks. this research direction matters because a graceful refusal can be safer than a confident guess, though excessive refusal can make a tool unusable. he thong du doan khong phai luc nao cung can tra loi moi cau hoi. du doan co chon loc cho phep tra loi khi rui ro uoc luong chap nhan duoc, con lai thi tu choi. trong san pham chat, tu choi co the la hoi them chi tiet, noi thieu bang chung hay chuyen cho nguoi. bai neurips 2024 nghien cuu mo hinh hoa bat dinh tuong minh bang token “i don’t know” va danh gia mo hinh co the the hien bat dinh tren tac vu thuc te khong. huong nay quan trong vi tu choi dung luc an toan hon doan chac, du tu choi qua nhieu khien cong cu kho dung. a selective system needs an answer policy and a threshold. if a model estimates that an answer has a 60% chance of being correct, the product might answer only when the threshold is 90%, depending on consequences. the threshold is not a universal constant; no phan anh chi phi tra loi sai, nang luc ra soat va ky vong nguoi dung. chatbot du lich co the hoi lam ro ngay mo ho, con cong cu phan loai khan cap can quy tac chuyen cap nghiem. nhom nen xac dinh truoc ket qua nao la tra loi, tu choi hay ban giao roi moi do hieu nang. two quantities describe the trade-off: coverage, the fraction of cases answered, and selective risk, the error rate among answered cases. raising the threshold usually lowers coverage and may lower risk, but only if confidence meaningfully ranks correctness. report a risk–coverage curve rather than one threshold score. also track the types of cases rejected: if the system abstains disproportionately on dialects or people with disabilities, it may shift work onto those users. fairness analysis should therefore include both errors and non-answers, plus the quality and timeliness of human support. hai dai luong mo ta danh doi: do bao phu la phan truong hop duoc tra loi; multiple answers may repeat the same error; and an estimator can fail under distribution shift. a refusal policy can also be gamed by an attacker who phrases a harmful request as a harmless one. the system needs evaluation on both answerable and unanswerable questions, including ambiguous and adversarial cases. tu choi co the trien khai nhieu cach. mo hinh hoc token bat dinh rieng, tao loi de dat, so nhieu dap an mau hay dung bo uoc luong tu tin rieng. moi cach co diem yeu. “toi khong chac” co the chi la van phong, khong duoc hieu chuan; long-horizon-agent-reliability: agent ai lam viec dai han: xac suat hoan thanh giam the nao qua nhieu buoc long-horizon agent reliability: small errors accumulate giai thich danh gia agent theo thoi gian hoan thanh nhiem vu, loi tich luy va phu thuoc cong cu; dung metr time horizon 2025 va gioi han chuyen tu benchmark sang cong viec that. an ai agent may need to perform many actions—open files, inspect evidence, edit code, run tests, and report results—before a task is complete. reliability over a long sequence is different from success on a single prompt. if each action has a 95% chance of being correct and the task needs 20 dependent actions, the chance that every step succeeds can be much lower than 95%. metr’s 2025 time-horizon work measures the task duration at which an agent is estimated to succeed at a chosen reliability level. it provides a useful lens, not a universal forecast for all occupations. agent ai co the can nhieu hanh dong—mo tep, kiem tra bang chung, sua ma, chay thu va bao ket qua—truoc khi hoan tat. do tin cay qua chuoi dai khac thanh cong mot loi nhac. neu moi hanh dong co 95% kha nang dung va tac vu can 20 buoc phu thuoc, kha nang moi buoc deu thanh cong thap hon nhieu. nghien cuu time-horizon cua metr nam 2025 do thoi luong tac vu ma agent uoc tinh hoan thanh o muc tin cay chon truoc. day la goc nhin huu ich, khong phai du bao chung cho moi nghe. long tasks amplify several weaknesses: forgotten constraints, mistaken assumptions, tool failures, and difficulty noticing that an earlier action changed the environment. a coding agent can pass an initial test, modify a dependency, and later discover the build is broken. a research agent may collect many sources but overlook that two webpages repeat the same original report. the longer the chain, the more opportunities for an error to propagate. this does not mean every long task must fail; can do tin cay o cap toan tac vu, gom phuc hoi va xac minh. metr-style task-duration estimates require a defined task set, human completion-time measurements, model versions, agent scaffolding, and a success criterion. a “one-hour task” means that domain experts took around that long under the study’s protocol; khong co nghia moi lao dong hay tac vu kho nhu nhau. hieu nang agent con tuy cong cu, loi nhac, ngan sach tinh toan va so lan thu lai cho phep. doi dieu kien se doi thoi han do. bao cao tot xem ket qua la bang chung co dieu kien va giai thich thiet lap, khong chi trich con so thoi gian lon. a robust evaluation includes tasks with varied lengths and failure modes. researchers can record partial completion, correctness, efficiency, and whether the agent recognises uncertainty. a simple success/failure label may conceal whether the system completed 95% of a workflow or made no useful progress. repeated trials matter because agent behaviour can vary with sampling and tool responses. for consequential settings, run a task with realistic interruptions, ambiguous instructions, and missing information. measure not only “can it finish?” but also “can it detect a problem, pause, and recover safely?” danh gia vung gom tac vu dai ngan va kieu loi khac nhau. nha nghien cuu ghi hoan thanh mot phan, do dung, hieu suat va agent nhan ra bat dinh khong. nhan dat/truot don gian che viec he thong hoan thanh 95% quy trinh hay chang tien trien. thu lap quan trong vi hanh vi agent doi theo lay mau va phan hoi cong cu. voi boi canh he trong, thu gian doan thuc te, chi dan mo ho va thieu thong tin. khong chi do “lam xong duoc khong?” ma ca “phat hien loi, dung va phuc hoi an toan khong?” users can shorten error chains through checkpoints. ask the agent to state its plan, request approval before irreversible actions, save intermediate results, and verify outputs with independent tests. a human should review high-impact decisions rather than every low-risk click; giam sat tap trung noi loi dat hay kho dao. giao dien tot cho thay cong cu da dung va viec con dang do. diem kiem tra ton thoi gian nhung ngan loi som nho thanh hong hoc ton kem ve sau. as of 2026, public agent evaluations continue to evolve, and metr’s time-horizon pages report specific versions and assumptions rather than a single fixed ability. do not translate a benchmark horizon directly into a claim that an agent can replace a job: jobs combine social coordination, tacit knowledge, accountability, and changing goals. for a real workflow, pilot the exact agent, tools, data permissions, and interruption patterns. the useful takeaway is to evaluate reliability on complete tasks and make recovery, oversight, and rollback part of the design. tinh den nam 2026, danh gia agent cong khai tiep tuc doi; cap nhat owasp agentic ai guidance 2025–26, nhan manh quyen o he thong dich. an ai agent becomes riskier when it can act through tools such as email, files, payments, or code execution. the principle of least privilege means granting only the minimum permissions needed for the current task, for the shortest necessary time. owasp’s 2025 guidance on agentic applications highlighted excessive agency, identity, and privilege abuse as concrete risks. in 2026, its agentic security materials further distinguish tool misuse from authority problems. this is a current security snapshot; til-therapy-lifileucel-2024: lieu phap til: nuoi tang te bao mien dich lay tu khoi u tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy fda cap phep tang toc lifileucel nam 2024 cho mot nhom nguoi lon bi melanoma tien trien sau dieu tri truoc do. bai viet giai thich cach til duoc lay, mo rong va truyen lai, cung loi ich, doc tinh nang va gioi han cua bang chung cap phep. in february 2024, the us fda granted accelerated approval to lifileucel, marketed as amtagvi, for certain adults with unresectable or metastatic melanoma after prior treatment. it was the first fda-approved tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (til) therapy. unlike a drug designed from one receptor, til therapy begins with immune cells already found inside a patient’s tumor. the 2024 decision was based on tumor-response data in a small clinical population; cap phep tang toc can bang chung theo doi tiep. dieu tri phuc tap va chi danh cho nguoi dap ung dung chi dinh. tils are t cells that have entered tumor tissue, where some may already recognize abnormal tumor features. a surgeon removes a tumor sample; reproduce selected human biology more directly than a static cell dish. these systems can help study toxicity, disease mechanisms, or drug responses, but they are models of specific functions, not miniature complete organs. a result in a chip does not by itself predict what will happen in a whole person. organ-on-chip la thiet bi vi ky thuat nho dat te bao nguoi song trong cac kenh duoc kiem remote-patient-monitoring-clinical-workf: theo doi benh nhan tu xa: bien du lieu lien tuc thanh cham soc remote patient monitoring: turning continuous data into care theo doi tu xa co the giup phat hien thay doi som, nhung chi khi du lieu duoc loc, nhan vien phan hoi va nguoi benh duoc ho tro phu hop. remote patient monitoring uses connected devices to collect measurements such as blood pressure, oxygen saturation, glucose, weight, or heart rhythm outside a clinic. its appeal is continuous visibility: a care team may notice a change between appointments rather than relying on memory at the next visit. but a stream of numbers is not a care pathway. readings can be inaccurate, affected by technique, or clinically unimportant. monitoring is valuable only when a defined signal leads to a timely response, and when the patient knows what to do if a device fails or symptoms worsen. theo doi benh nhan tu xa dung thiet bi ket noi de thu thap huyet ap, do bao hoa oxy, duong huyet, can nang hoac nhip tim ngoai phong kham. diem hap dan la kha nang quan sat lien tuc: nhom cham soc co the nhan ra thay doi giua cac lan hen thay vi dua vao tri nho o lan kham tiep theo. nhung mot dong so lieu khong phai quy trinh cham soc. so do co the sai, phu thuoc ky thuat hoac khong quan trong ve lam sang. theo doi chi co gia tri khi tin hieu xac dinh dan toi phan hoi kip thoi va nguoi benh biet phai lam gi neu thiet bi hong hoac trieu chung nang len. a safe program begins with a clinical question. for example, a heart-failure team might ask whether daily weight and symptom reports can identify fluid retention early enough to adjust care. the team then chooses devices, thresholds, and escalation rules. one isolated high reading may reflect a misplaced cuff, while a sustained trend combined with breathlessness may justify a call. thresholds should be tested against the population and workflow; copying a setting from another clinic can create alert overload. staff need clear responsibility for reviewing data, including weekends and periods when the usual clinician is away. chuong trinh an toan bat dau bang mot cau hoi lam sang. chang han, nhom suy tim co the hoi lieu can nang hang ngay va bao trieu chung co nhan ra u dich du som de dieu chinh cham soc khong. sau do nhom chon thiet bi, nguong va quy tac chuyen cap. mot so do cao don le co the do dat vong bit sai, trong khi xu huong tang keo dai kem kho tho co the can goi dien. nguong can duoc kiem tra voi dung nhom benh va quy trinh; sao chep cai dat tu phong kham khac co the tao qua tai canh bao. nhan vien can biet ro ai chiu trach nhiem xem du lieu, ke ca cuoi tuan hoac khi bac si thuong le vang mat. evidence depends on the condition, device, and service design. a monitor may improve measurement frequency without changing hospital admissions or quality of life. studies should compare the complete remote-care service with usual care, not merely compare sensors. they need to specify who enrolled, how many readings were missing, what action clinicians took, and whether patients could access the technology. in 2024–2025, regulators and health systems continued to emphasize lifecycle evaluation of connected medical devices, including software updates and cybersecurity. a clinically useful device can become unsafe if alerts stop arriving or data are routed to the wrong team. bang chung phu thuoc benh ly, thiet bi va thiet ke dich vu. may theo doi co the tang tan suat do ma khong lam thay doi so lan nhap vien hay chat luong song. nghien cuu nen so sanh toan bo dich vu cham soc tu xa voi cham soc thuong quy, chu khong chi so cam bien. can neu ai duoc tuyen, bao nhieu so do bi thieu, bac si da lam gi va benh nhan co tiep can cong nghe khong. trong giai doan 2024–2025, co quan quan ly va he thong y te tiep tuc nhan manh danh gia vong doi thiet bi y te ket noi, gom cap nhat phan mem va an ninh mang. thiet bi co ich ve lam sang co the tro nen khong an toan neu canh bao ngung den hoac du lieu chuyen nham nhom. the human interface matters. some users may have limited connectivity, low digital confidence, visual or motor impairments, or language barriers. programs should provide training, accessible instructions, technical support, and a non-digital alternative when needed. clinicians must explain what the monitor can and cannot detect; a normal oxygen reading does not rule out every serious problem. data protection also requires a clear account of who can see measurements, how long they are retained, and whether they are used beyond care. consent is meaningful when people understand both the benefit and the workload they are taking on. giao dien con nguoi rat quan trong. mot so nguoi dung co ket noi yeu, it tu tin cong nghe, khiem thi hoac han che van dong, hay gap rao can ngon ngu. chuong trinh nen cung cap dao tao, huong dan de tiep can, ho tro ky thuat va lua chon khong dung ky thuat so khi can. bac si phai giai thich thiet bi co the va khong the phat hien gi; chi so oxy binh thuong khong loai tru moi van de nghiem trong. bao ve du lieu cung can neu ro ai xem duoc so do, luu bao lau va lieu co dung ngoai muc dich cham soc. dong thuan co y nghia khi moi nguoi hieu ca loi ich lan cong viec ho can dam nhan. remote monitoring can shift work rather than remove it. a nurse who reviews alerts needs time, protocols, and access to the medical record. a physician needs a route to act on concerning patterns, while administrative teams handle device replacement and reimbursement. if alert volume exceeds capacity, clinicians may ignore warnings or patients may receive inconsistent messages. pilot programs should measure alert burden, response time, staffing hours, device failure, equity, and patient outcomes. they should also identify which groups benefit most; monitoring every patient with the same intensity can waste resources and widen access gaps. theo doi tu xa co the chuyen viec chu khong xoa bo viec. dieu duong xem canh bao can co thoi gian, quy trinh va quyen truy cap ho so benh an. bac si can duong hanh dong voi xu huong dang lo, trong khi doi hanh chinh xu ly thay thiet bi va thanh toan. neu so canh bao vuot nang luc, nhan vien co the bo qua canh bao hoac benh nhan nhan thong diep khong nhat quan. chuong trinh thi diem nen do ganh nang canh bao, thoi gian phan hoi, gio nhan luc, loi thiet bi, cong bang va ket qua benh nhan. cung can xac dinh nhom nao huong loi nhat; theo doi moi nguoi voi cung cuong do co the lang phi va lam rong khoang cach tiep can. a sensible implementation plan defines a target condition, a response team, escalation thresholds, and an exit process before devices are distributed. it trains patients, tests connectivity, and audits whether alerts led to documented action. as of 2025, remote monitoring should be understood as a service model supported by devices, not a gadget that independently prevents deterioration. its value is strongest when the signal is actionable, the team has capacity, and patients can participate without unreasonable burden. programs should scale only after measuring clinical outcomes and workflow costs against a realistic alternative. ke hoach trien khai hop ly xac dinh benh muc tieu, doi phan hoi, nguong chuyen cap va quy trinh ket thuc truoc khi phat thiet bi. ke hoach dao tao benh nhan, kiem tra ket noi va ra soat canh bao co dan toi hanh dong duoc ghi nhan khong. tinh den nam 2025, theo doi tu xa nen duoc hieu la mo hinh dich vu co thiet bi ho tro, khong phai mon do tu ngan tinh trang xau di. gia tri cao nhat khi tin hieu co the hanh dong, nhom cham soc co nang luc va benh nhan tham gia ma khong bi dat ganh nang vo ly. chi nen mo rong sau khi do ket qua lam sang va chi phi quy trinh so voi phuong an thuc te khac.

voi benh pho bien hoac thay doi khi tre lon len. hanh trinh chan doan co the keo theo nhieu lan kham, xet nghiem va bat dinh. chan doan phan tu co the lam ro nguyen nhan, dinh huong theo doi, ket noi nguoi than voi xet nghiem va doi khi mo ra dieu tri. no khong tu dong giai quyet moi kho khan: bien the di truyen co the chua ro y nghia, benh co the chua co thuoc dich va ho tro thuc te van can thiet story narrows which genes or pathways are plausible. exome sequencing examines protein-coding regions, while genome sequencing includes a broader range of dna; each can miss certain changes, including biochemical test should depend on the phenotype, urgency, available expertise, and what a result could change. danh gia huu ich bat dau tu kieu hinh: mo ta co cau truc ve trieu chung, dau hieu kham, phat trien, tien su gia dinh va xet nghiem. cau chuyen lam sang nay giup thu hep gene hoac con duong sinh hoc co kha nang lien quan. giai trinh tu exome khao sat vung ma hoa protein, con giai trinh tu genome bao quat pham vi dna rong hon; tuy phuong phap, ca hai co the bo sot mot so bien doi nhu lap doan, bien the cau truc hoac kham. xet nghiem cha me cung tre co the giup dien giai cach di truyen. interpretation is a living process, not a one-time verdict. ban cap nhat nam 2024 cua mang luoi benh chua chan doan thuoc nih mo ta cach nhom da chuyen khoa ket hop ra soat lam sang, xet nghiem va cong cu nghien cuu cho ca kho. mang luoi nhu vay co gia tri vi ket qua gene khong duoc dien giai tach roi: bac si so sanh voi trieu chung, co che benh da biet va bang chung tu nguoi than. bien the how uncertain findings are handled, whether data may be reanalyzed, and who will explain results. genetic counseling supports informed choices and protects family members from misunderstood risk claims. ket qua am tinh cung can duoc giai thich can than. no co the chi nghia la xet nghiem khong tim thay nguyen nhan di truyen dang nghi ngo, chu khong phu nhan trieu chung hay khang dinh khong co benh di truyen. mot so gene benh chua duoc phat hien, mot so bien the kho do va mot so chan doan den tu nguyen nhan khong di truyen. phan tich lai co the huu ich khi co so du lieu, lien he gene–benh ngu va kha nang di lai. he thong y te co the cai thien bang tieu chi chuyen tuyen ro, tu van gene tu xa, van chuyen mau va hop tac voi bac si dia phuong. nen bao cao ty le chan doan theo nhom dan so newborn-screening-genomic-expansion: mo rong sang loc so sinh bang gene: bang chung, dong thuan va nang luc theo doi expanding newborn genomic screening: evidence, consent, and follow-up capacity danh sequencing could expand the search to many disorders at once, but more information is not automatically better. it can reveal variants with uncertain meaning, conditions that may appear only in adulthood, or findings that have no available intervention. any expansion should start with a clear question: which conditions can be detected reliably, and what timely care will be offered after a positive result? sang loc so sinh nham phat hien som benh nghiem trong, thuong truoc khi xuat hien trieu chung, de dieu tri kip thoi ngan ton hai. chuong trinh da thiet lap su dung tap hop xet nghiem mau got chan gioi han, chon benh ma can thiep som co the cai thien ket qua. giai trinh tu gene co the mo rong tim nhieu roi loan cung luc, nhung nhieu thong tin hon khong mac nhien tot hon. no co the phat hien bien the chua ro y nghia, benh chi xuat hien khi truong thanh hoac phat hien khong co can thiep. moi mo rong nen bat dau bang cau hoi ro: co the phat hien benh nao dang tin va cham soc kip preserving findings that have a credible childhood intervention. ket qua sang loc khong phai chan doan. sang loc duong tinh bao hieu can xet nghiem xac nhan va danh gia lam sang; duong tinh gia co the gay lo lang cho gia dinh va su dung nang luc chuyen khoa. ket qua am tinh cung co gioi han vi khong bang nao phat hien moi benh hoac moi bien the gay benh. voi sang loc gene, so phat hien co the rat lon, nen chuong trinh phai xac dinh gene, benh va loai ket qua se tra. thu hep pham vi bao cao co the bao ve gia dinh khoi thong tin ngoai muc tieu trong khi van giu phat hien co can thiep thoi tho au dang tin cay. the babyseq project has studied how sequencing can be incorporated into newborn care and how parents understand results. research from such programs can inform feasibility and family transfer automatically to regions with fewer genetic counsellors or pediatric specialists. du an babyseq da nghien cuu cach tich hop giai trinh tu vao cham soc so sinh va cach cha me hieu ket qua. nghien cuu nhu vay giup danh gia tinh kha thi va trai nghiem gia dinh, nhung nghien cuu trinh dien khong giong chung minh loi ich suc khoe cho toan dan. nha hoach dinh can bang chung so sanh ve ket qua, tac hai, chi phi va ganh nang theo doi. ho nen hoi phat hien gene som co cai thien hon sang loc hien hanh khong, va he thong y te co tiep can moi tre can xac nhan hay dieu tri khong. loi ich o benh vien nghien cuu khong tu dong chuyen sang noi thieu tu van di truyen hoac bac si nhi khoa chuyen sau. consent is complicated because the newborn cannot decide, and genomic data may remain informative for decades. parents need understandable choices about whether sequencing is performed, which results are returned, and whether secondary findings are included. a program should explain storage, access, data sharing, reanalysis, and withdrawal options. it should also consider how results could affect relatives and future autonomy. this does not mean genomic screening must be rejected; it means consent should be proportionate to the scope and consequences of testing. a short checkbox cannot replace an explanation of uncertainty and privacy practices. dong thuan phuc tap vi tre so sinh chua the tu quyet, con du lieu gene co the con y nghia suot nhieu thap ky. cha me can lua chon de hieu ve viec co giai trinh tu khong, loai ket qua nao duoc tra va co bao gom phat hien ngoai muc tieu khong. chuong trinh nen giai thich luu tru, quyen truy cap, chia se du lieu, phan tich lai va lua chon rut lui. cung can can nhac ket qua anh huong toi nguoi than va quyen tu quyet tuong lai ra sao. dieu nay khong co nghia phai bac bo sang loc gene; no co nghia muc dong thuan phai tuong xung voi pham vi va hau qua xet nghiem. mot o danh dau ngan khong the thay loi giai thich ve bat dinh va quyen rieng tu. follow-up capacity is part of the screening test. a program needs confirmatory laboratories, pediatric specialists, genetic counselling, treatment access, and a reliable way to contact families. if a result arrives but no service can act, screening may create inequity without delivering benefit. programs should measure time from sample collection to confirmation, time to treatment, loss to follow-up, false-positive burden, and outcomes by population. they should also monitor whether expansion diverts resources from established tests that already prevent severe disease. economic evaluation can help compare value, but it cannot replace ethical discussion about data and family choices. nang luc theo doi la mot phan cua xet nghiem sang loc. chuong trinh can nguon luc khoi xet nghiem hien hanh von ngan benh nang khong. danh gia kinh te giup so sanh gia tri, nhung khong thay the thao luan dao duc ve du lieu va lua chon gia dinh. a responsible expansion is staged. it selects conditions with strong evidence that early identification changes care, pilots the workflow, involves families and communities, and publishes both benefits and harms. independent pharmacogenomic-test-implementation: duoc di truyen hoc: khi ket qua gene lam thay doi cach ke don pharmacogenomics: when genetic results change prescribing giai thich cach bien the gene anh huong chuyen hoa hoac dap ung thuoc va vi sao xet nghiem chi huu ich khi quy trinh ke don co the hanh dong theo ket qua. pharmacogenomics studies how inherited genetic differences influence a person’s response to medicines. a variant can alter an enzyme that activates a drug, breaks it down, or moves it into a tissue. the same prescribed dose may therefore produce too little effect in one person or excessive exposure in another. this is different from testing a tumour for a treatment target: pharmacogenomics concerns the patient’s inherited biology and drug handling. it does not predict every side effect or replace clinical judgment, but for selected gene–drug pairs it can help clinicians choose a dose or an alternative medicine. duoc di truyen hoc nghien cuu khac biet gene di truyen anh huong cach mot nguoi dap ung thuoc. bien the co the lam thay doi enzyme kich hoat thuoc, phan giai thuoc hoac van chuyen thuoc vao mo. vi vay, cung lieu ke co the tao hieu qua qua thap o nguoi nay hoac phoi nhiem qua cao o nguoi khac. dieu nay khac xet nghiem khoi u de tim dich dieu tri: duoc di truyen hoc lien quan sinh hoc di truyen cua nguoi benh va cach xu ly thuoc. no khong du doan moi tac dung phu hay thay the phan doan lam sang, nhung voi mot so cap gene–thuoc duoc xac lap, co the giup chon lieu hoac thuoc khac. the clinical question is not whether a gene is associated with a drug response; it is whether testing and using the result improves a decision. in 2024, a review of us clinical practice guidelines examined recommendations for 21 gene–drug pairs considered actionable by cpic. it found that guidance varied across organizations and pairs. examples with recommendations included cyp2c19 and clopidogrel, cyp2d6 and codeine, and tpmt or nudt15 with thiopurines. these are not blanket rules for every patient. prescribers must check the specific guideline, indication, phenotype, and competing clinical factors. cau hoi lam sang khong phai gene co lien he voi dap ung thuoc khong; cau hoi la xet nghiem va dung ket qua co cai thien quyet dinh khong. nam 2024, mot tong quan huong dan thuc hanh lam sang hoa ky xem xet khuyen nghi cho 21 cap gene–thuoc duoc cpic danh gia la co the hanh dong. huong dan khac nhau giua to chuc va tung cap. vi du co khuyen nghi gom cyp2c19 voi clopidogrel, cyp2d6 voi codeine, va tpmt hoac nudt15 voi thiopurine. day khong phai quy tac bao quat moi benh nhan. nguoi ke don can kiem tra huong dan cu the, chi dinh, kieu hinh va cac yeu to lam sang canh tranh. testing can happen before a prescription or after an unexpected response. hoac sau dap ung bat ngo. xet nghiem du phong luu ket qua trong ho so suc khoe de ho tro ke don tuong lai, nhung chi co tac dung neu de tim va gan voi ho tro quyet dinh lam sang. xet nghiem theo phan ung co the tap trung hon va tranh xet nghiem nguoi khong bao gio dung thuoc lien quan. bao cao phong xet nghiem can chuyen kieu gene thanh kieu hinh co y nghia nhu chuyen hoa kem hay nhanh, dong thoi cong bo bat dinh va huong dan duoc dung. bac si cung can biet cach dien giai ap dung cho thuoc, lieu va tinh huong nao. implementation is a system task. pharmacists, genetic counsellors, prescribers, interactions, and patient preferences. programs should measure prescribing changes, adverse events, effectiveness, turnaround time, and unequal access rather than counting tests alone. trien khai la nhiem vu cua he thong. duoc si, chuyen vien tu van gene, nguoi ke don, nhan vien phong xet nghiem va nhom cong nghe thong tin phai thong nhat cach dua ket qua vao ho so, ai nhan canh bao va cach cap nhat cach dien giai da loi thoi. xet nghiem co the chinh xac ve phan tich nhung khong giup duoc neu bac si khong biet ket qua ton tai hoac thuoc da duoc ke truoc khi ket qua tra. dao tao nen giai thich kieu gene chi la mot dau vao ben canh tuoi, chuc nang than gan, tuong tac thuoc va lua chon benh nhan. chuong trinh nen do thay doi ke don, bien co bat loi, hieu qua, thoi gian tra va tiep can khong cong bang thay vi chi dem so xet nghiem. population representation matters because reference data and clinical studies may be uneven across ancestry groups. a genotype panel can miss rare confidence. reports should state assay limitations, and health systems should monitor whether recommendations work similarly across groups. patients should also be able to correct family history or lieu tham chieu va nghien cuu lam sang co the khong dong deu giua nhom to tien. bang gene co the bo sot bien the hiem nhung pho bien hon o nhom it duoc dua vao phat trien xet nghiem. mot so phong xet nghiem dung nhan “chuyen hoa binh thuong” dua tren pham vi bien the han che, tao cam giac chac chan sai. bao cao can neu gioi han xet nghiem, con he thong y te can theo doi khuyen nghi co hoat dong tuong tu giua cac nhom khong. benh nhan cung nen co the sua thong tin gia dinh hoac thuoc. ket qua gene la du lieu lau dai, vi vay can quan tri than trong ve quyen rieng tu, kiem soat truy cap va chia khi ket noi duoc sinh hoc, thuoc cu the, boi canh benh nhan va loi ich do luong duoc.
surrogate-endpoint-validation: chi dau thay the: khi nao mot dau an sinh hoc dai dien duoc cho loi ich suc khoe? surrogate endpoints: when can a biomarker stand in for health benefit? giai thich vi sao thay doi dau an sinh hoc co the giup nghien cuu nhanh hon nhung khong luon du doan ket qua nguoi benh, va cach fda phan loai bang chung. a surrogate endpoint is a laboratory measurement or physical sign used in place of a direct clinical outcome. blood pressure can help predict stroke risk, viral load can reflect infection control, and tumour size can indicate response. surrogates can make trials shorter or smaller when waiting for death, disability, or long-term complications would take years. but association is not enough: a treatment can improve a biomarker while causing harm through another pathway. the central question is whether changing the surrogate reliably predicts a meaningful change in how patients feel, function, or survive. chi dau thay the la phep do phong xet nghiem hoac dau hieu the chat duoc dung thay cho ket qua lam sang truc tiep. huyet ap giup du doan nguy co dot quy, tai luong virus phan anh kiem soat nhiem trung va kich thuoc khoi u co the bieu thi dap ung. chi dau giup thu nghiem ngan hoac nho hon khi cho tu vong, tan tat hay bien chung dai han se mat nhieu nam. nhung chi co lien he la chua du: thuoc co the cai thien chi dau dong thoi gay hai qua con duong khac. cau hoi cot loi la thay doi chi dau co du doan dang tin thay doi co y nghia ve cam nhan, chuc nang hoac song con cua benh nhan khong. validation depends on context. a surrogate may predict outcomes for one disease, intervention, or patient group but fail for another. lowering a biomarker through a different mechanism may not reproduce the benefit seen in earlier trials. fda distinguishes a validated surrogate, supported by strong evidence that it predicts clinical benefit, from a reasonably likely surrogate that has a plausible basis but still needs confirmation. the agency’s public table lists endpoints used in specific approvals; inclusion does not mean the same measure is a valid substitute for every drug or condition. each claim needs a defined scope. tham dinh phu thuoc boi canh. mot chi dau co the du doan ket qua cho mot benh, can thiep hoac nhom benh nhan nhung that bai o nhom khac. ha chi dau bang co che khac chua chac tai tao loi ich trong thu nghiem truoc. fda phan biet chi dau thay the da duoc xac nhan, co bang chung manh rang du doan loi ich lam sang, voi chi dau duoc xem la co kha nang hop ly nhung van can xac nhan. bang cong khai cua co quan liet ke chi dau dung trong mot so phe duyet; co ten trong bang khong co nghia phep do do thay the hop le cho moi thuoc hay benh. moi tuyen bo can pham vi xac dinh. evidence can come from several layers. biological understanding should show why the marker lies on a pathway that affects the outcome. randomized trials can test whether treatment effects on the surrogate track effects on clinical endpoints across interventions. individual-level association alone is weaker than trial-level prediction: people with lower biomarker values may do better, yet a drug that lowers the marker may not improve outcomes. statistical methods should account for baseline risk, measurement error, and competing mechanisms. independent replication matters because a surrogate chosen after seeing the data can exaggerate apparent predictive power. bang chung co the den tu nhieu lop. hieu biet sinh hoc can cho thay dau an nam tren con duong anh huong ket qua. thu nghiem ngau nhien co the kiem tra tac dong dieu tri len chi dau co di cung tac dong len ket cuc lam sang qua nhieu can thiep khong. lien he o tung ca nhan yeu hon kha nang du doan giua cac thu nghiem: nguoi co gia tri chi dau thap co the khoe hon, nhung thuoc lam giam chi dau chua chac cai thien ket qua. phuong phap thong ke can tinh nguy co ban dau, sai so do va co che canh tranh. tai lap doc lap quan trong vi chon chi dau sau khi xem du lieu co the phong dai suc du doan. accelerated or conditional approvals may rely on a surrogate that is reasonably likely to predict benefit, with confirmatory studies required afterward. this can give patients earlier access to promising therapies, particularly for serious diseases with few options. it also creates an obligation to finish follow-up trials and revise decisions if benefit is not confirmed. a biomarker response should be described honestly: it is evidence supporting a regulatory decision under specified conditions, not a guarantee that a patient will live longer or feel better. public communication should distinguish preliminary approval logic from final proof of clinical effect. phe duyet tang toc hoac co dieu kien co the dua tren chi dau duoc xem la co kha nang hop ly du doan loi ich, kem yeu cau nghien cuu xac nhan sau do. cach nay giup benh nhan tiep can som lieu phap hua hen, nhat la voi benh nang it lua chon. no cung tao nghia vu hoan tat nghien cuu theo doi va xem lai quyet dinh neu loi ich khong duoc xac nhan. dap ung dau an sinh hoc nen duoc mo ta trung thuc: do la bang chung ho tro quyet dinh quan ly trong dieu kien xac dinh, khong phai bao dam benh nhan song lau hon hay cam thay tot hon. truyen thong cong chung can phan biet ly do phe duyet ban dau voi chung minh cuoi cung ve tac dong lam sang. surrogate endpoints also shape what patients and clinicians notice. a treatment may improve an imaging measure while leaving pain, mobility, or daily function unchanged. conversely, a therapy can benefit patients in ways not captured by a single biomarker. trials should therefore collect patient-centred outcomes and safety data even when a surrogate is the primary endpoint. regulators, researchers, and health systems should ask whether the marker is meaningful for the condition and whether confirmatory evidence is on schedule. the fda table is a useful record of precedent, but precedent must be interpreted endpoint by real-world-evidence-trial-emulation: bang chung thuc te: mo phong thu nghiem muc tieu tu du lieu quan sat real-world evidence: emulating a target trial with observational data khung thu nghiem muc tieu giup thiet ke nghien cuu du lieu thuong quy nhu mot thu nghiem ro cau hoi, nhung khong tu loai bo nhieu va sai lech. randomized trials remain a strong way to estimate treatment effects, but they may be slow, expensive, or too narrow to answer every question. electronic health records and insurance data can show what happens in routine care, including older patients and people with multiple conditions. observational data do not randomly assign treatment, so healthier patients may be more likely to receive one option while sicker patients receive another. target-trial emulation addresses this by writing down the hypothetical randomized trial researchers would ideally run, then mapping its design to available data before analyzing outcomes. thu nghiem ngau nhien van la cach manh de uoc tinh tac dong dieu tri, nhung co the cham, ton kem hoac qua hep de tra loi moi cau hoi. ho so suc khoe dien tu va du lieu bao hiem cho thay dieu gi xay ra trong cham soc thuong quy, ke ca voi nguoi lon tuoi va nguoi mac nhieu benh. du lieu quan sat khong phan bo dieu tri ngau nhien, nen nguoi khoe hon co the de nhan mot lua chon trong khi nguoi nang hon nhan lua chon khac. mo phong thu nghiem muc tieu giai quyet bang cach viet ra thu nghiem ngau nhien gia dinh ma nha nghien cuu muon lam, roi anh xa thiet ke do vao du lieu san co truoc khi phan tich ket qua. a protocol should specify eligibility, treatment strategies, assignment, start of follow-up, outcomes, and analysis—the same core elements of a trial. time zero is particularly important: if patients are classified as treated only after surviving long enough to receive a prescription, the analysis can create immortal-time bias. researchers also need a causal estimand, such as the effect of starting treatment now versus not starting within a defined window. the 2024 nejm perspective on target-trial emulation highlighted both its potential and pitfalls. a clear protocol makes assumptions visible; it does not make them automatically true. de cuong can xac dinh tieu chi du dieu kien, chien luoc dieu tri, phan nhom, thoi diem bat dau theo doi, ket qua va phan tich—nhung yeu to cot loi giong thu nghiem. moc thoi gian so khong dac biet quan trong: neu chi xep benh nhan vao nhom da dieu tri sau khi ho song du lau de nhan toa, phan tich co the tao thien lech thoi gian bat tu. nha nghien cuu cung can xac dinh dai luong nhan qua, chang han tac dong cua bat dau thuoc ngay so voi khong bat dau trong mot khoang thoi gian xac dinh. bai binh luan nejm nam 2024 ve mo phong thu nghiem muc tieu neu ca tiem nang lan cam bay. de cuong ro lam lo gia dinh, nhung khong tu khien gia dinh dung. confounding remains the main threat. disease severity, clinician preference, income, access, and patient adherence may influence both treatment choice and outcome. statistical adjustment can address measured factors, but no model can fully correct information that was never recorded or measured badly. researchers should draw a causal diagram, define which variables are confounders, and avoid adjusting for mediators or colliders in ways that introduce bias. negative controls and sensitivity analyses can test how strong an unmeasured factor would need to be to change the conclusion. results should be described as causal only when assumptions are credible and explicitly defended. nhieu van la moi de doa chinh. muc do benh, so thich bac si, thu nhap, kha nang tiep can va tuan thu cua benh nhan co the anh huong ca lua chon dieu tri lan ket qua. dieu chinh thong ke xu ly duoc yeu to da do, nhung mo hinh khong the sua hoan toan thong tin chua tung duoc ghi hoac do kem. nha nghien cuu nen ve so do nhan qua, xac dinh bien gay nhieu va tranh dieu chinh bien trung gian hoac bien va cham theo cach tao thien lech. doi chung am va phan tich do nhay kiem tra yeu to chua do can manh toi dau moi doi ket luan. chi mo ta ket qua nhu quan he nhan qua khi gia dinh dang tin va duoc giai thich ro. large datasets do not causal comparisons for that group may rely on extrapolation. bo du lieu lon khong dam bao bang chung dai dien. ho so co the bo qua trieu chung, dung ma hoa khong nhat quan hoac thieu thuoc mua ngoai mot dieu tri hiem o nhom phu, so sanh nhan qua cho nhom do co the dua vao ngoai suy. the framework can answer questions that trials cannot easily address, such as long-term safety, treatment effects toi thu thap bang chung it gay gian doan benh nhan. thiet ke tinh gon van can dong thuan, du lieu tot, ky luat de cuong va bien phap bao ve. du lieu thuc te mo ta thuc hanh; chi thiet ke hop le moi bien chung thanh bang chung dang tin ve tac dong dieu tri. the 2025 target reporting statement further emphasized stating the causal question, protocol, assumptions, mapping to observational data, and sensitivity analyses. reporting standards cannot rescue poor design, but they help readers judge what was actually estimated. before relying on a result, decision makers should ask whether eligibility and treatment timing were well defined, whether important confounders were measured, and whether results agree with randomized evidence. target-trial emulation is a disciplined use of observational clinical-prediction-model-external-valid: mo hinh du doan lam sang can duoc kiem dinh ngoai noi phat trien clinical prediction models need validation beyond their development site kham pha vi sao mo hinh nguy co mat hieu nang khi chuyen benh vien hoac thoi gian, va cach kiem dinh ngoai danh gia hieu chuan, phan biet va tac dong thuc te. a clinical prediction model combines patient information to estimate a future outcome, such as deterioration, readmission, or disease risk. it may use regression or machine learning, but the algorithm’s complexity does not guarantee usefulness. a model can fit its development dataset exceptionally well because it has learned local patterns, coding quirks, or random noise. when moved to another hospital, age mix, equipment, care practices, and disease prevalence may differ. external validation asks whether the model’s predictions remain accurate and well calibrated in new people, places, or time periods before clinicians rely on its scores. mo hinh du doan lam sang ket hop thong tin benh nhan de uoc tinh ket qua tuong lai nhu dien bien xau, tai nhap vien hoac nguy co benh. mo hinh co the dung hoi quy hay hoc may, nhung thuat toan phuc tap khong dam bao huu ich. mo hinh co the khop rat tot du lieu phat trien vi hoc duoc mo thuc dia phuong, loi ma hoa hoac nhieu ngau nhien. khi chuyen sang benh vien khac, phan bo tuoi, thiet bi, thuc hanh cham soc va muc pho bien benh co the khac. kiem dinh ngoai hoi du doan con chinh xac va hieu chuan tot o nguoi, noi hoac thoi ky moi truoc khi bac si dua vao diem so khong. discrimination measures whether a model ranks people with an outcome above those without it. calibration asks whether predicted probabilities match observed frequencies: among patients assigned a 20 percent risk, roughly one in five should experience the outcome over the defined period. a model can discriminate reasonably yet be systematically overconfident, leading to too many alerts. calibration may shift when prevalence changes, even if the ranking stays similar. validation should report both properties, with confidence intervals, and examine thresholds relevant to decisions. a single area-under-the-curve number cannot show whether a model’s risk estimates are trustworthy. kha nang phan biet do mo hinh xep nguoi co ket qua benh len tren nguoi khong co. hieu chuan hoi xac suat du doan co khop tan suat quan sat khong: trong nhom duoc du bao nguy co 20%, xap xi mot phan nam nen gap ket qua trong khoang thoi gian da dinh. mo hinh co the phan biet tuong doi tot nhung qua tu tin co he thong, dan toi qua nhieu canh bao. hieu chuan co the thay doi khi muc pho bien benh doi du thu hang tuong tu. kiem dinh nen bao cao ca hai thuoc tinh, kem khoang tin cay, va xem cac nguong lien quan quyet dinh. mot con so dien tich duoi duong cong khong cho biet uoc luong nguy co co dang tin khong. external validation must match the intended deployment. temporal validation tests later patients at the same hospital; geographic validation tests another site; subgroup validation examines groups such as age, sex, or ancestry. these designs reveal different kinds of drift. a model trained before a new treatment guideline may become outdated even within the original hospital. researchers should preserve the original model and threshold during initial validation rather than silently refitting it, then report any recalibration as a separate step. this distinction shows whether the original tool travels and what adaptation is required. kiem dinh ngoai can khop muc tieu trien khai. kiem dinh theo thoi gian kiem tra benh nhan den sau o cung benh vien; kiem dinh dia ly kiem tra noi khac; kiem dinh nhom phu xem xet tuoi, gioi hay to tien. cac thiet ke nay phat hien dang troi lech khac nhau. mo hinh huan luyen truoc huong dan dieu tri moi co the loi thoi ngay tai benh vien goc. nha nghien cuu nen giu nguyen mo hinh va nguong ban dau trong lan kiem dinh dau thay vi am tham huan luyen lai, sau do bao cao hieu chinh lai nhu buoc rieng. phan biet nay cho thay cong cu goc co chuyen duoc khong va can thich ung gi. the 2024 tripod+ai statement updated reporting guidance for prediction models developed with regression or machine learning. it asks researchers to describe participants, data sources, missing data, model building, and evaluation clearly enough for readers to judge risk of bias and applicability. reporting is not validation itself, and a checklist cannot fix an unrepresentative sample. still, transparent methods make it easier to reproduce results and detect leakage, such as information from after the prediction time accidentally entering the model. developers should publish the intended use, target population, and prediction horizon before claiming broad clinical relevance. tuyen bo tripod+ai nam 2024 cap nhat huong dan bao cao mo hinh du doan dung hoi quy hoac hoc may. tuyen bo yeu cau mo ta nguoi tham gia, nguon du lieu, du lieu thieu, qua trinh xay dung va danh gia du ro de doc gia xet nguy co thien lech va kha nang ap dung. bao cao khong phai ban than kiem dinh, va bang kiem khong the sua mau khong dai dien. tuy vay, phuong phap minh bach giup lap lai ket qua va phat hien ro ri du lieu, nhu vo tinh dua thong tin xuat hien sau thoi diem du doan vao mo hinh. nha phat trien nen cong bo muc dich, quan the dich va khoang du doan truoc khi tuyen bo lien quan lam sang rong. even a well-validated model may not improve care. a risk score must reach a clinician at the right moment, fit the workflow, and lead to an intervention that benefits the patient. decision-curve analysis can estimate net benefit across thresholds, but a prospective impact study is needed to observe real consequences, including alert fatigue, extra tests, and unequal treatment. monitoring after deployment matters because coding, patient populations, and care pathways change. a governance plan should specify who reviews performance, how drift is detected, and when the model is paused, recalibrated, or retired. ngay ca mo hinh duoc kiem dinh tot cung co the khong cai thien cham soc. diem nguy co phai toi bac si dung luc, phu hop quy trinh va dan toi can thiep co loi cho benh nhan. phan tich duong cong quyet dinh uoc luong loi ich rong qua cac nguong, nhung can nghien cuu tac dong tien cuu de quan sat he qua that nhu met moi canh bao, xet nghiem them va dieu tri khong cong bang. theo doi sau trien khai quan trong vi ma hoa, quan the benh nhan va duong cham soc thay doi. ke hoach quan tri can neu ai xem xet hieu nang, phat hien troi lech ra sao va khi nao tam dung, hieu chinh lai hay ngung mo hinh. a strong validation report states how many events occurred, whether participants resemble future users, how missingness was handled, and whether predictions were calibrated. it examines performance across clinically important subgroups and explains what happens when confidence is low or inputs are unavailable. the 2024 tripod+ai guidance supports more complete reporting, while clinical impact still needs separate evidence. models should be treated as versioned tools, with dates and change logs, because even a minor update can alter who is flagged. external validation is not a one-time stamp; it is a repeated check against the setting where decisions are made. bao cao kiem dinh manh neu so bien co, nguoi tham gia co giong nguoi dung tuong lai khong, xu ly du lieu thieu the nao va du doan co hieu chuan khong. bao cao xem hieu nang qua nhom lam sang quan trong va giai thich chuyen gi xay ra khi do tin cay thap hoac thieu dau vao. huong dan tripod+ai nam 2024 ho tro bao cao day du hon, con tac dong lam sang van can bang chung rieng. mo hinh nen duoc xem la cong cu co phien ban, ghi ngay va lich su thay doi vi cap nhat nho cung co the doi ai bi gan co. kiem dinh ngoai khong phai dau chung nhan mot lan; do la viec kiem tra lap lai voi moi truong noi quyet dinh duoc dua ra.
diagnostic-test-predictive-values: gia tri du doan: vi sao muc pho bien benh lam doi y nghia ket qua predictive values: why prevalence changes what a test result means do nhay va do dac hieu khong cho biet truc tiep xac suat mac benh sau khi co ket qua; gia tri du doan con phu thuoc xac suat truoc xet nghiem. sensitivity and specificity describe how a test behaves among people whose disease status is already known. patients and clinicians usually ask a different question: given this result, how likely is disease? positive predictive value answers that question for positive results; negative predictive value does so for negative results. both depend on the prevalence, or pre-test probability, in the tested population. the same test can therefore produce very different meanings in a high-risk clinic and a low-risk screening group. a positive result is not a fixed probability attached to the device; it is an update from the patient’s starting risk. do nhay va do dac hieu mo ta xet nghiem hoat dong ra sao o nguoi da biet tinh trang benh. benh nhan va bac si thuong hoi cau khac: voi ket qua nay, kha nang mac benh la bao nhieu? gia tri du doan duong tra loi cho ket qua duong; gia tri du doan am lam vay voi ket qua am. ca hai phu thuoc muc pho bien, hay xac suat truoc xet nghiem, trong nhom duoc kiem tra. cung xet nghiem co the mang y nghia rat khac tai phong kham nguy co cao va nhom sang loc nguy co thap. duong tinh khong co mot xac suat co dinh gan voi thiet bi; do la cap nhat tu nguy co ban dau cua benh nhan. consider a hypothetical disease affecting 1 percent of 10,000 people. a test with 90 percent sensitivity identifies about 90 of the 100 people with disease. with 95 percent specificity, however, it also gives false positives to about 495 of the 9,900 people without disease. among roughly 585 positive results, only 90 are true positives, so the positive predictive value is about 15 percent. the arithmetic surprises people because the test is reasonably accurate yet the disease is rare. this is why screening positives often need confirmation and why prevalence must accompany performance statistics. xet benh gia dinh anh huong 1% trong 10.000 nguoi. xet nghiem co do nhay 90% tim ra khoang 90 trong 100 nguoi mac benh. nhung voi do dac hieu 95%, xet nghiem cung cho duong tinh gia o khoang 495 trong 9.900 nguoi khong benh. trong khoang 585 ket qua duong, chi 90 la duong that, nen gia tri du doan duong khoang 15%. phep tinh khien nhieu nguoi bat ngo vi xet nghiem tuong doi chinh xac nhung benh hiem. day la ly do ket qua sang loc duong tinh thuong can xac nhan va vi sao muc pho bien can duoc neu cung so lieu hieu nang. the result depends not only on population prevalence but also on who was selected for testing and why. a clinician testing a patient with characteristic symptoms starts from a higher pre-test probability than a workplace screening programme testing asymptomatic people. risk factors, exposure history, and local outbreaks can shift that starting point. if a study tests mostly severe cases and healthy controls, estimates may look better than performance in ordinary patients with borderline symptoms. diagnostic accuracy studies should describe the intended-use population and avoid presenting predictive values as universal properties of the assay. ket qua khong chi phu thuoc ty le benh trong dan so ma con vao ai duoc chon xet nghiem va vi sao. bac si kiem tra benh nhan co trieu chung dac trung bat dau voi xac suat truoc xet nghiem cao hon chuong trinh sang loc nhan vien khong trieu chung. yeu to nguy co, tien su phoi nhiem va o dich dia phuong co the thay doi nguy co ban dau. neu nghien cuu chu yeu kiem tra ca nang va nguoi khoe lam doi chung, uoc tinh co the dep hon hieu nang o benh nhan thuong co trieu chung ranh gioi. nghien cuu do chinh xac chan doan nen mo ta nhom su dung du kien, tranh trinh bay gia tri du doan nhu thuoc tinh pho quat cua xet nghiem. likelihood ratios can help update risk without forcing every setting into one predictive-value table. a positive likelihood ratio describes how much more common a positive result is in disease than no disease; a negative likelihood ratio describes the corresponding reduction after a negative result. clinicians can combine these with a pre-test estimate using a nomogram or calculator. but the numbers still rely on valid sensitivity and specificity estimates from comparable patients and procedures. if the test performs differently at another disease stage, with another specimen, or in a population with different variants, the update may be misleading. ty so kha di giup cap nhat nguy co ma khong can co nhet moi moi truong vao mot bang gia tri du doan. ty so kha di duong mo ta ket qua duong pho bien hon bao nhieu o nguoi benh so voi khong benh; ty so am mo ta muc giam tuong ung sau ket qua am. bac si co the ket hop chung voi uoc tinh truoc xet nghiem bang bieu do hoac cong cu tinh. tuy nhien, cac so lieu van dua vao uoc tinh do nhay va dac hieu hop le o benh nhan va quy trinh tuong dong. neu xet nghiem hoat dong khac theo giai doan benh, loai mau hoac bien the dan so, cap nhat co the gay hieu lam. communication should use natural frequencies and explain the next step. rather than saying “the test is 95 percent accurate,” a clinician can describe how many people out of 1,000 with a similar risk would likely receive true and false results. visual grids can make base rates easier to understand. the team should also state whether the result is a screening finding, a diagnosis, or a reason for another test. the fda’s guidance on diagnostic-study reporting emphasizes clear performance estimates and uncertainty intervals; numbers without the study population and confidence bounds invite overconfidence. truyen dat nen dung tan suat tu nhien va giai thich buoc tiep theo. thay vi noi “xet nghiem chinh xac 95%”, bac si co the mo ta trong 1.000 nguoi co nguy co tuong tu se co bao nhieu nguoi nhieu kha nang nhan ket qua dung hoac sai. luoi hinh anh giup hieu ty le nen de hon. nhom cham soc cung nen neu ket qua la phat hien sang loc, chan doan hay ly do lam xet nghiem khac. huong dan fda ve bao cao nghien cuu chan doan nhan manh uoc tinh hieu nang ro va khoang bat dinh; con so khong kem nhom nghien cuu va khoang tin cay de tao tu tin qua muc. predictive values are useful when choosing whether to confirm, treat, or monitor, but they should not be used to dismiss a patient’s symptoms. a low positive predictive value may mean a confirmatory test is sensible, not that every positive is false. a high negative predictive value in a low-risk population may still leave meaningful residual risk for an exposed patient. the right interpretation combines test performance, pre-test probability, clinical context, and consequences of action or delay. the durable lesson is simple: ask “among people like this patient,” not merely “how accurate is the test?” gia tri du doan huu ich khi chon xac nhan, dieu tri hay theo doi, nhung khong nen dung de bac bo trieu chung benh nhan. gia tri du doan duong thap co the cho thay nen lam xet nghiem xac nhan, chu khong co nghia moi ket qua duong deu sai. gia tri du doan am cao o nhom nguy co thap van co the de lai nguy co dang ke cho nguoi da phoi nhiem. cach hieu dung ket hop hieu nang xet nghiem, xac suat truoc xet nghiem, boi canh lam sang va hau qua hanh dong hay tri hoan. bai hoc ben vung rat don gian: hay hoi “o nguoi giong benh nhan nay”, khong chi “xet nghiem chinh xac bao nhieu?”.
diagnostic-stewardship-workflow: chan doan co trach nhiem: chon dung xet nghiem vao dung thoi diem diagnostic stewardship: choosing the right test at the right time chan doan co trach nhiem toi uu chi dinh, lay mau, xu ly va dien giai de ket qua ho tro cham soc va han che khang thuoc. diagnostic stewardship means using tests in a way that improves patient care and public health. it covers the whole process: deciding whether to test, choosing the right assay, collecting a suitable specimen, transporting it correctly, interpreting the result, and acting on it. ordering more tests is not automatically safer. a poorly chosen test can detect colonization rather than infection, return a result too late, or trigger unnecessary antibiotics. in june 2026, who’s western pacific region published a practical facility-oriented manual that treats diagnostic stewardship as part of antimicrobial-resistance response. the date marks new guidance; the underlying principle is broader than one region. chan doan co trach nhiem nghia la su dung xet nghiem theo cach cai thien cham soc benh nhan va suc khoe cong dong. no bao trum ca quy trinh: quyet dinh co xet nghiem khong, chon phep thu phu hop, lay mau dung, van chuyen chuan, dien giai ket qua va hanh dong theo do. lam nhieu xet nghiem hon khong tu dong an toan hon. xet nghiem chon kem co the phat hien vi khuan cu tru thay vi nhiem trung, tra ket qua qua muon hoac kich hoat khang sinh khong can. thang 6 nam 2026, who khu vuc tay thai binh duong xuat ban cam nang thuc hanh cap co so, xem chan doan co trach nhiem la mot phan cua ung pho khang khang sinh. ngay thang danh dau huong dan moi; nguyen tac nen rong hon mot khu vuc. a good workflow starts with a clinical question and a pre-test plan. for a suspected urinary infection, the clinician should consider symptoms, risk factors, specimen quality, and whether a culture will change treatment. testing people without compatible symptoms may identify bacteria that do not need antibiotics. in respiratory illness, a molecular panel that detects several viruses can still create confusion if the clinician cannot distinguish the cause of symptoms from incidental medication-reconciliation-care-transitio: doi chieu thuoc khi chuyen vien: ngan bo sot, trung lap va nham lieu medication reconciliation during care transitions: preventing omissions, duplication, and dose errors khi benh nhan nhap vien, chuyen khoa hoac xuat vien, danh sach thuoc can duoc so khop voi don moi va giai thich ro thay doi cho nguoi benh. a care transition moves a patient between settings or teams: home to hospital, emergency department to ward, or hospital back to primary care. medication lists can become inaccurate at each handoff. a medicine may be omitted, duplicated, restarted at the wrong dose, or continued despite a new contraindication. medication reconciliation compares the best available history of what a patient actually takes with new orders, identifies discrepancies, and resolves them with the responsible clinician. it is more than copying a list into a discharge form; it is a safety conversation about why each medicine is started, stopped, or changed. chuyen tiep cham soc dua benh nhan giua moi truong hoac nhom dieu tri: tu nha vao vien, tu cap cuu len khoa hoac tu vien ve cham soc ban dau. danh sach thuoc co the sai o moi lan ban giao. thuoc co the bi bo, ke trung, dung lai sai lieu hoac tiep tuc du co chong chi dinh moi. doi chieu thuoc so sanh lich su tot nhat ve thuoc benh nhan thuc su uong voi y lenh moi, xac dinh sai khac va giai quyet cung bac si chiu trach nhiem. day khong chi la sao chep danh sach vao giay xuat vien; do la cuoc trao doi an toan ve ly do bat dau, ngung hoac doi tung thuoc. the process begins by gathering multiple sources: the patient or caregiver, primary-care record, pharmacy dispensing history, medication containers, and prior discharge summaries. no single source is always complete. staff should record prescription medicines, over-the-counter products, supplements, allergies, actual dose, and how often each is taken. patients may not know generic names or may use medicines intermittently, so open questions work better than asking only “do you take this?” a “best possible medication history” is a reasoned list with discrepancies made visible, not an assumption that the electronic record is correct. quy trinh bat dau bang cach thu thap nhieu nguon: benh nhan hoac nguoi cham soc, ho so cham soc ban dau, lich cap phat cua nha thuoc, vo thuoc va giay xuat vien truoc. khong nguon don le nao luon day du. nhan vien nen ghi thuoc ke don, thuoc khong ke don, thuc pham bo sung, di ung, lieu thuc te va tan suat dung. benh nhan co the khong biet ten goc hoac uong khong deu, nen cau hoi mo hieu qua hon chi hoi “co dung thuoc nay khong?”. “lich su thuoc tot nhat co the” la danh sach duoc lap co can nhac, lam lo sai khac, khong phai gia dinh ho so dien tu luon dung. at admission, clinicians compare the verified history with inpatient orders. some home medicines should be held because of surgery, kidney injury, or interactions; thuoc khac can tiep tuc de tranh cai thuoc hoac benh mat on dinh. khi xuat vien, nhom so phac do trong vien voi ke hoach ve nha va giai thich tung thay doi. ban tom luoc chinh sach “thuoc khong gay hai” who nam 2024 uu tien chuyen tiep cham soc la linh vuc co the giam ton hai do thuoc. van ban nhan manh hanh dong phoi hop giua benh nhan, nhan vien y te, he thong thuoc va thuc hanh. day la khung chinh sach, khong bao dam mot bang kiem don le ngan duoc moi loi. high-risk transitions deserve extra attention: older adults taking many medicines, people with limited health literacy, patients leaving intensive care, or those changing anticoagulants, insulin, opioids, or seizure medicines. a pharmacist can identify duplicate therapies, unclear indications, dose changes, and interactions. however, reconciliation is not simply deprescribing; quy trinh dia phuong can thich ung nhan luc va ho so. muc tieu thuc te la duy tri thuoc co chu dich, khong tu dong. moi muc trong danh sach can co ly do, nguoi phu trach va ke hoach ra soat khi boi canh benh nhan thay doi.
clinical-guidelines-living-evidence: huong dan lam sang song: cap nhat khuyen nghi khi bang chung thay doi living clinical guidelines: updating recommendations as evidence changes huong dan song ket hop giam sat nghien cuu lien tuc voi quy trinh ra soat de khuyen nghi co the cap nhat nhanh ma van minh bach va dang tin. a traditional clinical guideline is published after a review of evidence, but new trials may make parts outdated before the next scheduled revision. a living guideline treats selected recommendations as continuously monitored products: a team searches for new studies, assesses whether they change the balance of benefits and harms, and updates the text when needed. it does not mean recommendations change every week or that every guideline should be permanently open. the method is most useful when evidence is emerging quickly, decisions matter, and new findings could alter practice. clear dates and version histories help clinicians know which advice is current. huong dan lam sang truyen thong duoc xuat ban sau khi tong hop bang chung, nhung thu nghiem moi co the khien mot phan loi thoi truoc lan sua dinh ky. huong dan song xem mot so khuyen nghi la san pham duoc giam sat lien tuc: nhom tim nghien cuu moi, danh gia chung co doi can can loi ich–tac hai khong va cap nhat noi dung khi can. dieu do khong co nghia khuyen nghi doi hang tuan hay moi huong dan phai mo vo han. phuong phap huu ich nhat khi bang chung dang xuat hien nhanh, quyet dinh co y nghia va phat hien moi co the thay doi thuc hanh. ngay thang ro cung lich su phien ban giup bac si biet loi khuyen nao dang hien hanh. the process needs a defined scope. developers decide which clinical questions require living surveillance, how often searches occur, and what level of evidence triggers an update. they should register a protocol, use systematic search methods, assess certainty, and involve patients and clinicians in prioritizing outcomes. if every minor paper triggers a revision, guidance may become unstable; if searches are too infrequent, “living” becomes a label rather than a practice. the team should also document when no update is warranted. an unchanged recommendation can be reassuring when it follows a genuine review rather than neglect. quy trinh can pham vi xac dinh. nhom phat trien quyet dinh cau hoi lam sang nao can theo doi song, tan suat tim kiem va muc bang chung nao kich hoat cap nhat. nhom nen dang ky de cuong, dung phuong phap tim kiem co he thong, danh gia do chac chan va moi benh nhan lan bac si uu tien ket qua quan trong. neu moi bai nho deu kich hoat sua, huong dan co the bat on; neu tim qua thua, “song” chi con la nhan chu khong phai thuc hanh. nhom cung can ghi ro khi nao khong can cap nhat. khuyen nghi giu nguyen van co the tao yen tam neu sau ra soat that su, khong phai do bo mac. who’s covid-19 clinical management living guideline illustrates the approach. the june 2025 version presented current recommendations for clinical management and was designed to be updated as evidence evolved. covid research has included changing variants, treatments, and care practices, so a dated recommendation matters. clinicians should consult the specific version relevant to their jurisdiction and patient group rather than reuse an old saved copy. a who living guideline is global guidance, not an automatic substitute for local regulation, medicine availability, or bedside judgment. its value is timely synthesis, while implementation still requires adaptation. huong dan song cua who ve quan ly lam sang covid-19 minh hoa phuong phap nay. phien ban thang 6 nam 2025 trinh bay khuyen nghi hien hanh ve quan ly lam sang va duoc thiet ke de cap nhat khi bang chung thay doi. nghien cuu covid bao gom bien the, thuoc va thuc hanh cham soc thay doi, nen khuyen nghi co ngay thang rat quan trong. bac si nen tra phien ban phu hop voi quyen han dia phuong va nhom benh nhan thay vi dung lai ban da luu cu. huong dan song who la chi dan toan cau, khong tu dong thay quy dinh dia phuong, kha nang cung ung thuoc hay phan doan tai giuong benh. gia tri la tong hop kip thoi, con trien khai van can dieu chinh. evidence surveillance is only one part of updating. a panel must decide whether new studies are trustworthy, applicable, and important enough to change a recommendation. randomized trials may have small samples, early stopping, or outcomes that matter less to patients. observational findings can add context but may be confounded. the group should update certainty ratings and explain whether the recommendation is strong or conditional. when evidence remains uncertain, the guideline can state that uncertainty directly, identify research gaps, and avoid false precision. maintaining credibility requires resisting pressure to overreact to a single headline result. giam sat bang chung chi la mot phan cua cap nhat. hoi dong phai quyet dinh nghien cuu moi co dang tin, ap dung duoc va du quan trong de doi khuyen nghi khong. thu nghiem ngau nhien co the co mau nho, dung som hoac do ket qua it quan trong voi benh nhan. phat hien quan sat co the bo sung boi canh nhung de bi nhieu. nhom nen cap nhat muc do chac chan va giai thich khuyen nghi manh hay co dieu kien. khi bang chung con bat dinh, huong dan co the noi ro, neu khoang trong nghien cuu va tranh do chinh xac gia. giu uy tin doi hoi khong phan ung qua muc voi mot tieu de don le. version control is crucial for real-world use. the document should show publication date, search cut-off, updated recommendations, and a concise change summary. electronic health records and decision-support systems may embed a recommendation, so they need a method to receive revisions and prevent stale prompts. clinicians should be able to see why a change occurred and whether local guidance differs. audit teams can track adherence after updates, but should account for implementation delays and supply limits. without an operational update route, a theoretically current guideline can remain inaccessible to the people making decisions. quan ly phien ban rat quan trong trong thuc hanh. tai lieu nen ghi ngay xuat ban, ngay chot tim kiem, khuyen nghi duoc sua va tom tat thay doi. kiem toan co the theo doi tuan thu sau cap nhat nhung phai tinh do tre trien khai va gioi han nguon cung. thieu duong cap nhat van hanh, huong dan ve ly thuyet moi van co the khong toi duoc nguoi ra topics by expected impact and rate of evidence change, then records why updates were made or deferred. the aim is trustworthy guidance that responds to important new knowledge without confusing users. kien thuc moi quan trong ma khong lam nguoi dung boi roi. huong dan song nen lam lo ca dong thoi gian bang chung lan logic quyet dinh.
health-technology-assessment-decisions: danh gia cong nghe y te: noi bang chung, chi phi va kha nang tiep can health technology assessment: connecting evidence, cost, and access hta danh gia cong nghe y te theo loi ich, rui ro, chi phi, to chuc va cong bang de ho tro quyet dinh mua sam, chi tra va trien khai. health technology assessment, or hta, is a structured evaluation of a medicine, diagnostic, device, procedure, or service before or during adoption. it asks more than whether a technology can work: does it improve outcomes compared with current care, what harms may follow, how much does it cost, and who can access it? assessment may include clinical effectiveness, safety, economics, ethics, legal questions, and organizational effects. hta supports decisions such as reimbursement, procurement, or service planning. it does not mechanically decide what a society should value; decision makers must combine evidence with public priorities and transparent reasoning. danh gia cong nghe y te, hay hta, la danh gia co cau truc mot loai thuoc, xet nghiem, thiet bi, thu thuat hoac dich vu truoc hay trong qua trinh ap dung. hta hoi nhieu hon viec cong nghe co hoat dong khong: no cai thien ket qua so voi cham soc hien tai khong, co the gay hai gi, ton bao nhieu va ai tiep can duoc? danh gia co the gom hieu qua lam sang, an toan, kinh te, dao duc, phap ly va tac dong to chuc. hta ho tro quyet dinh chi tra, mua sam hay lap ke hoach dich vu. no khong tu dong quyet dinh xa hoi nen coi trong dieu gi; nguoi ra quyet dinh can ket hop bang chung voi uu tien cong chung va ly giai minh bach. the comparator is essential. a new imaging device should be compared with the current diagnostic pathway, not merely with no testing. a medicine may offer a small health gain at a high price, while a low-cost test may prevent expensive complications. economic analysis often estimates incremental cost-effectiveness, but results depend on perspective, time horizon, treatment effects, prices, and discounting. the 2025 second edition of who’s medical-device hta guidance describes assessment as support for adoption and reimbursement decisions, particularly where systems need to build capacity. it emphasizes a process tailored to device characteristics rather than copying drug-assessment templates. phuong an so sanh rat quan trong. thiet bi hinh anh moi nen duoc so voi quy trinh chan doan hien hanh, khong chi voi viec khong xet nghiem. thuoc co the dem lai muc tang suc khoe nho nhung gia cao, trong khi xet nghiem gia thap co the ngan bien chung ton kem. phan tich kinh te thuong uoc tinh hieu qua chi phi gia tang, nhung ket qua phu thuoc goc nhin, thoi gian, tac dung dieu tri, gia va chiet khau. an ban thu hai huong dan hta thiet bi y te cua who nam 2025 mo ta danh gia la ho tro quyet dinh ap dung va chi tra, nhat la noi can xay nang luc. tai lieu nhan manh quy trinh phu hop dac tinh thiet bi thay vi sao chep mau danh gia thuoc. devices pose particular challenges because they change quickly, depend on operators, and can work differently across sites. a diagnostic device may improve accuracy but have little benefit if clinicians cannot act on results. a surgical robot may require new training, maintenance, and operating-room time. hta should therefore examine learning curves, infrastructure, consumables, compatibility, and how the technology affects existing services. evidence from a specialist centre may not transfer to a smaller hospital. assessors may use rapid hta for urgent decisions, but they should state what was omitted and whether a later full assessment is needed. thiet bi dat ra thach thuc rieng vi thay doi nhanh, phu thuoc nguoi van hanh va hoat dong khac giua co so. thiet bi chan doan co the tang do chinh xac nhung it loi ich neu bac si khong hanh dong theo ket qua. robot phau thuat co the can dao tao, bao tri va thoi gian phong mo moi. vi vay, hta nen xem xet duong cong hoc tap, ha tang, vat tu tieu hao, tinh tuong thich va cong nghe anh huong dich vu hien co ra sao. bang chung tu trung tam chuyen khoa co the khong chuyen duoc sang benh vien nho. nguoi danh gia co the dung hta nhanh cho quyet dinh gap, nhung can neu dieu bi luoc va co can danh gia day du sau khong. equity is not an optional paragraph at the end. assessors should ask whether a technology reaches rural areas, people with disabilities, groups underrepresented in trials, or patients who cannot pay for associated travel and follow-up. average effectiveness can hide unequal benefit. a device may lower costs for a hospital but increase out-of-pocket expense for families. budget impact analysis helps estimate whether a payer can afford the technology at scale, while distributional analysis examines who gains and who bears burdens. these questions support decisions that are efficient without treating access as an afterthought. cong bang khong phai doan bo sung tuy chon o cuoi. nguoi danh gia nen hoi cong nghe co co the giam chi phi benh vien nhung tang tien tui cua gia dinh. phan tich tac dong ngan sach giup uoc tinh ben chi tra co du kha nang ap dung quy mo lon khong, con phan tich phan phoi xem ai duoc loi va ai ganh chi phi. nhung cau hoi nay ho tro quyet dinh hieu qua ma khong xem tiep can la van de phu. hta is also a governance process. it needs a mandate, transparent methods, independent appraisal, conflict-of-interest rules, patient input, and a route to appeal or update decisions. who’s 2025 guidance on medical devices links assessment to national policies, essential-device lists, and health-system capacity. countries can adapt international evidence rather than duplicate every study, but local prices, disease burden, workforce, and infrastructure still matter. publicly explaining why a technology was adopted, restricted, or deferred can build trust. a technically rigorous assessment that is hidden from the people affected may still lack legitimacy. hta cung la quy trinh quan tri. no can tham quyen, phuong phap minh bach, tham dinh doc lap, quy tac xung dot loi ich, y kien benh nhan va duong khieu nai hoac cap nhat quyet dinh. huong dan who nam 2025 ve thiet bi y te ket noi danh gia voi chinh sach quoc gia, danh muc thiet bi thiet yeu va nang luc he thong. quoc gia co the dieu chinh bang chung quoc te thay vi lap moi nghien cuu, nhung gia dia phuong, ganh nang benh, nhan luc va ha tang van quan trong. giai thich cong khai vi sao cong nghe duoc chap nhan, han che hoac tri hoan co the xay long tin. danh gia ky thuat tot nhung giau khoi nguoi bi anh huong van co the thieu tinh chinh danh. a recommendation is not the end of evaluation. after adoption, health systems should monitor real-world effectiveness, adverse events, use rates, and budget impact; devices may need recalibration, software updates, or replacement. if a technology underperforms, the original decision can be revised. who’s 2025 second edition gives a current framework for medical-device assessment, while country-specific appraisal remains necessary. the core question is not “is the technology innovative?” but “does it improve health fairly and affordably compared with what we already who nam 2025 dua ra khung cap nhat de danh gia thiet bi, con tham dinh theo quoc gia van can thiet. cau hoi cot loi khong phai “cong nghe co moi khong?” ma la “no co cai thien suc khoe cong bang va du kha nang chi tra so voi viec dang lam khong?” hta lam ro su danh doi va cho nguoi quyet dinh co so co ly le de hanh dong.
